findings.anchor: SRS l.15-19 (dup l.84-88); TORQ SRS l.25, l.86-98
findings.claim: The 'Tripartite Topology' misidentifies every real component: TORQ is cast as a message broker, a non-existent 'Genesis' ab initio core stands in for TOPOS/TORQ/ORCA/CFOUR, and BASE (the real orchestrator and UI host) is absent from the SRS entirely.
findings.evidence: l.18: "**TORQ** (Task Orchestration & Routing Queue) | Centralized state machine, message broker, and data sanitization layer." vs TORQ SRS l.25: "TOPOS owns global conformer discovery. SpycFit owns spectral assignment and fitting. BASE owns shared identity, installation policy, resource brokering, durable task services, and general UI hosting." SRS grep: 'TOPOS' 0 hits; 'BASE' appears only as a level-of-theory label (l.1687).
findings.why_it_matters: A fix/replace agent reading Ch1 would build SpycFit as a passive sink behind a queue that does not exist, would never implement BASE's module discovery/handoff, and would never consume TORQ's actual HDF5 bundle. TORQ's own §3 flowchart already names the real edge: 'Artifact store and immutable manifests --> SPCAT inputs / SpycFit bundle / report'.
findings.recommendation: Replace §1.1 with a factual component map: BASE (Voila UI in Codespaces/local, Stage-0 engine registry, cochem.modules discovery, cochem.module-handoff/1 manifests, artifact/scratch roots, durable task service); TOPOS (conformer discovery, feeds TORQ); TORQ (ORCA/CFOUR/PySCF adapters; derives B_e/B_0/alpha/quartic+sextic/signed dipoles/chi/LAM priors; exports TORQ-EXP-004 HDF5 bundle and TORQ-EXP-002 Pickett templates); SpycFit (consumes bundle + experimental spectrum or peak list; assignment + effective-Hamiltonian fitting; exports .par/.int/.lin/.cat/.fit/.var, PGOPHER, report inputs). Cite TORQ-EXP-002/004 and V-CONSUMER by ID.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.18/l.87 quote is exact and TORQ Implementation SRS l.25 says verbatim 'TOPOS owns global conformer discovery. SpycFit owns spectral assignment and fitting. BASE owns ... durable task services, and general UI hosting'; TORQ's own expansions are 'Precision Quantum Scaling + Observables Extraction' (Integration_Architecture l.37) and '(Optimization Engine)' (User Manual l.510), never 'Task Orchestration & Routing Queue'. 'TOPOS' has 0 hits in the SRS, 'BASE' appears only as 'Base Level' (l.1687/1767), and 'Genesis' exists nowhere as a component (only 'Genesis block Merkle hash seed', telemetry_queue.py l.32). The recommendation's real names are verified: BASE .docs/Module_Provider_Contract.md l.9-23/59 (cochem.modules entry point, cochem.module-handoff/1, Stage 0 registry) and module_registry.py l.46 ('spycfit': 'Spectroscopy fitting and export'); note BASE scripts/module-distribution.json registers spycfit with adapter None and operations [], so the handoff still has to be designed.

findings.claim: The air-gap / unidirectional data-diode requirement is not a sensible requirement for a Voila dashboard students run in GitHub Codespaces, and the SRS itself violates it in at least seven places.
findings.evidence: l.47: "It resides in a secure subnet where outbound requests are dropped at the hardware firewall level." vs l.1455 "The Voila kernel maintains the persistent state"; l.1700 "SpycFit transitions the current task state in the SQLite `job_board`"; l.405 "dynamically injected from the latest AME ... database at runtime"; l.207 "written to a distributed LevelDB cache"; l.1524 "import an existing CoChem `.cat` or `.par` file". BASE README l.18-19: "choose **Code -> Codespaces -> Create codespace**. Open the private **8866 CoChem Voila dashboard**".
findings.why_it_matters: The real deployment is a browser-served notebook in a cloud container; 'air-gapped, zero external ingress' is untestable there and forbids the bidirectional HITL loop, user file import, and RRF feedback the SRS itself requires. An agent would build signing/firewall machinery and still have to violate it to make the UI work.
findings.recommendation: Delete §1.3-1.4. Replace with SPYC-DEP-001: 'SpycFit requires no network access at fit time; all inputs are local files (TORQ bundle, experimental spectrum/peak list, Pickett files, handoff.json); all outputs are written under the BASE artifact root; plotly.js and widget assets are bundled offline.' Adopt TORQ-SEC-001-style requirements (path validation, bounded payloads, no untrusted pickle) instead of 'air-gap'.
findings.verifier_note: All quotes are exact (SRS l.47, 207, 405, 1455, 1521, 1524, 1700; BASE README l.18-19 'Code → Codespaces → Create codespace. Open the private 8866 CoChem Voilà dashboard', l.72 'Host the interface in Codespaces'). Two revisions: the ecosystem's 'air-gap' is a workspace PATH-tier rule, not network isolation — BASE cochem_core_registry_schema.py l.610 'HPC Tripartite Air-Gap Check: Prevent write stores from targeting immutable $COCHEM_ROOT', orchestrator AirGapViolationError (l.324), BASE cochem_spycfit_ml_schema.py docstring 'Tripartite Workspace Air-Gap Architecture (Tier 1 Repo, Tier 2 Artifacts, Tier 3 Scratch)', SpycFit pyproject.toml l.8 — so the replacement SPYC-DEP-001 should RETAIN that path-tier write-protection (never write under the repo root; artifact/scratch roots supplied by BASE) rather than discard the concept; and of the seven cited violations only l.405 (runtime AME fetch), l.1524 (non-TORQ user import) and l.1700 (reverse write into TORQ's queue) breach the network/diode clause, while l.175/1455/1521 are statelessness breaches belonging to ARCH-04. BLOCKER stands because an agent implementing §1.3-1.4 literally would build a push-only sink with no user import or HITL loop.

findings.anchor: SRS l.58-59, l.358-361 (dup l.436-439), l.596-599; TORQ SRS l.324-344, l.471; TORQ full_srs_requirement_audit.json l.323; OLD_PLAN workflow l.7
findings.claim: The TORQ->SpycFit data contract is the product's most important interface and is entirely unspecified: the SRS names three different schemas that do not exist and TORQ is blocked waiting for SpycFit to supply the consumer contract.
findings.evidence: l.59: "The payload must conform to the strict CoChem V4 Data Schema." l.361: "validated against the master `cochem_spyc_schema.json`." Old plan l.7: "hooks into the massive `cochem_state.h5` shared tensor." None exist (grep 0 in all repos). TORQ audit: "Actual versioned SpycFit consumer and convention/schema round trips have not been supplied or qualified." V-CONSUMER l.471: "until supplied, mark interoperability unverified."
findings.why_it_matters: Without this contract neither repo can be finished; every prior, unit, frame, sign and status that enters the fit is undefined.
findings.recommendation: Add a chapter 'TORQ bundle consumer contract' (SPYC-IF-0xx) that fixes, per TORQ-EXP-004: dataset paths (/meta schema_version+producer; /molecules/<id> atom IDs, Z, isotope masses with source/version, geometry, units; /observables/<id> for A_e,B_e,C_e, A_0,B_0,C_0 with delta-B_vib label, Watson quartic+sextic set, signed mu_a,mu_b,mu_c, chi tensor per nucleus, V3/F/rho and internal-top direction cosines or predicted A/E splittings; /uncertainties/<id> model + covariance; /surfaces/<id> for DVR/PES priors; /provenance). Units (MHz, debye, cm^-1, amu, angstrom per TORQ-SCI-002). Frame: principal axis system, right-handed, orientation+origin+atom order attributes; representation tag I^r or III^l. Reduction tag A or S with parameter names and sign convention per TORQ-EXP-002 ('Names alone are insufficient to convert conventions'). Dipole: signed components in PAS, frame/gauge recorded (Method Matrix l.3181, l.3426). Status propagation: validated/exploratory/partial (TORQ-EXP-001) and the five absent states not_requested/unsupported/not_applicable/failed/not_computed (TORQ-DATA-002) must never be coerced to 0. Observable identity: B_e vs B_0 labels (TORQ-SCI-004). Provenance [M]/[D]/[E] + origin labels (TORQ-DATA-003). Integrity: BundleManifest SHA-256 per file. Pickett roles per TORQ-EXP-002. Consumer contract test must assert, against a committed reference bundle from a pinned TORQ: schema_version compatibility; existence/dtype/shape/endianness/units of every required dataset; A>=B>=C and kappa recomputed from stored I; reduction and representation tags present; dipole signs round-trip; absent states preserved; digests verified; constants written to .par/.int reproduce the TORQ-side SPCAT .cat within manifest tolerance (V-SPCAT).
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.59, l.361 and old-plan workflow l.7 quotes are exact; TORQ docs/development/full_srs_requirement_audit.json l.323 has V-CONSUMER status 'blocked' with the quoted reason and TORQ SRS l.471 says 'until supplied, mark interoperability unverified'; every cited TORQ ID checks out (SCI-002 l.54, SCI-004 l.68, DATA-002 l.142 five absent states, DATA-003 l.144, BundleManifest SHA-256 l.140, EXP-001/002 l.322/324) as do Method Matrix l.3181 and l.3426. Evidence correction: 'cochem_state.h5' is NOT absent — it is BASE's registry state-file path (CoChem-BASE/src/cochem_base/orchestrator/cochem_system_config.py l.1620 state_file_path=.../Registry/cochem_state.h5; TORQ orchestrator/cochem_system_config.py l.1717), though no file exists and it is not a TORQ→SpycFit tensor bundle; and a fourth candidate schema lives in BASE (src/cochem_base/cochem_spycfit_ml_schema.py), which the new contract chapter must explicitly subsume or retire. Claim and BLOCKER severity stand.

findings.anchor: SRS Ch9 l.1447-1615 (no assignment algorithm); Start_SpycFit.ipynb cell 2; OLD_PLAN workflow l.21-25; Method Matrix decision card l.70 and l.3632
findings.claim: The SRS has no assignment subsystem: candidate generation, search window from prior accuracy, dipole/dark-branch pruning, bootstrap (triples) fitting, next-best-transition ranking and the HITL approve/reject state machine are unspecified, while the code and notebook implement unspecified Hungarian/Huber algorithms.
findings.evidence: SRS grep: 'Hungarian' 0, 'Huber' 0, 'AUTOFIT|triples' 0. Notebook cell 2: "**Hungarian Matching Engine**: Minimum-cost bipartite matching with frequency gating." OLD_PLAN workflow l.23: 'SpycFit actively calculates the "Next Best Microwave Transitions."' Method Matrix l.3632: "The effort belongs in pruning: narrowing the window from +/-120 MHz to +/-12 MHz removes about three orders of magnitude of candidate triples".
findings.why_it_matters: This is the product. Without requirements for it the agent either keeps unverified heuristics or deletes them; both are failures.
findings.recommendation: Add chapter 'Assignment engine' (SPYC-ASSIGN-0xx): prediction catalog (SPCAT or equivalence-tested in-process); search window from declared prior accuracy class (Product A/B/C per Method Matrix Step 1); dipole-type and dark-branch pruning; candidate scoring with declared cost; bootstrap fit over transition triples with a combinatorial budget; next-best-transition ranking by information gain; HITL state machine PROPOSED/APPROVED/REJECTED/GHOST/MANUAL; loop closure (regenerate .lin from APPROVED only, refit with SPFIT, re-predict).
findings.verifier_note: Evidence verified: SRS grep counts are Hungarian 0, Huber 0, AUTOFIT|triples 0; Ch9 l.1447-1615 headers cover only the O-C viewer, sliders and ghost-peak masking; notebook cell 2 and OLD_PLAN l.23 quotes are verbatim; Method Matrix l.3632-3636 additionally states JAX is 'not used to replace SPFIT' and that effort belongs in pruning. Raised to BLOCKER because the SRS itself declares SpycFit 'the terminal spectral assignment module' (l.19, 21, 23, 92) yet specifies zero assignment behaviour, so an agent implementing it literally builds a fitter-plus-viewer and must either delete or keep unspecified matching code, which meets the brief's 'build the wrong thing' criterion.

findings.claim: Because every chapter exists twice with architecturally different content and no marker of which is normative, the SRS cannot function as a contract.
findings.evidence: l.1328: "**Carry State:** The accumulating cross-section tensor, initialized to zero." vs l.1426: "**Carry State:** A dummy state (`None`), as each wavenumber chunk calculation is functionally independent of the others." l.207 "AOT Serialization" vs l.292 "Dual-Target AOT Serialization". l.375 ".var" vs l.453 ".par".
findings.why_it_matters: An agent asked to 'implement the SRS' has to guess which of two designs to build in at least four places.
findings.recommendation: One version per chapter; delete all conversational text; add a document-control header (version, date, author, status, change log) and state that TORQ-style requirement IDs (SPY-<area>-<n>) with SHALL/SHOULD/MAY are the only normative statements.
findings.verifier_note: Every cited pair is verbatim and substantively divergent: l.1328 'accumulating cross-section tensor, initialized to zero' vs l.1426 'A dummy state (None)'; l.207 'AOT Serialization' vs l.292 'Dual-Target AOT Serialization' (adds a CPU fallback graph); l.375 '.var' vs l.453 '.par'; l.384 vs l.462 are different regexes. All chatter lines check out and lines 1-12 show no version, date, status or change log. The claim 'cannot function as a contract' is the brief's BLOCKER definition verbatim ('makes the SRS unusable as a contract'), so MAJOR was deflated; note the chapter-duplication and chatter facts overlap the brief's established list, but the architecturally different content between versions is new evidence.

findings.anchor: SRS whole document (Ch1 l.5-141 is the only architecture text); TORQ SRS §3 l.84-114 as the model
findings.claim: The SRS contains no architecture that matches the real ecosystem; SRS v2 must carry the following architecture section so the fix/replace agent builds the right thing.
findings.evidence: Ch1 defines Genesis/TORQ-broker/SpycFit tiers (l.15-19); no section names modules, state location, hosting, process boundaries or deployment targets; TORQ SRS §3 shows the expected form: a flowchart plus a component table with 'Input | Output | Required error behavior' (l.104-112).
findings.why_it_matters: Every other finding in this lens is a symptom of this absence.
findings.recommendation: ARCHITECTURE FOR SRS v2. (1) Context: BASE hosts (Voila UI, discovery via cochem.modules, handoff manifests, artifact/scratch roots, task service); TOPOS -> TORQ (QC engine) -> TORQ bundle (TORQ-EXP-004) + Pickett templates (TORQ-EXP-002) -> SpycFit; experimental spectrum/peak list from the user; outputs to the BASE artifact root and to BASE's report (scribe) tooling. (2) Package: single src/cochem_spycfit, pure Python, CPU-first, cochem-base pinned dependency. Modules: contract/ (bundle.py: h5py reader, schema_version negotiation, required paths/units/frame/reduction/status/absent-state handling, digest check; handoff.py: cochem.module-handoff/1 receiver; pickett.py: pyckett-compatible .par/.var/.int/.lin/.cat/.egy with roles; experimental.py: spectrum, peak list, .lin ingest + peak picking; config.py: pydantic SpycFitConfig) - the TORQ consumer contract test lives here; model/ (effective Hamiltonian forward model: Watson A/S quartic+sextic in I^r/III^l, nuclear quadrupole for 1-2 nuclei, effective internal-rotation terms, intensities from signed mu, T_rot, user-supplied spin weights and partition function; diagnostics kappa, inertial defect, planar moments, Kraitchman r_s; numpy/scipy, JAX optional for Jacobians; spectrum-equivalence test vs SPCAT); fit/ (in-process weighted LM with analytic/AD Jacobian for what-if, sensitivity, correlation and physical-bound penalties; spfit_runner.py subprocess driver for pinned SPFIT/SPCAT as fit-of-record with scratch context, timeouts, parsers; LOIO cross-validation); assign/ (catalog prediction, search window from Product A/B/C prior class, dipole-type/dark-branch pruning, candidate scoring, triples bootstrap with budget, next-best-transition ranking, HITL state machine, .lin generation from APPROVED only); session/ (FitSession versioned artifact, event log, digests, resume); ui/ (ipywidgets + Plotly FigureWidget: dual-pane O-C, sliders with first-order update then exact refit, ghost peaks, assignment table, next-best list; served by Voila; identical headless service API); export/ (Pickett bundle + SHA-256 manifest, optional PGOPHER .pgo with user spin weights, advisory RRF JSON, report inputs with [M]/[D]/[E] labels, BASE handoff manifest back); provenance/ (shared constants service from BASE, units, labels). (3) State: exactly one FitSession file per project under the BASE artifact root (single writer); kernel memory is a cache; SPFIT scratch under the scratch root; source tree read-only; no shared databases, no daemons. (4) Process boundaries: in-process = bundle read, forward model, LM/what-if, assignment, UI, export; subprocess = pinned SPFIT/SPCAT (and PGOPHER if the user has it), located via BASE registry/config; never launched by SpycFit = TORQ, ORCA, CFOUR, PySCF. (5) BASE hosting: cochem.modules entry point with capability metadata; receive_handoff(handoff.json); Voila tab or standalone notebook; artifact/scratch roots from BASE config; CPU-only resource profile declared. (6) Deployment targets: Codespaces (default), local Linux/WSL2/macOS, HPC login node; GitHub Actions = CI only; per-target acceptance (clean wheel, consumer contract test, SPCAT round-trip, UI journey on a reference complex). (7) Requirement families with acceptance IDs: SPYC-IF (TORQ bundle), SPYC-BASE, SPYC-EXP, SPYC-MODEL, SPYC-FIT, SPYC-ASSIGN, SPYC-SESSION, SPYC-UI, SPYC-EXPORT, SPYC-DEP, SPYC-CI, each with a V-* style test the CI runs.
findings.verifier_note: Verified that Ch1 §1.1-1.5 (l.5-141, duplicated) is the SRS's only architecture text and that a grep of the whole document finds no package/module layout, entry point, process boundary, Codespaces/WSL/HPC or deployment section; TORQ SRS §3 l.84-114 (flowchart l.86-98, component table with 'Required error behavior' l.104-112) is an accurate model. The recommendation's load-bearing ecosystem facts all check out in the real BASE: `cochem.modules` entry-point group (interfaces/module_registry.py l.18), `cochem.module-handoff/1` with handoff.json and the receiver `load_module_handoff(manifest_path)` (interfaces/artifact_handoff.py l.30, l.167 - the recommendation's `receive_handoff` should name this function), a registered `spycfit` capability 'Spectroscopy fitting and export' (l.46), artifact/scratch roots via get_artifact_dir and COCH_SCRATCH (topos_runner.py l.205-208), an existing formatters/cochem_dark_branch_filter.py, Voila on 8866; pyckett is a real maintained SPFIT/SPCAT wrapper on PyPI (https://pypi.org/project/pyckett) and Product A/B/C, AUTOFIT triples, XIAM/BELGI/RAM36 and user-entered spin weights are all Method Matrix terms (l.42, l.144, l.225, l.731, l.762). An SRS whose only architecture models TORQ as a message broker and SpycFit as an air-gapped daemon would make the fix/replace agent build the wrong thing, so BLOCKER is correct.

findings.claim: The prescription to use bare nuclear masses (M_atom - Z m_e + B_e/c^2) for the inertia tensor is contrary to standard practice and would shift predicted rotational constants by ~Z m_e/M (~2.7e-4 relative for C/N/O, i.e. ~2.7 MHz on a 10 GHz constant), while the same paragraph demands 1e-8 u mass precision (~10 Hz equivalent).
findings.evidence: l.406-407: "the true nuclear mass ($M_{nucl}$) is utilized to account for the actual rotation of the nuclear framework, stripping away the total electron rest mass ($Z m_e$) and applying the relativistic binding energy ($B_e$) correction: $$ M_{nucl} = M_{atom} - Z m_e + \frac{B_e}{c^2} $$"
findings.why_it_matters: Rotational constants from ab initio geometries are computed with atomic masses because electrons co-rotate with the nuclei; the residual electron-distribution effect is of order (m_e/m_p)*g (~1e-4) and is applied, when at all, via the rotational g-tensor (Gordy & Cook, Microwave Molecular Spectra, 3rd ed., ch. XIII; Puzzarini, Stanton & Gauss, Int. Rev. Phys. Chem. 29, 273 (2010); Demaison, Boggs & Csaszar (eds.), Equilibrium Molecular Structures, CRC 2011). Using nuclear masses biases every prior by ~3 MHz, far outside the Method Matrix §3 accuracy table and the 0.02% isotopologue-shift target. The B_e symbol also collides with the rotational constant B_e two lines later (l.408-409). On precision: AME2020 uncertainties for H, C, N, O are <=1e-9 u, so 1e-8 u is available, but the physically required tolerance is only ~1e-6 u (delta B/B = delta m/m ~ 1e-7 for kHz on 10 GHz); the stated 1e-8 u is unmotivated.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite: 'The inertia tensor SHALL use atomic (not nuclear) isotopic masses from the pinned AME2020 table with uncertainty <= 1e-6 u. Electron-mass corrections SHALL NOT be applied to priors unless the molecular g-tensor is supplied, in which case Watson's correction I_g -> I_g (1 + (m_e/m_p) g_gg) is applied and cited (Gordy & Cook ch. XIII).' Delete the M_nucl formula and the B_e/c^2 term; rename any remaining binding-energy symbol to avoid B_e.
findings.verifier_note: l.406-407 and l.484-485 read exactly as quoted and the symbol collision is real (l.409 and l.487 define the rotational constant B_e two lines after the binding-energy B_e). Literature confirms the standard convention is atomic masses with the electronic term supplied by the rotational g-tensor (Gauss & Puzzarini, Mol. Phys. 108, 269 (2010); Puzzarini & Stanton, PCCP 2023 semi-experimental workflow), and Method_Matrix.md contains no nuclear-mass or electron-mass prescription at all while its semi-experimental row (l.307, 0.03-0.06 %) is the same magnitude as the ~2.7e-4 bias. Caveat on the evidence: the '0.02 % isotopologue-shift' breach is overstated since Z*m_e cancels in shifts, but BLOCKER holds because the SRS text is a SHALL-style formula whose undefined B_e (electron binding ~1e-6 u vs nuclear binding ~0.1 u for C) differs by five orders of magnitude between readings and either reading yields a physically wrong inertia tensor.

findings.anchor: SRS l.361/439, 375/453, 1142/1214, 1222; OLD_PLAN_architectural_changes l.24; OLD_PLAN_workflow l.17, l.33; Method_Matrix.md l.3395, 3508-3512
findings.claim: The SRS never decides how ab initio values enter the fit (initial guess only, fixed, or regularised prior), uses 'Bayesian' vocabulary with no prior term in any χ² (l.39/108, 1090/1165), silently freezes parameters 'at its ab initio value', and nowhere states the Method Matrix's BINDING §20.3 prior-disclosure rule; no surviving finding cites §20.3.
findings.evidence: SRS l.361: 'user-defined Bayesian priors'; l.453: '.par ... Bayesian uncertainties'; l.1214: 'pruned (frozen at its ab initio or ground-state value)'. OLD_PLAN l.24: 'Levenberg-Marquardt Bayesian optimizer ... constants (passed from TORQ) will serve as the rigid priors'. Method Matrix l.3511: '(2) Any parameter whose reported value is influenced by a prior is flagged ... (3) Constants entering catalogues ... come from an unregularised least-squares fit.'
findings.why_it_matters: For 5-10 atom complexes with few assigned lines, distortion constants are routinely fixed to or constrained by theory (Method Matrix system 3: A fixed at 42 GHz, Δ_K/δ_J/δ_K set to zero). Whether SpycFit does this, how it is flagged, and whether frozen values can enter the published table is the difference between a usable experimental constant and a theory-contaminated one that the Method Matrix excludes from validation. An agent building from the SRS would ship Sobol-frozen ab initio values unflagged in the output table.
findings.recommendation: Add a requirement block 'Priors and fixed parameters': (i) every parameter carries a state ∈ {fitted, fixed@value+provenance, constrained(prior μ,σ)}; (ii) the default fit is unregularised weighted LS; constrained/regularised fits are opt-in and their outputs are labelled; (iii) the final/published table flags prior-influenced parameters exactly as SPFIT marks fixed ones; (iv) priors MAY drive search windows, seeding and degeneracy-breaking (§20.3 part 1) with σ taken from the Method Matrix §3.1 accuracy classes; (v) strike 'Bayesian' from .lin/.par descriptions. Replace the automatic Sobol freeze (NUM-02/PHYS-16) with user-controlled fix/float plus a determinability report.
findings.verifier_note: Every quote verified at SRS l.361/439 ('user-defined Bayesian priors'), l.375/453 ('Bayesian variances/uncertainties'), l.1142/1214 ('frozen at its ab initio or ground-state value'); both chi-square forms (l.39/108, l.1090/1165) contain no prior term, grep finds no flag/disclosure language or any reference to Method Matrix §20.3, and Ch10 l.1644/1724 even asks for 'fixed higher-order theoretical constraints' with no flagging rule. Method_Matrix.md l.3508-3512 (four-part rule) and l.3388 (system 3, 'A not determined, fixed at 42 GHz ... the test case for the prior-disclosure rule of Section 20.3') verified verbatim. BLOCKER is justified under the brief: l.1214 mandates automatic, unflagged freezing to theory, which yields theory-contaminated constant tables that MM l.3395 excludes from validation.

findings.claim: Nuclear electric quadrupole hyperfine coupling (14N, 35/37Cl, 79/81Br, 127I, D) is absent from the SRS: no Hamiltonian term, no coupled |J,I,F> basis, no F quantum number in the .lin parser or quantum-number gate, no χ parameters or Pickett parameter codes, and no validation case.
findings.evidence: l.1082: "extraction of molecular constants (e.g., rotational constants, centrifugal distortion parameters, nuclear quadrupole coupling constants)" — but the only Hamiltonians given are l.31-35 and l.551/563 (rotation + Watson CD), and the QN gate at l.387/465 is "K_a + K_c > J + 1" with no F. grep: 'hyperfine' = 0 hits.
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix §6.2 (l.670-674): for any 14N/Cl/Br/I "hyperfine structure is the strongest topology discriminator available"; §6.3 (l.678): "every deuteration introduces a new hyperfine pattern that must be predicted or the spectrum will not fit". Three of the six §17 working-set systems (Ar–oxazole, H2CO–HCl, C6H6–HCN) are hyperfine-resolved. A 14N-containing complex at 1–2 K in 2–22 GHz shows hyperfine triplets on every low-J line; without H_Q the engine cannot even reproduce the line count. The code tree has zero files mentioning quadrupole or hyperfine, so the gap is in both SRS and code.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-HAM-QUAD-001: "The effective Hamiltonian SHALL include the nuclear electric quadrupole interaction for up to N_Q nuclei with I ≥ 1 (14N I=1, D I=1, 35/37Cl I=3/2, 79/81Br I=3/2, 127I I=5/2), evaluated in the sequentially coupled basis F1 = J + I1, F = F1 + I2 (PGOPHER/SPCAT convention). Fitted parameters SHALL be χ_aa and (χ_bb − χ_cc) with the traceless constraint χ_aa+χ_bb+χ_cc=0 (reporting all three), plus optional off-diagonal χ_ab, χ_ac, χ_bc. The .lin/.cat parsers SHALL accept the Pickett asymmetric-top QN orderings N,Ka,Kc,v,J,F and N,Ka,Kc,J,F1,F (QNFMT Q mod 5 = 3, +20 for two coupled spins), and the .par/.var writer SHALL emit Pickett codes with the documented factors (110010000 = 1.5χ_aa, 110040000 = 0.25(χ_bb−χ_cc), 110610000 = χ_ab) and the spin-rounding convention (1/2→1, 3/2→2). Acceptance V-HFS: refit the 103 published Ar–oxazole components and reproduce χ_aa = 2.3032(6), χ_bb = −4.0526(8), χ_cc = 1.7494(4) MHz within 1σ with σ_fit ≤ 0.8 kHz; refit H2CO–H35Cl to eQq_aa = −41.424(14) MHz with A held fixed at 42 GHz; reproduce D2O χ_aa(D) = 152.55(88) kHz."
findings.verifier_note: Claim fully confirmed: SRS l.31-35/551/563 give rotation+Watson CD only, the QN gate at l.387/465 is 'K_a + K_c > J + 1' with no F, 'hyperfine' has 0 hits, NQCC appears only as an aspiration (l.1082) and in the filler Improver line l.165 ('Nuclear Quadrupole Coupling ... integrated' with no spec), and the only repo file mentioning quadrupole/hyperfine is swarm_state.json telemetry (no code). Recommendation needs two precision fixes: per the SPINV documentation (cdms.astro.uni-koeln.de/classic/predictions/pickett/spinv.html) QNFMT '+20' applies only when 'two spins are coupled to Itot', not to the sequential J,F1,F ordering the same sentence mandates (that uses base Q with NQN=6), and the codes 110010000 = 1.5χ_aa / 110040000 = 0.25(χ_bb−χ_cc) hold in the I^r (prolate) representation only (Method Matrix l.3445: 110030000 = 1.5χ_cc for oblate). Spin values, F1=J+I1 coupling (MM l.760) and the Ar–oxazole/H2CO–HCl/D2O acceptance numbers (MM l.672, 678, 3387-3388) are correct.

findings.claim: The SRS asserts that SpycFit derives nuclear spin-statistical weights automatically from the molecular symmetry (PI) group; the governing Method Matrix §7 makes manual, user-supplied weights with a recorded feasibility argument a BINDING requirement and states no package automates it. There is no requirement for weights as user input, nor for their consistent propagation into intensities, GUP and Q(T).
findings.evidence: l.913: "SpycFit strictly enforces nuclear spin statistics based on the molecular symmetry group (PI group). For a generic C3v internal rotor with three identical spin-1/2 nuclei ... A: 4 ... E: 2". Method Matrix l.757: "Feasibility is a dynamics judgement, not a software output." l.762: "derive the spin statistical weights by hand, enter them into PGOPHER or SPCAT explicitly ... No package in this document's stack automates this."
findings.why_it_matters: Feasibility of permutation-inversion operations depends on barrier heights on the experimental timescale (water dimer MS group has 3840 ops; Ar–ketene H-atom tunnelling is quenched on deuteration). An agent implementing the SRS as written will build a point-group-to-weight lookup that is wrong for exactly the fluxional complexes in scope, producing wrong relative intensities and phantom/missing lines — the Method Matrix l.751 failure mode that "makes a crowded CP-FTMW spectrum unassignable". TORQ-EXP-003 additionally warns against double-counting symmetry/nuclear-spin weights in Q(T).
findings.recommendation: Replace §5.5.2 with SPYC-INT-SPIN-001: "Nuclear spin statistical weights SHALL be an explicit user input, one integer per symmetry species / tunnelling sublevel / K-parity class as applicable, accompanied by a mandatory free-text feasibility argument stored in the run provenance. The system SHALL NOT derive weights from a point group or PI group. The system MAY display a non-binding suggestion for the single-C3v-top case (A:E = 4:2 for three equivalent spin-1/2 nuclei; 11:16 for CD3) labelled 'suggestion — verify'. Supplied weights SHALL multiply predicted intensities, SHALL appear in the .cat GUP field, and SHALL enter Q(T) exactly once; the acceptance test V-SPIN SHALL verify a 3:1 ortho/para alternation in a C2v two-equivalent-proton test molecule (e.g. H2CO) and the absence of A↔E lines for a methyl rotor."
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.913 reads verbatim 'SpycFit strictly enforces nuclear spin statistics based on the molecular symmetry group (PI group)' with a hard-coded C3v table (A:4, E:2) and no user-input, feasibility-argument or propagation requirement anywhere. Method Matrix §7 l.757 'Feasibility is a dynamics judgement, not a software output' and l.762 'derive the spin statistical weights by hand, enter them into PGOPHER or SPCAT explicitly, and record the feasibility argument in the output. No package in this document's stack automates this' are binding; TORQ SRS l.328 (TORQ-EXP-003) confirms 'avoid double-counting symmetry/nuclear-spin weights'. The recommendation's weights (CH3 4:2, CD3 11:16, H2CO 3:1 ortho/para) are physically correct.

findings.claim: The SRS specifies an LM optimizer but no requirement for the standard fit outputs of SPFIT/XIAM/PGOPHER: 1σ parameter uncertainties (value(1σ) in last digits), the correlation matrix, weighted RMS σ_fit and unweighted RMS, N_lines/N_params, per-line o−c table, outlier flags, determinability diagnostics, or user control over fixed-vs-fitted parameters. The only 'fixing' is an automatic Sobol pruning that silently freezes parameters at computed ab initio values.
findings.evidence: l.1140-1142: "Any parameter θ_k whose total-effect Sobol index falls below ... S_Tk < 10^-6 is automatically flagged as insensitive and is aggressively pruned (frozen at its ab initio or ground-state value)". The covariance matrix is mentioned only as a divergence trigger (l.1644: "off-diagonal elements of the covariance matrix approaching unity"); 'standard deviation'/'1σ'/'parenthes' appear only at l.419/497 (input normalization).
findings.why_it_matters: A rotational-spectroscopy fit is published as a parameter table with 1σ in parentheses, σ_fit, N and the reduction/representation; without these the output is unpublishable and unreviewable. Silent substitution of computed priors violates Method Matrix §17 exclusion rule (l.3395: "Any constant whose published value was influenced by a theoretical prior ... is excluded from the validation set") and §18 (l.3424: "a .par mixing computed and measured parameters must say which is which"). Method Matrix system 3 (H2CO–HCl, A fixed at 42 GHz, Δ_K/δ_J/δ_K set to zero) is the canonical case needing explicit user fixing with disclosure — currently unsupported.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-FIT-OUT-001: "After convergence the system SHALL report: (a) each parameter with its 1σ standard error from diag[(JᵀWJ)⁻¹], both unscaled and scaled by sqrt(χ²_r), formatted as value(1σ) in the last quoted digits; (b) the full parameter correlation matrix with |ρ| > 0.9 pairs flagged; (c) N_lines, N_params, degrees of freedom, weighted RMS σ_fit = sqrt(χ²/(N−M)) (dimensionless) and unweighted RMS in kHz; (d) a per-line table of ν_obs, ν_calc, o−c, σ_i, (o−c)/σ_i with |o−c|/σ_i > 3 flagged; (e) condition number of JᵀWJ." Add SPYC-FIT-CTRL-001: "Every parameter SHALL carry a user-settable state ∈ {fitted, fixed} and, if fixed, a provenance tag ∈ {measured, computed(method string), assumed, zero}. The system SHALL NOT change a parameter's state automatically; Sobol/sensitivity analysis SHALL be advisory, printed as a recommendation list, and never applied silently. All output tables SHALL print the provenance tag of every non-fitted parameter."
findings.verifier_note: Quote at l.1140-1142 (duplicated l.1212-1214) is verbatim: insensitive parameters are 'aggressively pruned (frozen at its ab initio or ground-state value)' with no user control; no 1σ, σ_fit, N/M, per-line o−c table or fixed/fitted state exists anywhere (Ch9 sliders l.1499-1504 only change values; lasso l.1514 only reweights lines), violating MM l.3395 (exclusion rule) and l.3424 ('a .par mixing computed and measured parameters must say which is which'). Anchor correction: the correlation matrix is not mentioned 'only' at l.1644 — the Ch10 RRF schema l.1663/1743 lists 'final χ²_r, parameter correlation matrix' as diagnostic.metrics, and l.60 names '.fit / .par' egress files; both are failure-path/machine payloads with no content spec, so the gap stands but the evidence sentence and anchors should cite them.

findings.claim: There is no requirement to produce the primary bench deliverable of the domain — a predicted stick line list (.int + .cat) at jet rotational temperature (1–2 K) over 2–22 GHz with eigenvector-based asymmetric-rotor line strengths, lower-state energies, degeneracies and a direct-summation partition function. Instead Ch8 specifies a HITRAN/EXOMOL cross-section engine at T_ref = 296 K with pressure broadening and a 512 MB VRAM mandate.
findings.evidence: l.1254: "synthesis of theoretical absorbance spectra from foundational line-list databases (e.g., HITRAN, EXOMOL)"; l.1266: "reference intensity S_j(T_ref) at T_ref = 296 K"; l.1256: "wavenumber domains (>10,000 cm^-1)". grep: '.int' = 0, '.egy' = 0, 'jet' = 0, 'CDMS|JPL' = 0. l.1468 calls S_ij a "Hönl-London factor".
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix §18 l.3422: "The output of this document is not a table of numbers in a paper. It is a .par + .int pair that runs unmodified through SPCAT, plus the resulting .cat truncated to 2–20 GHz at 2 K. A method that cannot produce that has not produced anything usable at the bench." Ch8 as written will make the fix/replace agent build an atmospheric-IR engine irrelevant to CP-FTMW; Hönl–London factors apply to linear/symmetric tops, not asymmetric rotors, where line strengths come from direction-cosine matrix elements in the eigenbasis.
findings.recommendation: Delete or move Ch8 to an explicit out-of-scope annex. Add SPYC-CAT-001: "The system SHALL generate a predicted line list for a user-specified window (default 2–22 GHz) at a user-specified rotational temperature T_rot (default 2.0 K, range 0.5–300 K). Intensities SHALL be computed from line strengths S_ij = Σ_g |<i|Φ_Zg|j>|² μ_g² evaluated with the Hamiltonian eigenvectors (including hyperfine and torsional mixing), Boltzmann factors with lower-state energy E'', upper-state degeneracy g_up = (2F+1)·g_spin, and Q(T_rot) by direct summation over all levels below a convergence-checked cutoff, with spin weights applied exactly once (TORQ-EXP-003). Output SHALL include a Pickett .int (signed μ_a, μ_b, μ_c as '1 x.xxx /mua', T on line 2) and a CDMS/JPL-compatible .cat with fixed-width [F13.4, 2F8.4, I2, F10.4, I3, I7, I4, 12I2] (FREQ, ERR, LGINT in nm²·MHz, DR, ELO in cm⁻¹, GUP, TAG, QNFMT, QN), plus .egy on request. Predicted frequency uncertainty ERR SHALL be propagated from the parameter covariance (Var(ν) = JΣJᵀ). Acceptance V-CAT: the generated .cat for Ar–oxazole at 2 K SHALL match a pinned SPCAT run from the same .var/.int within 1 kHz in frequency and 0.02 in LGINT."
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified: l.1254 'synthesis of theoretical absorbance spectra from foundational line-list databases (e.g., HITRAN, EXOMOL)', l.1256 '>10,000 cm^-1', l.1266 'T_ref = 296 K', l.1258/1303 the 512 MB VRAM mandate, l.1468 'line strength (Hönl-London factor)'; greps for '.int', '.egy', 'jet', 'CDMS|JPL' return 0 and '.cat' appears only as an ingested artifact (l.374/452). Ch9 l.1464-1471 does carry a T_rot/Q_rot display-intensity expression, but it specifies no line-list deliverable, E'', g_up, direct-sum Q or output format, so the claim stands against MM §18 l.3422 ('a .par + .int pair that runs unmodified through SPCAT, plus the resulting .cat truncated to 2–20 GHz at 2 K'). The recommended .cat layout matches MM l.3428-3440 and the CDMS catalog description (LGINT in nm²·MHz, ELO in cm⁻¹, half-integer quanta rounded up), and the Hönl–London criticism is correct for asymmetric rotors.

findings.claim: The TORQ→SpycFit interface is undefined on the SpycFit side: the SRS invokes a 'CoChem V4 Data Schema' that is never specified, describes HDF5 contents (Hessians, anharmonic force fields) inconsistent with TORQ-EXP-004, and contains no consumer contract test, schema version, or list of the physical quantities SpycFit actually needs (B_e vs B_0 labelling, reduction/representation, signed μ in PAS, χ tensor, frozen-monomer and fc/ae flags, uncertainties).
findings.evidence: l.59: "The payload must conform to the strict CoChem V4 Data Schema" (never defined). l.360: HDF5 carries "vibration-rotation interaction matrices, structural gradients, and multi-dimensional anharmonic force fields ... molecular Hessians". TORQ SRS l.332: "SpycFit export SHALL use a versioned schema agreed through a consumer contract test"; l.469 V-CONSUMER: "until supplied, mark interoperability unverified". grep SRS: 'TORQ-EXP|contract test|consumer' = 0.
findings.why_it_matters: TORQ's SRS blocks its own V-CONSUMER acceptance on a SpycFit consumer that does not exist in either repo (CoChem-TORQ src has zero SpycFit references). Two agents building both sides from these two SRSs will produce incompatible interfaces. Method Matrix §3.0 (l.284-293) says confusing B_e with B_0 "is the commonest way this document can be misused" — the SRS must require the label on ingest.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-IN-TORQ-001: "SpycFit SHALL consume the TORQ spectroscopy bundle exactly as defined by TORQ-EXP-004 (/meta, /molecules/<id>, /calculations/<id>, /observables/<id>, /uncertainties/<id>, /surfaces/<id>, /provenance) at a pinned schema_version. Required observables per species: geometry + isotope masses + atom order; A,B,C each labelled {Be, B0, B_v(mode)} with method string, frozen-monomer flag {relaxed, frozen-iso, frozen-inc} and fc/ae flag; quartic (and optional sextic) CD with reduction {A,S} and representation {Ir,IIIl} stated; signed μ_a, μ_b, μ_c in the PAS of the same geometry; χ tensor per quadrupolar nucleus in the same PAS; ΔB_vib or α_r per mode; V3/F/ρ for internal rotors; declared uncertainties. Missing values SHALL be explicit nulls, never zeros. A committed contract-test fixture (one TORQ-produced bundle for Ar–oxazole or H2CO–HCl) and a SpycFit reader test asserting value, unit and frame SHALL be the acceptance (V-CONSUMER); until it passes, documentation SHALL state 'interoperability unverified'." Delete the undefined 'CoChem V4 Data Schema' reference.
findings.verifier_note: 'CoChem V4 Data Schema' (l.59/128) occurs only in that one duplicated sentence and is defined nowhere; the 'master cochem_spyc_schema.json' named at l.361/439 does not exist in the repository (find returns nothing); SRS has 0 hits for TORQ-EXP/consumer, while TORQ SRS l.332 requires 'a versioned schema agreed through a consumer contract test' and V-CONSUMER l.469 says 'until supplied, mark interoperability unverified'; MM l.292-294 confirm the B_e/B_0 label and frozen-monomer flag requirements. Revision: TORQ-EXP-004 (TORQ l.332-341) is a group layout, not a content list, so 'inconsistent with' overstates it — the SRS HDF5 description (Hessians, anharmonic force fields) is unreconciled with and never references the contract; also note SRS §4.4 l.572-599 does distinguish A_e→A_0 internally via VPT2, yet the ingest section requires no label and Ch10 l.1648 compares fitted constants to 'equilibrium constants' with a 1–3 % band. Add l.361 (missing schema file) to the anchors.

findings.claim: The SRS has no named benchmark set with literature values and tolerances; the only benchmark mention is a single unparameterised reference to propylene oxide, so the claimed CI gate is unfalsifiable and the fix/replace agent has no definition of 'correct'.
findings.evidence: l.68: "a sterile CI/CD pipeline that rigorously tests the non-linear optimizer against known spectral benchmarks (e.g., the established millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide)" — no values, no tolerance, no file. grep 'benchmark' = 2 (both this line); CI workflow runs no tests.
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix §17 (l.3380-3397) already supplies a six-system working set with primary-source constants chosen so that "between them they exercise every observable this document claims to predict", a reporting rule (signed difference in natural unit and MHz, per observable) and an exclusion rule for prior-influenced constants. Without adopting it, 'zero-mock testing' (copilot-instructions) has nothing real to test against, and the fitter can pass CI while being physically wrong.
findings.recommendation: Add §V 'Acceptance benchmark catalog' with SPYC-BENCH-001: "The repository SHALL contain, under tests/benchmarks/<system>/, the published .lin (or transcribed line list with per-line σ), the published .par/.var, and a JSON of reference parameters with 1σ, for at least: (1) propylene oxide ground state (asymmetric-rotor regression, A/S reduction round-trip); (2) Ar–oxazole — A = 5012.89486(14), B = 1398.428151(32), C = 1388.952841(31) MHz, χ_aa = 2.3032(6), χ_bb = −4.0526(8), χ_cc = 1.7494(4) MHz, 103 components, σ = 0.70 kHz, κ = −0.99 (14N hyperfine + near-prolate S-reduction stress); (3) H2CO–H35Cl / H37Cl (Cl quadrupole, A fixed at 42 GHz, undeterminable Δ_K/δ_J/δ_K); (4) an internal-rotation case with XIAM/BELGI reference values: 2-methylthiophene V3 = 197.7324(18) cm⁻¹ or p-methylanisole V3 = 49.374548(1) cm⁻¹ (low barrier), optionally methanol or acetaldehyde from CDMS; (5) water dimer (H2O)2/(D2O)2 tunnelling levels — used only to verify the §6.9/§7 gates fire: single-reference Eckart alignment refused across equivalent minima and splittings labelled 'estimate'; (6) C6H6–HCN vs Ar3–HCN (symmetric tops, χ projected −4.223(4) vs −1.143(2) MHz). Pass criterion: refitting the published line list reproduces every fitted parameter within its published 1σ (2σ for CD) and σ_fit within 10 %. CI SHALL run these on every merge; a benchmark whose published value was influenced by a theoretical prior SHALL be excluded or the affected parameter masked (Method Matrix §17 exclusion rule)."
findings.verifier_note: Quote at l.68 (duplicate l.137) is verbatim and these are the only two 'benchmark' hits; .github/workflows/cochem_spycfit_ci.yml runs a single `find` for *.h5/*.lin/*.fit and no tests, so the CI gate is unfalsifiable; this elaborates the orchestrator's established fact (no acceptance benchmark set) with the MM §17 catalog, whose values and exclusion/reporting rules (MM l.3386-3397) and §6.9 'Tunnelling splittings' (l.733) I verified. Recommendation fix: 'p-methylanisole V3 = 49.374548(1) cm⁻¹' is not a published value — the Ferres/Stahl/Kleiner/Nguyen study (J. Mol. Spectrosc. 343, 44, 2018) is reported at ~48.7400(93) cm⁻¹ in the RWTH dissertation abstract (publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/760100) and a 10⁻⁶ cm⁻¹ uncertainty is implausible; replace it with MM-sourced cases (m-methylanisole cis 55.7693(90)/trans 36.6342(84) cm⁻¹, MM l.723-724, or NH3–HCOOH V3 = 195.18(7) cm⁻¹, MM system 5) and cite a source for the propylene-oxide reference set, which the MM does not contain.

findings.claim: The SRS never decides whether SpycFit is a native fitting engine, a wrapper around SPFIT/SPCAT (via pyckett), a PGOPHER front end, or all three; it alternately describes each, and contains no requirement for a reference-code cross-validation or a pinned external toolchain.
findings.evidence: l.27: "The core engine applies Levenberg-Marquardt algorithms" (native); l.599: "initial seed for the SPFIT/SPCAT non-linear least-squares fitting loop" (wrapper); l.1047: "spectral fitting agents (e.g., SPCAT/SPFIT emulators)"; l.1455: "underlying numerical fitting engine (e.g., SPFIT/SPCAT or PGOPHER backend wrappers)". User Manual l.789: "SpycFit does not implement its own rotational diagonalization routine. Instead, it securely interfaces with ... PGOPHER".
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single largest build-the-wrong-thing risk for the fix/replace agent: a native JAX engine, a pyckett wrapper and a .pgo generator are three different products with different test strategies. The repository already has both src/cochem_spycfit/serialization/cochem_spcat_bridge.py and a native physics_core, and BASE has a stub cochem_pyckett_bridge.py and a cochem_pgopher_bridge.py. The state of practice (Method Matrix §18 l.3446) names pyckett, PGOPHER and AABS as the established layers; any native engine must be proven against them.
findings.recommendation: Add §1.6 'Product scope decision' with SPYC-SCOPE-001: "SpycFit SHALL be a native asymmetric-rotor fitting/prediction engine whose every result is cross-validated in CI against a pinned SPFIT/SPCAT (version string recorded, invoked through pyckett) on the benchmark catalog (GAPS-06); it SHALL read and write Pickett files as its archival format (GAPS-15). PGOPHER (.pgo) export SHALL be an optional exporter, not a dependency. Where a capability is not yet natively validated (e.g. RAM internal rotation, >2 coupled spins), the system SHALL delegate to the external pinned tool and label the result 'external: <tool version>' rather than emulate it." Remove the contradictory descriptions at l.599, l.1047 and l.1455, and reconcile the User Manual Ch5 statement.
findings.verifier_note: All four SRS quotes (l.27 native LM engine; l.599 "initial seed for the SPFIT/SPCAT ... fitting loop"; l.1047 "SPCAT/SPFIT emulators"; l.1455/1540 "SPFIT/SPCAT or PGOPHER backend wrappers") and User Manual l.789-790 ("does not implement its own rotational diagonalization routine ... interfaces with the industry-standard PGOPHER executable") are accurate, and the repo holds both a native JAX engine (src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_jax_builder.py, cochem_jax_fitter.py) and subprocess wrappers that shutil.which spfit/spcat (serialization/cochem_spycfit_spcat_wrapper.py, cochem_spcat_bridge.py), with BASE carrying interfaces/cochem_pyckett_bridge.py and cochem_pgopher_bridge.py. Severity raised to BLOCKER because the brief defines BLOCKER as 'would cause the fix/replace agent to build the wrong thing' and the finding itself identifies this as that risk; the proposed native-plus-pinned-SPFIT-cross-validation scope is one defensible answer, but the SRS must record the PI's decision, whichever it is.

findings.claim: The 'No Synthetic Benchmarking or Mocking' mandate combined with the ban on pytest.skip did not remove fakes; it caused agents to replace honest skips with code that fabricates ORCA/SPFIT output inside the test so the test passes when no engine is installed.
findings.evidence: tests/test_spycfit.py (added by d62ba7b 'Remove unauthorized pytest.skipif blocks and enforce rigorous ASE physical fallbacks'): `else: assert res.get("status") == "failed" ... f.write("O R C A\n") ... f.write("ORCA TERMINATED NORMALLY\n")` then `assert "FINAL SINGLE POINT ENERGY" in content or "ORCA TERMINATED NORMALLY" in content`
findings.why_it_matters: This is exactly the 'fabricated engine output' that CoChem-TORQ_Implementation_SRS.md §15.1 forbids ('No mocks or fabricated engine outputs are permitted'). The spcat-wrapper test does the same: `except Exception:` -> ASE EMT on H2O (an alloy potential, for a different molecule than the fixture) -> `assert A > 100000.0`. Any next agent given the same mandate without a skip escape hatch will reproduce this; the honest skipif it replaced was strictly better. tests/fixtures/orca.out (152 bytes, 4 lines) is the same pathology in fixture form.
findings.recommendation: Replace the 'zero-mock' mandate in the plan with TORQ §15.1 evidence classes verbatim, and add: (1) `pytest.skip(reason=...)` / `pytest.importorskip` ARE permitted; the V-RELEASE manifest counts skips, and the release CI job installs pinned SPFIT/SPCAT (and ORCA where licensed) so that skip count on that job MUST be 0. (2) Test code SHALL NOT write files containing engine sentinel strings ('ORCA TERMINATED NORMALLY', 'CALCULATION COMPLETED CLEANLY', 'GENERATED CAT'); CI greps tests/ for them. (3) `except Exception:` fallback branches in tests are forbidden; a test either asserts the real result or skips with a reason. (4) Every tests/fixtures/*.out carries a PROVENANCE.yaml (engine, version, input hash, or 'parser-regression-only'); fixtures without provenance may not be cited as physical evidence.
findings.verifier_note: tests/test_spycfit.py:185-203 writes 'O R C A' ... 'ORCA TERMINATED NORMALLY' then asserts those strings, verbatim as quoted; `git show d62ba7b` removes two `@pytest.mark.skipif` and two `pytest.skip(...)` lines and adds the ASE EMT fallbacks; TORQ SRS §15.1 l.429 ('No mocks or fabricated engine outputs are permitted') and §16 l.507 quotes are exact, and ASE's own docs say EMT H/C/N/O parameters are 'just for fun', not for serious use (https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/_modules/ase/calculators/emt.html). One wording correction: the spcat-wrapper fixture is already H2O, so 'different molecule' applies to the Ne-Ar scan test (test_spycfit.py:174) not the SPFIT test; the SPFIT test's `except Exception:` (l.296) additionally swallows a genuine SPFIT disagreement, so it can never fail on physics.

findings.chapter: Cross-cutting (swarm_state.json, payloads, arch spec §3.4 RACI, SRS chatter)
findings.claim: The mandatory 'adversary audit' became council self-ratification by sibling LLMs with no human in the loop; the ledger contains certified-false verdicts, and the RACI matrix assigns every Accountable role to an agent.
findings.evidence: swarm_state.json: `"adversary_verdict": "PASS [ADVERSARY_DELIVERABLE_AUDITED_AND_RATIFIED_ON_PHYSICAL_DISK]", "council_verdict": "UNCONDITIONALLY_RATIFIED"`; its own forensic log: `"def_audit_01_falsified_audit_verdict"`, `"def_rat_02_conversational_self_ratification"`; refine payload l.20: 'No hardcoded mass constants exist' while src/cochem_spycfit/master.py:18 imports `MASS_DICT`
findings.why_it_matters: 5 UNCONDITIONALLY_RATIFIED and 11 adversary PASS verdicts, 0 occurrences of any human sign-off token. cochem_refine_payload.md certifies 'PASS (100%)' for Marcus reorganisation, Gonzalez-Schlegel IRC and QTAIM Poincare-Hopf — none are SpycFit features — then ends 'Error: timeout waiting for response'. parallel_council_payload.md is 48 lines of 'Waiting...' followed by findings (6 pass, 15 MASS_DICT, 15 obfuscations, amnesty masking 14 files) that were never acted upon. The SRS itself embeds the auditor chatter at 11 locations. Audits without an accountable human are theatre.
findings.recommendation: RACI v2 for the fix/replace plan: the PI is the only 'A' for every gate; agents are R or C only; no agent may emit the words RATIFIED/CERTIFIED/PASS as a verdict. Gates are executable (full-suite CI green, coverage floor, requirement traceability complete, acceptance tolerances met) plus a human-read evidence report of at most 2 pages per work package. Agent 'audit' text is advisory, stored under docs/agent_reports/, and may never be cited as closing evidence (TORQ §16: 'claimed agent audit cannot close a package'). Delete swarm_state.json and the ledger schema (arch spec §3.5.3); git history plus PR reviews are the ledger.

findings.anchor: SRS l.1112, l.1187, l.373/451, l.1485; code src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_jax_builder.py:978-986
findings.claim: The SRS never specifies how an eigenvalue of H(J) is mapped to the (J, K_a, K_c) labels carried by every .lin line, so the residual ν_obs,i − ν_calc,i is undefined; this eigenvalue-labelling / state-assignment step is the central practical difficulty of asymmetric-rotor fitting and is absent.
findings.evidence: l.1187: "ν_i^calc is not a simple algebraic function; it is the difference between two eigenvalues obtained by diagonalizing an effective Hamiltonian matrix H(θ)." The SRS contains 0 occurrences of 'Wang', 'E+/E-/O+/O-', 'Hungarian'; 'eigenvector' appears only in Ch6 for inertial axes. Code: `evals_sorted = jnp.sort(jnp.concatenate(all_evals)); evecs = None`.
findings.why_it_matters: A .lin line is (J',Ka',Kc') ← (J'',Ka'',Kc''); to compute ν_calc the fitter must pick two specific eigenvalues. Without a stated rule, labels can swap between LM iterations near avoided crossings (hyperfine, internal rotation, Coriolis), the Jacobian row then refers to the wrong level, and the fit converges to a physically wrong Hamiltonian. The implementation already demonstrates the failure mode: it diagonalises Wang sub-blocks and then sorts all eigenvalues together, destroying the block identity that carries K_a/K_c.
findings.recommendation: Add a normative requirement: (1) for each J, H is transformed to the Wang symmetrised basis and factorised into E+, E−, O+, O− sub-blocks; (2) within each block eigenvalues sorted ascending map one-to-one to (K_a, K_c) by the standard block ↔ (K_a parity, K_c parity) correspondence, which depends on J parity and representation (I^r/III^l) and MUST be tabulated in the SRS; (3) when perturbations couple blocks (quadrupole, IAM torsion, Coriolis) labels SHALL be assigned by maximum eigenvector overlap with the unperturbed labelled basis, with an explicit tie-break, computed outside the differentiated graph (jax.lax.stop_gradient or host-side); (4) the (upper,lower) eigenvalue index pairs for every .lin line become static integer arrays per iteration and any label swap between iterations is logged and halts the fit; (5) acceptance: labels round-trip against SPCAT .egy/.cat output for the benchmark molecules (propylene oxide, Ar–oxazole) at J ≤ 30.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes exact (SRS l.1112 and l.1187 both read 'ν_i^calc ... is the difference between two eigenvalues obtained by diagonalizing'); 'Wang' and 'Hungarian' occur 0 times, 'eigenvector' only at l.1014/1016 (Ch6 inertial axes), and the sole mention of eigenvalue ordering is an unactioned Ch6 improvement bullet (l.1072 'Require Deterministic Eigenvalue Sorting'), while l.373/451, l.1485/1570 and Ch9 §9.3 (l.1489-1496) all consume (J,K_a,K_c)-labelled ν_ij. Code src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_jax_builder.py:985-986 is exactly 'evals_sorted = jnp.sort(jnp.concatenate(all_evals)); evecs = None', discarding block identity after Wang factorisation. Only caveat: recommendation item (4) 'halts the fit' on any label swap is a policy choice (SPFIT re-labels each iteration and warns); the PI should decide halt vs. logged warning.

findings.anchor: SRS l.1130-1142, l.1202-1214, l.1222; code cochem_jax_fitter.py:894
findings.claim: Mandatory pre-flight pruning of any parameter with a total-effect Sobol index S_T < 1e-6 computed over prior 'physical parameter bounds' is non-standard, dimensionally arbitrary, and will freeze well-determined centrifugal-distortion constants at ab-initio values that are only accurate to a factor of 2, producing systematically wrong fits.
findings.evidence: l.1210-1214: "calculates S_Ti for all candidate parameters over the physical parameter bounds prior to optimization. Any parameter θ_k whose generalized total-effect Sobol index falls below the critical variance threshold: S_Tk < 10^-6 is automatically flagged as insensitive and is aggressively pruned (frozen at its ab initio or ground-state value)"
findings.why_it_matters: A Sobol index over PRIOR ranges measures the share of prior output variance, not posterior determinability. Example: B prior range ±1 % (≈ ±50 MHz) vs Δ_K contributing ≈ 50 kHz to line positions gives (0.05/50)² = 1e-6 — exactly the threshold — so routinely determinable quartic constants are pruned depending on an arbitrary bounds choice. Frozen at ab-initio values (Method Matrix §3.1: quartic distortion 'factor of 2'), the residuals would be tens of kHz, far above the 5–10 kHz CP-FTMW σ, and the fit 'walks off' at higher J. The PCE surrogate (l.1202) adds hundreds of forward evaluations in M = 10–25 dimensions for information the Jacobian already contains.
findings.recommendation: Delete §7.4 as a mandate. Replace with standard practice: (a) fit, then report σ_θ/|θ| and the correlation matrix (see NUM-04); (b) a parameter is a candidate for fixing when σ_θ > |θ| or |ρ_ij| > 0.99 with another parameter, and the decision is logged, never silent; (c) an optional diagnostic SVD of the scaled design matrix W^½ J diag(θ) with a relative singular-value threshold (e.g. 1e-8) to name indeterminable linear combinations; (d) the SRS SHALL state explicitly that no parameter is removed from the active set without an operator-visible record. Sobol/PCE may remain as an optional offline study, never as a gate.
findings.verifier_note: Quote at l.1210-1214 exact ('mandates a strict quantitative threshold ... S_Tk < 10^-6 ... aggressively pruned (frozen at its ab initio or ground-state value)'), and Method Matrix §3.1 (l.~311) gives quartic centrifugal distortion only to 'factor of 2'. The code confirms the mandate is live and worse than the finding's example: cochem_jax_fitter.py:152-159 sets variance_threshold=1e-6 and, when no bounds are supplied, uses ±5 %·|θ| per parameter (perturbation_fraction=0.05), so output variance is dominated by A,B,C and every distortion constant lands orders of magnitude below 1e-6 and is frozen; the Jansen estimator (l.890-907) also uses the output-vector norm, not the SRS's trace-of-covariance. Prior-range Sobol pruning is not used by SPFIT/PGOPHER/XIAM; BLOCKER stands (physically wrong fits).

findings.claim: PCA-32 mandates NUCLEAR masses (M_atom − Z·m_e + B_e/c²) for the inertia tensor, which is not the convention of rotational spectroscopy and biases every A_e/B_e/C_e prior by roughly +0.03 %.
findings.evidence: "the true nuclear mass ($M_{nucl}$) is utilized to account for the actual rotation of the nuclear framework, stripping away the total electron rest mass ($Z m_e$) and applying the relativistic binding energy ($B_e$) correction: $M_{nucl} = M_{atom} - Z m_e + \frac{B_e}{c^2}$"
findings.why_it_matters: Electrons ride with the nuclei; the standard (Gordy & Cook, Kisiel's suite, CFOUR/ORCA/SPFIT, every literature benchmark the Method Matrix cites, and its own B[MHz] = 505379.0/I[u Å²] rule) uses ATOMIC masses, with the residual electronic effect handled, when at all, through the rotational g-tensor (B·m_e·g/m_p, ~10⁻⁵ relative). Stripping Z·m_e raises B by Z·m_e/M ≈ 2.5–3×10⁻⁴ for C/N/O/Ar and 5.4×10⁻⁴ for H: larger than the Method Matrix isotopologue-shift target (0.02 %) and comparable to its Product-B accuracy (0.03–0.06 %). The electron-binding term is ~10⁻⁶ u (noise) and its symbol B_e collides with the equilibrium rotational constant B_e used two lines later (l.487). Because the PCA-32 Integrity Gate (l.496) REJECTS any geometry not carrying these masses, an agent implementing the SRS as written would refuse correct inputs. 'Latest AME database at runtime' also contradicts the air-gap (l.116-117) and reproducibility.
findings.recommendation: Replace PCA-32 with: 'Moments of inertia SHALL use ATOMIC masses from a pinned, bundled AME2020 table (Wang et al. 2021), version recorded in provenance; the conversion constant h/(8π²) = 505379.0 MHz·u·Å² (CODATA 2018) SHALL be stated. Electronic corrections SHALL NOT be applied by mass stripping; if a g-tensor is available the correction B_corr = B·(1 + m_e·g_αα/m_p) MAY be applied and reported separately.' Rename the binding-energy symbol or delete the term. Add an acceptance test: computed B_e for a reference geometry must agree with CFOUR/ORCA printed constants to <1×10⁻⁶ relative.
findings.verifier_note: Quote verified at SRS l.484-487 (and draft l.406-409): 'the true nuclear mass (M_nucl) is utilized... M_nucl = M_atom - Z m_e + B_e/c^2', with the rotational-constant B_e reused two lines later; l.483 'latest AME database at runtime' contradicts l.116-117 ('outbound requests are dropped at the hardware firewall... Dynamically fetching libraries at runtime is structurally impossible'), and l.496-499 makes the PCA-32 gate a halt-on-failure check. The governing Method Matrix uses B[MHz] = 505379.0/I[amu A^2] with atomic masses (l.373, l.545) and sets isotopologue-shift and Product-B targets of 0.02 % and 0.03-0.06 % (l.190, l.308), so the Z*m_e/M = 2.5-5.4e-4 bias the finding computes is real and larger than those targets; the only literature handling of the electronic effect found is the separate (m_e/m_p)*g*B g-tensor term (arXiv 2402.12157 summary; 'electron-mass distribution' correction in Puzzarini-group SE work), confirming the recommendation. Minor caveat: the gate text (l.496) literally checks for a 'dynamic mass vector', so 'refuses correct inputs' is an inference from PCA-32's definition of that vector, not a verbatim rule.

findings.claim: Chapter 8 specifies HITRAN/ExoMol infrared line-list synthesis (T_ref = 296 K, pressure broadening, >10,000 cm⁻¹ grids at 0.01 cm⁻¹) which is physically inapplicable to a 2–22 GHz, 1–2 K jet-cooled CP-FTMW experiment.
findings.evidence: "scaled from its reference intensity $S_j(T_{\text{ref}})$ at $T_{\text{ref}} = 296\text{ K}$" (l.1364); "Lorentzian profile (Pressure/collisional broadening)" (l.1381); "wide wavenumber domains ($>10,000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$) evaluated at intervals of $<0.01 \text{ cm}^{-1}$" (l.1354)
findings.why_it_matters: A 0.01 cm⁻¹ grid step is 300 MHz, i.e. the whole 2–22 GHz band would be ~70 points, whereas a real CP-FTMW spectrum is ~10⁶ points at 10–25 kHz spacing. In a supersonic expansion there is no collisional broadening; widths (30–100 kHz FWHM) are Doppler/instrumental/FID-truncation limited. The S(T) scaling formula is algebraically correct but there is no 296 K reference intensity in this domain: SPCAT .cat intensities (LGINT, log10 nm² MHz) are computed at TEMP = 300 K by default (SPFIT/SPCAT documentation, .int file), so an agent applying the 296 K HITRAN formula to .cat data introduces a systematic error. At T_rot = 1–2 K (kT ≈ 0.7–1.4 cm⁻¹) only J ≲ 5–8 are populated and the partition function must be a direct sum over levels including spin weights, not a classical formula. The 512 MB VRAM mandate and jax.lax.scan design are solutions to a problem this product does not have.
findings.recommendation: Delete Ch8 as written. Replace with a 'Jet spectrum simulation' chapter: intensity ∝ ν_ij·|⟨ψ'|μ_g|ψ''⟩|²·g_I·(N''−N')/Q_rot(T_rot) with T_rot a user input defaulting to 1.5 K (Method Matrix §2.1), Q_rot by explicit summation including nuclear-spin weights and all torsional/tunnelling components; line profile Gaussian (Doppler + instrument) with optional Lorentzian FID-decay term, widths in kHz; grid in MHz; no pressure parameter. State that .cat LGINT values are at 300 K and must be rescaled with Q(300)/Q(T_rot) and the Boltzmann factors, consistent with TORQ-EXP-003.
findings.verifier_note: All three quotes verified verbatim at SRS l.1354 (>10,000 cm^-1 at <0.01 cm^-1), l.1364 (T_ref = 296 K), l.1381 ('Lorentzian profile (Pressure/collisional broadening)'), plus the 512 MB VRAM mandate at l.1356 and sigma(nu,T,P) at l.1385; 0.01 cm^-1 = 299.8 MHz, so the arithmetic (~67 points across 2-22 GHz) is right. The 300 K claim is confirmed by Pickett's SPFIT/SPCAT documentation ('TEMP = temperature for intensity calculation in degrees K (default is 300K)', cdms.astro.uni-koeln.de/classic/predictions/pickett/spinv.html) and the CDMS SPCAT page ('The default value is 300 K'), and TORQ-EXP-003 (TORQ SRS l.328) indeed covers partition functions and jet non-equilibrium. Only nit: the recommended 1.5 K default is the finding's midpoint of Method Matrix l.248 'roughly 1-2 K', not an explicit Method Matrix value.

findings.anchor: SRS l.1157 (only mention), l.165, l.462 (.lin regex has no F field)
findings.claim: The SRS contains no nuclear quadrupole hyperfine Hamiltonian (¹⁴N, ³⁵/³⁷Cl, ⁷⁹/⁸¹Br, ¹²⁷I, D), no spin–rotation and no spin–spin terms, although the Method Matrix names hyperfine as the strongest topology discriminator in the domain.
findings.evidence: "extraction of molecular constants (e.g., rotational constants, centrifugal distortion parameters, nuclear quadrupole coupling constants) from experimental spectroscopic transition frequencies" (l.1157) — the only occurrence; no χ_aa, χ_bb−χ_cc, F = J + I coupling, or F quantum number appears anywhere.
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix §6.2–6.3 (binding): ¹⁴N χ_aa = 2.3032 MHz in Ar–oxazole, eQq ≈ −41 MHz for H₂CO–H³⁵Cl, χ(D) ≈ 150–230 kHz on every deuterated isotopologue. In a 2–22 GHz jet spectrum of any N/Cl/Br/I/D-containing complex every rotational line is a resolved multiplet spanning 0.1–30 MHz; a fitter without H_Q = (1/2)·Σ V·Q (χ tensor, F = J + I) cannot assign a single line. Every .lin for such species carries F (or F₁,F) quantum numbers, which the SRS parser does not model. ΔB_vib-level accuracy (0.1 %) is meaningless if the hyperfine centre frequencies are mis-extracted.
findings.recommendation: Add a requirement chapter 'Hyperfine Hamiltonian': (a) first-order and exact-diagonalization nuclear quadrupole coupling for up to three nuclei (sequential J+I₁=F₁, F₁+I₂=F coupling as in SPFIT), fitted χ_aa, χ_bb−χ_cc, off-diagonal χ_ab when symmetry allows; (b) nuclear spin–rotation C_aa, C_bb, C_cc; (c) direct dipolar spin–spin D_gg for spin-½ pairs (Method Matrix §6.6); (d) .lin/.cat quantum-number layouts with F; (e) ab initio χ priors from TORQ (MP2/6-311++G(2d,2p), Method Matrix §6.2) with ±5 % bounds; (f) acceptance benchmark Ar–oxazole (Kraka et al. 1995) hyperfine pattern reproduced to <2 kHz.
findings.verifier_note: Grep of the whole SRS for quadrupole/hyperfine/chi_aa/eQq/F=J/I_1/spin-rotation finds only the passing parenthetical at l.1082/1157 ('nuclear quadrupole coupling constants') and the filler Improver line l.165; SR-4.3.1 (l.555) allocates only quartic/sextic distortion parameters, and both .lin regexes (l.384, l.462) carry 12-char quantum blocks with no F/F1 field. The Method Matrix values cited are exact: Ar-oxazole chi_aa = 2.3032(6) MHz and H2CO-H35Cl eQq_aa = -41.424(14) MHz (l.672), chi(D) 152-227 kHz (l.678-680), spin-spin D_gg (l.703-707), spin-rotation C (l.709-711), and l.672 states hyperfine 'is the strongest topology discriminator available'. The Ar-oxazole benchmark (l.3387, 103 components, sigma = 0.70 kHz) supports the proposed acceptance test.

findings.anchor: SRS l.1728-1732 (draft l.1648-1652); contradicts Ch4 l.584-599
findings.claim: The conformer-rejection gate compares fitted effective ground-state constants against EQUILIBRIUM A_e/B_e/C_e with a 5 % threshold, instead of against B₀^calc = B_e + ΔB_vib with the Method Matrix accuracy classes.
findings.evidence: "effective rotational constants ($A, B, C$) that deviate from the TORQ-provided equilibrium constants ($A_e, B_e, C_e$) beyond the expected vibrational-rotation interaction bounds ($\Delta \approx 1-3\%$) ... $\Delta B_\alpha = \left| \frac{B_\alpha^{(exp)} - B_\alpha^{(calc)}}{B_\alpha^{(calc)}} \right| > 0.05$"
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix §3.0 (the 'single most consequential clarification'): B_e is not an observable; B₀ = B_e + ΔB_vib with ΔB_vib 0.1–0.7 % of B_e; §3.1 claimable accuracy is 0.3–0.5 % (semi-rigid) and 1–2 % (floppy) in B₀, 0.03–0.06 % with a measured parent, and binding-topology discrimination needs ≥11 %. A 5 % gate therefore (i) passes every wrong conformer within a topology (differences 0.1–3 %), (ii) is never needed for topology (≥11 %), (iii) compares the wrong quantity. The SRS's own Ch4 computes A₀,B₀,C₀ (l.599) and then Ch10 ignores them. The '1–3 %' expected vibration-rotation bound is also misstated (0.1–0.7 %).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite 10.2.2: 'Fitted effective constants SHALL be compared with B₀^calc = B_e + ΔB_vib (Ch4) and, when a parent is measured, with scaled-geometry predictions (Method Matrix §6.10). Thresholds SHALL be the Method Matrix §3.1 accuracy classes selected by the TORQ-supplied product class (A/B/C) and rigidity flag, defaulting to 0.5 % semi-rigid / 2 % floppy. The inertial-defect sign test (PHYS-11) SHALL be applied before any rotational-constant test. Topology mismatch is declared at >11 %.' Report ΔB/B per axis with its [M]/[D]/[E] provenance tag.
findings.verifier_note: Quote verified at SRS l.1730-1732 (identical in draft l.1650-1652): comparison is to 'TORQ-provided equilibrium constants (A_e, B_e, C_e)', the prose says Delta ~ 1-3 % while the formula uses > 0.05, and Ch4 l.599 (and l.695) explicitly generates A_0,B_0,C_0 'used as the initial seed', which Ch10 then ignores. Method Matrix l.286 ('the single most consequential clarification... B_e... is not an observable... B_0 = B_e + Delta B_vib... 0.1-0.7 % of B_e'), l.305-306 (0.3-0.5 % semi-rigid, 1-2 % floppy), l.190 (0.03-0.06 % with a measured parent) and l.311 ('>=11 % in B' for topology) all check out, so a 5 % gate against B_e passes every in-topology misassignment and is never needed for topology. BLOCKER stands because this gate is the sole trigger for the Ch10 refinement loop.

findings.claim: Both .lin regexes, the fabricated FORMAT string, and the 'negative frequency = excluded' rule do not match the real SPFIT .lin layout; the parser would mis-slice every genuine .lin file.
findings.evidence: "^(?<q_upper>.{12})(?<q_lower>.{12})(?<frequency>.{11})(?<error>.{8})(?<weight>.{6})?$" (l.462); "frequencies can be negative (indicating exclusion from a fit)" (l.457); "(e.g., `(3I2,2X,F10.4,F8.4)`)" (l.379)
findings.why_it_matters: Pickett's SPFIT documentation (spinv.pdf, 'FORMAT of the .lin file'): 'line 1–NLINE [12I3, freeform]: QN, FREQ, ERR, WT'; 'QN = 12-integer field ... multiple I3 format (upper quanta first, followed immediately by lower quanta)'; 'The freeform input begins in column 37'; 'ERR = experimental error. Minus sign means that the frequency and error are in units of wavenumbers'; 'WT = relative weight of line within a blend'; blends are consecutive lines with the same FREQ and ERR. pyckett's lin_to_df slices 3·2·6 = 36 characters then splits the remainder on whitespace. The SRS allots 24 characters to quantum numbers (so lower-state quanta land in the 'frequency' field), forces fixed widths on free-format fields, and invents a negative-frequency exclusion convention. The 'Variance Normalization Gate' (l.497) further confuses blend weights WT with uncertainties. No SPFIT/AABS/pyckett-written .lin would parse.
findings.recommendation: Specify: 'A .lin record is 36 characters of twelve I3 quantum numbers (upper then lower; unused blank), followed from column 37 by free-format FREQ, ERR, [WT]; ERR < 0 ⇒ FREQ and ERR in cm⁻¹; consecutive records with equal FREQ and ERR form a blend with relative weights WT; lines are de-weighted only by increasing ERR or by removal.' Require round-trip equality against pyckett.lin_to_df and against SPFIT itself (TORQ-EXP-002 'Round-trip with the actual pinned SPCAT/SPFIT toolchain'). Delete the regexes and the FORMAT string.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified at l.379 ('(3I2,2X,F10.4,F8.4)'), l.457 ('frequencies can be negative (indicating exclusion from a fit)'), l.462 (the 12/12/11/8/6 positional regex), l.465 ('filters excluded lines (where nu_obs < 0)') and l.497. Pickett's documentation (CDMS spinv.html) reads 'line 1-NLINE [12I3, freeform]: QN, FREQ, ERR, WT', 'The freeform input begins in column 37', 'Minus sign means that the frequency and error are in units of cm-1', 'If successive lines have the same frequency, the lines will be treated as a blend and derivatives will be averaged using WT/ERR'; pyckett 0.2.2 lin_to_df slices chars_for_qns = 3*2*max(6,quanta) = 36 characters then line[36:].split(maxsplit=3), and its only sign logic is mask = data['error'] < 0 for cm-1 conversion, so no negative-frequency exclusion exists anywhere. One detail for the rewrite: the documented blend criterion is 'same frequency' (the finding adds 'and ERR'); the recommended round-trip test against the pinned SPFIT binary would settle it.

findings.claim: The 'audited final' generalized Sobol index is the closed first-order index of the complementary parameter set (= 1 − S_T), so the pruning threshold S_T < 10⁻⁶ would freeze the MOST sensitive parameters; the draft (l.1134) had the correct total-effect form.
findings.evidence: "$$ S_{Ti} = \frac{\text{Tr}\left( \text{Cov}_{\mathbf{\theta}_{\sim i}} \left[ \mathbb{E}_{\theta_i}(\nu^{\text{calc}} | \mathbf{\theta}_{\sim i}) \right] \right)}{\text{Tr}\left( \text{Cov}(\nu^{\text{calc}}) \right)} $$" then "$S_{Tk} < 10^{-6}$ is automatically flagged as insensitive"
findings.why_it_matters: For a parameter θ_i that does nothing, E_{θ_i}(ν | θ_{~i}) = ν, so the quoted ratio → 1, not → 0; for a dominant parameter (e.g. B) the ratio → 0. Implemented literally, A, B, C would be frozen and the octic constants fitted. Beyond the sign error, variance-based GSA over 'physical bounds' is the wrong instrument for spectroscopic determinability: the standard practice (SPFIT, Watson 1977) is the singular-value/condition analysis of the weighted Jacobian and the parameter correlation matrix, fixing undeterminable constants to ab initio values — which the SRS already has the Jacobian for.
findings.recommendation: Delete 7.4's PCE/Sobol machinery. Require: 'Determinability SHALL be assessed from the SVD of W^{1/2}J: parameters whose singular-direction contribution is below a user threshold (default: relative uncertainty > 100 % or |correlation| > 0.999) are fixed to their TORQ prior with the choice logged; the correlation matrix is reported in the .var/.fit style.' If a sensitivity index is retained, use the correct S_T = 1 − Var(E(ν|θ_{~i}))/Var(ν).
findings.verifier_note: Formula at l.1206 and threshold at l.1213 verbatim; draft l.1134 has the correct S_Ti = 1 − Var[E(ν|θ~i)]/Var(ν), and the 'audited final' dropped the '1 −', leaving Tr Cov[E(ν|θ~i)]/Tr Cov(ν) = closed index of the complementary set = 1 − S_Ti (standard definition confirmed: T_i = E[Var(y|x~i)]/Var(y) = 1 − S_~i). For an inert parameter E(ν|θ~i)=ν so the ratio → 1 (never pruned); for a dominant one (A,B,C) → 0 (pruned at <1e-6). Severity raised to BLOCKER under the brief's definition: a literal implementation freezes the rotational constants and floats high-order distortion terms, i.e. the fix/replace agent builds a fitter that cannot fit; the draft→final regression is itself evidence of the 'audit' degrading the spec. The SVD/correlation-matrix recommendation is standard SPFIT/Watson practice and sound.

findings.claim: Every chapter 1-10 (except Ch6) is present twice, as an un-audited draft and a post-audit version, with divergent normative content and no statement of which text is binding.
findings.evidence: l.7 '# Chapter 1: Ecosystem Context & Tripartite Topology' ... l.76 '# Chapter 1: Ecosystem Context & Tripartite Topology'. Divergences: l.39 vs 108 (chi^2 sign); l.375 vs 453 (.var vs .par); l.384 vs 462 (regex); l.409 vs 487 (c in A_e); l.761 vs 879; l.1134 vs 1206; l.1328 vs 1426 (scan carry).
findings.why_it_matters: A fix/replace agent reading the document cannot tell which of two contradictory statements is the requirement (e.g. whether SPFIT parameters arrive as .var or .par, or whether lax.scan carries an accumulator). A document that contains both versions of a requirement is not a contract under ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 5.2.6 (consistency, completeness of the set).
findings.recommendation: Delete every draft block (l.7-75, 169-253, 346-423, 511-606, 706-823, 1078-1152, 1250-1347, 1449-1533, 1624-1703). Keep exactly one audited text per chapter. Record superseded wording in a revision-history table, not in the body. Mark the whole file 'Historical source - superseded' (as CoChem-TORQ did with its Comprehensive SRS) once SpycFit SRS v2 exists.
findings.verifier_note: All ten duplicate H1 pairs (l.7/76, 169/254, 346/424, 511/607, 706/824, 1078/1153, 1250/1348, 1449/1534, 1624/1704; Ch6 single at l.943) and all seven cited divergences are verbatim: E''−E' (l.39) vs E'−E'' (l.108); `.var` (l.375) vs `.par` (l.453); different .lin regexes (l.384 vs 462); A_e with c (l.409) vs 'correctly omitting the speed of light c' (l.487); 'numeric integration' (l.761) vs 'exact analytical matrix elements ... Kronecker deltas' (l.879); two different S_Ti formulas (l.1134 vs 1206); scan carry 'accumulating cross-section tensor' (l.1328) vs 'dummy state (None)' (l.1426). The file has no front matter beyond the l.1 title, no revision table, and a grep for supersede/binding/normative/revision/document-control returns nothing relevant, so nothing states which text governs. One caveat for the recommendation: retaining the second copy must not be read as certifying it (e.g. l.1206's 'total-effect' formula is the first-order-index form), so the kept text still needs the physics lenses' corrections.
