findings.claim: SpycFit is specified as stateless and memory-flushing in Chapter 1 and as a persistent state manager, persistent compiled-kernel cache, persistent Voila kernel, cross-session exclusion manifest and daemon in Chapters 2, 9 and 10.
findings.evidence: l.60 'immediately flushes its physical memory. It holds zero persistent state'; l.175 'centralized, in-memory continuous state manager'; l.207 'written to a distributed LevelDB cache on the local disk'; l.1455 'The Voila kernel maintains the persistent state of the active ... Hamiltonian'; l.1701 'The SpycFit daemon'.
findings.why_it_matters: State ownership is architecture-defining. The fix agent cannot decide whether session state, fit checkpoints, and task state live in SpycFit, in BASE's durable task service, or nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Replace the 'stateless' slogan with a state-class table: (a) interactive session state (SpycFit, lifetime = session), (b) compiled-kernel cache (local, content-addressed, non-authoritative), (c) durable task state (BASE, single commit authority per TORQ ARCH-07), (d) run artifacts and provenance (artifact store, immutable). One requirement per class with owner, lifetime and recovery behaviour.
findings.verifier_note: The contradiction stands and every opposing quote is verbatim (l.175/260 'centralized, in-memory continuous state manager'; l.207/292 'written to a distributed LevelDB cache on the local disk'; l.1455/1540 'The Voila kernel maintains the persistent state'; l.1521/1606 'reproducibility across sessions'; l.1700-1701/1780-1781 SpycFit 'transitions the current task state in the SQLite job_board' and 'The SpycFit daemon'), but the l.60 evidence quote is truncated: the full sentence is 'It holds zero persistent state regarding the origin of the data', so the quote must carry the qualifier and the unqualified stateless claim should instead be anchored on the bullet heading 'Stateless Processing', 'immediately flushes its physical memory' (l.60/129) and l.1805 'Explicit Preservation of Stateless Processing in Tier III. Rationale: Keeps state tracking securely in Tier I and Tier II.' Two amendments to the recommendation: the 'single commit authority' rule is TORQ-ARC-002 (TORQ SRS l.102, 'Only one authority commits task state'), with D08/ARCH-07 (l.536) being the local-SQLite-coordinator decision, so cite TORQ-ARC-002/D08; and the 'zero persistent state regarding the origin of the data' clause itself conflicts with the provenance/FAIR obligations the repo tests (tests/test_provenance_fair_security_suite.py), so provenance must be an explicit row in the state-class table. BLOCKER is not inflated: whether SpycFit is a daemon that writes TORQ's job_board or a stateless consumer decides the component boundary the fix agent builds.

findings.claim: The air-gap / unidirectional data-diode model is contradicted by six specified reverse or external flows: dead-letter writes back to TORQ, runtime queries to an isotope registry and 'latest AME', a web UI, user file imports, and direct SQLite job_board writes that inject TORQ tasks.
findings.evidence: l.55 'TORQ acts as a unidirectional data diode'; l.19 'Air-gapped. Zero external ingress'; l.59 'silent drop of the task back to TORQ's dead-letter queue'; l.1700-1701 'SpycFit transitions the current task state in the SQLite `job_board` ... injects a high-priority `TORQ_REFINEMENT_SWEEP` task'.

Security prose that cannot be reconciled with the functional requirements is not a requirement.
findings.recommendation: Delete the air-gap/diode narrative. Replace with verifiable interface requirements: SPYC-FB-001 refinement requests SHALL be submitted as versioned records through the BASE task-service contract (never direct DB writes); SPYC-NFR-SEC-001 a fit SHALL make no network calls (test: run under a no-route network namespace); SPYC-MASS-001 masses SHALL come from a pinned local table with recorded version and digest.

Zero external ingress', l.55/124 'TORQ acts as a unidirectional data diode', while l.59/128 and l.421/499 write back to TORQ's dead-letter queue, l.395/473 'query the central Mendeleev Isotope Registry', l.405/483 'latest AME ... at runtime', l.1453/1538 Voila web frontend, l.1524/1609 user file import, and l.1700-1701/1780-1781 'transitions the current task state in the SQLite job_board ... injects a high-priority TORQ_REFINEMENT_SWEEP task'. findings.chapter: Ch3 §3.3 vs Ch6 Improvements, Ch1 §1.3; TORQ-SCI-002
findings.claim: The mass mandate is triply contradictory and physically consequential: nuclear masses from the 'latest' AME fetched at runtime (PCA-32) vs hardcoded IUPAC enums (Ch6 improvement) vs the ecosystem convention of pinned isotope-specific atomic masses (TORQ-SCI-002), inside a system that forbids runtime fetching.
findings.evidence: l.395 'no static mass floats may exist within the SpycFit computational graph'; l.405 'dynamically injected from the latest AME ... at runtime'; l.407 'M_nucl = M_atom - Z m_e + B_e/c^2'; l.1064 'Hardcode IUPAC Mass Constants as Immutable Tier III Enums'; TORQ: 'Masses use isotope-specific atomic masses with source and version'.
findings.why_it_matters: Atomic vs nuclear mass differs by Z*m_e/M (approx. 0.027% for 12C), the same order as the Method Matrix isotopologue-shift target (0.02%) and Product-B accuracy (0.03-0.06%). If TORQ priors use atomic masses and SpycFit re-derives constants with nuclear masses, priors and fits sit on different mass scales. 'Latest' is non-reproducible. Standard rotational structure practice (Kraitchman/STRFIT) uses atomic masses; the physics lens should confirm.
findings.recommendation: SPYC-MASS-001: SpycFit SHALL use isotope-specific atomic masses from a pinned AME table shipped with the package (edition and SHA-256 recorded in every provenance record), identical to the TORQ constants service. Nuclear-mass correction, if ever wanted, is an explicitly named option with its own acceptance test. Delete 'PCA-32' (undefined acronym, 0 occurrences outside the SRS).
findings.verifier_note: Claim and physics confirmed: l.395/473, 405/483, 407/485, 1064 quoted accurately; TORQ SRS l.54 reads verbatim 'Masses use isotope-specific atomic masses with source and version.'; Z*m_e/M = 0.0274% (12C, 16O) and 0.054% (1H), exceeding Method Matrix l.309 isotopologue-shift target 0.02% and comparable to l.307 Product-B 0.03-0.06%; standard practice (Oka & Morino 1961, applied in Muller et al. arXiv:1812.01554) uses atomic masses and corrects electron effects via dB_el = -B_e*g_ii*m_e/m_p (~1e-5 relative), so stripping Z*m_e is both non-standard and ~20x too large. findings.claim: The .lin parser is specified by two different regular expressions that disagree with each other and (as far as I can verify) with the SPFIT .lin layout, and no acceptance test on a real .lin file is named.
findings.why_it_matters: A regex is design, not a requirement, and this one is the only normative interface text for the primary experimental input. SPFIT's documented .lin layout is 12 quantum numbers in 12I3 (36 columns) followed by free-format frequency, uncertainty and weight; both regexes allot 24 columns to quantum numbers. Confidence on the format detail is moderate; check Pickett's spfit documentation.
findings.recommendation: Specify by reference: 'SPYC-ING-00x: SpycFit SHALL read SPFIT .lin files as defined by the SPFIT documentation for the pinned version, including negative (excluded) frequencies and blank uncertainty defaults.' Acceptance SV-LIN: parse named public .lin files (e.g., the propylene oxide and H2CO-HCl datasets) and reproduce line counts, quantum numbers and frequencies exactly. Remove the regexes.
findings.verifier_note: Both regexes quoted accurately (l.384, l.462) and the external fact is confirmed: SPFIT .lin is '[12I3, freeform]: QN, FREQ, ERR, WT' (spinv.html), i.e. 36 fixed columns of quantum numbers then free-format fields, whereas both SRS regexes allot 24 columns ((?<q_upper>.{12})(?<q_lower>.{12})) and l.462 forces fixed widths on the free-format fields, so neither parses a real .lin file; no test on a real .lin is named (grep 'test' near .lin/parser: 0 hits). Recommendation must be corrected: SRS l.457/465 and the finding's own 'negative (excluded) frequencies' are wrong -- the documentation says 'Minus sign means that the frequency and error are in units of cm-1' (converted internally to MHz), not exclusion from the fit. Raised to BLOCKER because the only normative spec for the primary experimental input contradicts the pinned format in column count, fixed-vs-free layout and sign semantics, and with the repo's fabricated fixtures an agent building to it would pass tests while failing on every real .lin.

findings.claim: Chapter 2 specifies SpycFit as an NMR / FT-ICR mass-spectrometry / UV-Vis / EPR / protein-NMR engine, which is outside the Method Matrix system class (5–10 atom complexes, 2–22 GHz CP-FTMW) and outside every other SpycFit artifact.
findings.evidence: l.173: "experimental spectroscopic data (NMR, IR, UV-Vis, EPR)"; l.179: "In high-field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) or high-resolution Fourier-Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance Mass Spectrometry (FT-ICR MS)"; l.317: "3D HNCA (Protein NMR) | 2048 × 1024 × 1024 | 32.0 GiB | Depth-wise Slicing"
findings.why_it_matters: The entire VRAM-chunking, FFT cross-correlation and CPU-fallback design of Ch2 is sized for 16–32 GiB NMR tensors that a 2–22 GHz CP-FTMW spectrum (typically 10^5–10^7 points, ≤100 MB in FP64) never produces. An agent implementing Ch2 would build a hardware gatekeeper for a product that does not exist and the FP64 justification (l.179, 10^-3 Hz on 10^8 Hz carriers) is the wrong argument for microwave work (kHz on GHz).
findings.recommendation: Delete Ch2 §2.1 sentence 2, §2.2 paragraph 1, §2.5 entirely and the routing matrix rows that depend on it. Replace with a one-page 'Numerical environment' section: JAX FP64 mandatory because Watson-Hamiltonian eigenvalue differences of ~10^4 MHz must be resolved to ~1 kHz (10^-7 relative) and quartic constants are ~10^-6 of A; state the actual data sizes for this product (N_obs ≤ ~10^3 assigned lines, broadband trace ≤ 10^7 points, J ≤ ~30 at 2 K) so no VRAM chunking requirement is needed for the fitter. If FFT cross-correlation of a predicted stick spectrum against the observed trace is wanted for conformer identification, re-specify it as a microwave-domain feature in the assignment chapter, not as an NMR feature.
findings.verifier_note: Every anchor checks out: l.173/258 '(NMR, IR, UV-Vis, EPR)', l.179/264 NMR/FT-ICR MS with 10^-3 Hz on 10^8 Hz, l.206/291 '4-spin NMR Hamiltonian', l.216/301 NOESY/HSQC 32k x 32k, l.227-228/316-317 '2D Heteronuclear NMR' and '3D HNCA (Protein NMR) ... 32.0 GiB', l.321 'non-separable 3D Voigt convolutions'. The whole chunking/fallback design is sized for 16-32 GiB NMR tensors while a 2-22 GHz trace at 10 kHz spacing is ~2x10^6 points (~16 MB FP64); the FP64 case for this product rests on resolving ~10^6 MHz rotational energies (J~20) to ~1 kHz and D_J/A ~ 10^-6, not on NMR J-couplings, so the recommendation is sound and if anything understates the needed relative precision.

findings.claim: Chapter 8 specifies an infrared/exoplanet-atmosphere line-list cross-section engine (HITRAN/EXOMOL, T_ref = 296 K, >10,000 cm⁻¹ grids, pressure broadening, 512 MB VRAM cap) that has no relation to a jet-cooled 2–22 GHz CP-FTMW assignment tool, and its module path implies a monorepo that §1.5 forbids.
findings.evidence: l.1254: "synthesis of theoretical absorbance spectra from foundational line-list databases (e.g., HITRAN, EXOMOL)"; l.1266: "reference intensity S_j(T_ref) at T_ref = 296 K"; l.1299: "For typical EXOMOL datasets (N_lines > 10^6)"; l.1343: "Module: cochem.spycfit.convolution"
findings.why_it_matters: HITRAN/EXOMOL contain no 5–10 atom van der Waals complexes; a supersonic jet at 1–2 K has no pressure broadening to speak of and no 296 K reference population; cm⁻¹ grids are the wrong unit domain. The 512 MB VRAM mandate and jax.lax.scan chunking solve a problem the product does not have, while the real convolution need (overlaying a predicted rotational stick spectrum, Doppler/instrument-broadened in MHz, on the observed trace) is unspecified. The hardcoded 296 K default has already leaked into Start_SpycFit.ipynb cell 3 and interfaces/cochem_spycfit_ui.py l.205.
findings.recommendation: Delete Ch8. Replace with a short 'Rotational spectrum synthesis' section in the prediction chapter: intensities from the Ch9 formula at a user-supplied T_rot (default 1.5 K, range 0.5–10 K), nuclear-spin weights as explicit user input (see SCOPE-25), Gaussian or Voigt profile in MHz with FWHM set from the instrument (CP-FTMW Doppler-limited, typically 50–100 kHz), no pressure broadening, no reference-temperature scaling. Remove the 512 MB mandate; state a performance target in terms of this product (e.g., re-synthesis of a 2–22 GHz catalog of ≤10^5 lines in <1 s on Setup 2). Change the module path to cochem_spycfit.* consistent with §1.5 polyrepo.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes are exact at l.1254/1352 (HITRAN, EXOMOL), l.1266/1364 (T_ref = 296 K), l.1299/1397 (N_lines > 10^6), l.1256/1354 (>10,000 cm^-1), l.1258/1303/1356 (512 MB mandate), l.1343/1441 ('cochem.spycfit.convolution', a dotted parent package at odds with the §1.5 'cochem-spycfit-core' polyrepo); the 296 K leak is verified in Start_SpycFit.ipynb cell 3 (temperature_k=296.0) and ui.py l.205. Neither HITRAN nor ExoMol carries rotational line lists for 5-10 atom vdW complexes, a 1-2 K jet has no pressure broadening or 296 K reference population, and the real need (predicted stick spectrum broadened in MHz over the observed trace) is unspecified; the recommended FWHM default of 50-100 kHz is consistent with reported CP-FTMW linewidths (<40 kHz to ~100 kHz depending on instrument) and is correctly left as an instrument input.

findings.claim: The identity of the fitting engine is undecided across artifacts: Ch7 specifies SpycFit's own JAX autodiff LM as the fitter, Ch9 names 'SPFIT/SPCAT or PGOPHER backend wrappers', the Manual says SpycFit 'does not implement its own rotational diagonalization' and uses PGOPHER, and the code ships a parity auditor comparing JAX against SPFIT to 0.1 kHz.
findings.evidence: l.1455: "the underlying numerical fitting engine (e.g., SPFIT/SPCAT or PGOPHER backend wrappers)"; l.1084: "representing the entire forward model ... as a sequence of pure, differentiable JAX primitives"; auditor.py l.2: "Mathematical Parity Auditor: JAX autodiff Hamiltonian vs. Pickett SPFIT."
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single largest scope decision for the rebuild: writing and validating a general effective-Hamiltonian eigensolver (asymmetric top + quadrupole + internal rotation + tunnelling + Coriolis) is a multi-year project that SPFIT/SPCAT and PGOPHER already deliver; wrapping them is weeks. The SRS must say which is the engine of record and which (if any) is a cross-check, or the agent will build both badly.
findings.recommendation: Decide and state in Chapter 0: Option A (recommended for v2): SPFIT/SPCAT (pinned version) is the fitter and predictor of record; SpycFit owns assignment, bookkeeping, windows, UI and I/O; a JAX forward model may exist only for fast what-if rendering and must be labelled non-authoritative. Option B: SpycFit's JAX engine is authoritative, with SPFIT parity as an acceptance test for every Hamiltonian term supported, and unsupported terms (quadrupole, internal rotation) explicitly declared out of v2 scope. Remove PGOPHER from the SpycFit SRS unless a PGOPHER export is specified as an output format.
findings.verifier_note: All quotes exact (SRS l.1455/1540, l.1084/1159, auditor.py docstring l.1-2, Manual l.789-790), and the SRS itself holds three positions: l.599/695 seed "the SPFIT/SPCAT non-linear least-squares fitting loop", Ch7 makes JAX the entire forward model, Ch9 says "SPFIT/SPCAT or PGOPHER backend wrappers". Severity raised to BLOCKER because the governing Method Matrix l.3632 has already decided the question — "JAX and the GPU are retained for DVR Hamiltonian diagonalisation and search-space pruning ... and are **not** used to replace SPFIT" — so Ch7 is not ambiguous but contrary to the governing document and would have the agent build the wrong engine. Recommendation should present Option A as the decided answer citing MM l.3632 (SPFIT/SPCAT via pyckett, MM l.3446, as engine of record; JAX only for DVR/search pruning/what-if), not as a choice.

findings.recommendation: Proposed definition: 'CoChem-SpycFit is the rotational-spectroscopy assignment and fitting workbench of the CoChem ecosystem. It consumes (i) the versioned TORQ spectroscopy bundle containing, per candidate conformer/topology and isotopologue, A0/B0/C0 (or Ae/Be/Ce + ΔB_vib) with Method-Matrix Product class and [M]/[D]/[E] tags, quartic (and where available sextic) distortion constants, signed dipole components, nuclear quadrupole tensors, inertial defect and planar moments, vibrational-satellite constants and, for LAM systems, barrier and tunnelling estimates, and (ii) a jet-cooled broadband CP-FTMW spectrum (2–22 GHz, T_rot 1–2 K) or its peak list. It predicts catalogs with search windows, drives the human assignment loop (predict → search → pattern-match → assign → fit → re-predict) with full quantum-number labelling (J Ka Kc, F for hyperfine, vt/σ or tunnelling-doublet symmetry), fits effective rotational Hamiltonians (Watson A/S, quadrupole, internal rotation/tunnelling doublets) to assigned lines by weighted least squares with SPFIT/SPCAT parity, runs isotopologue and conformer campaigns, and exports SPFIT/SPCAT-compatible files, residual lists, refinement requests and publication tables with provenance. It is an interactive, stateful, single-workstation (Method Matrix Setup 2) tool hosted in BASE's UI.' IS: microwave/CP-FTMW rotational assignment and fitting; effective-Hamiltonian fitting; isotopologue, conformer, satellite and hyperfine campaigns; prediction windows from Product class; SPFIT/SPCAT I/O and parity; residual bookkeeping; publication export; refinement-request authoring. IS NOT: electronic structure, geometry optimization, VPT2 or any quantum-chemistry output parsing (TORQ); conformer/topology search (TOPOS); UI hosting, scheduling, task queues, air-gap/network security (BASE/deployment); IR, Raman, UV-Vis, TD-DFT, NMR, EPR, mass spectrometry; HITRAN/EXOMOL line lists, 296 K scaling, pressure broadening, radiative transfer; mm-wave/THz/radio-astronomy catalog production beyond 26 GHz; MLFF/scout-anchor logic; Jensen inverse-inertia averaging (TORQ §5.1). IR/Raman convolution decision: SpycFit v2 contains none. The only lineshape operation retained is a MHz-domain Gaussian/Voigt instrument-function convolution of its own rotational stick spectrum for overlay on the observed trace. Move vibrational IR/Raman stick-spectrum rendering to a separate small module (the repo already names one, cochem_vibspyc_snap, 'VibSpyc') or to TORQ reporting, and rewrite README §1-3 and Manual §5.2.1/§5.4.1 (drop Type=IR|Raman|UVVIS) in the same change so the three documents agree.

findings.claim: Nuclear quadrupole (14N, 35/37Cl, 79/81Br, 127I) and deuterium hyperfine structure, which the Method Matrix calls the strongest topology discriminator and which every deuterated isotopologue introduces, is absent from the SRS's Hamiltonian, quantum-number model (.lin regex has no F), UI and fitting chapters, and from the code.
findings.evidence: l.1082: "extraction of molecular constants (e.g., rotational constants, centrifugal distortion parameters, nuclear quadrupole coupling constants)" (the only body mention); Method Matrix l.672: "hyperfine structure is the strongest topology discriminator available, because χ is a tensor and therefore reports the orientation of the nucleus in the principal axis frame"
findings.why_it_matters: Half of the Method Matrix's anchor systems (Ar–oxazole, H2CO–HCl, C6H6–HCN, SO2⋯DF, ammonia–formic acid) have resolvable hyperfine in a CP-FTMW spectrum; without F quantum numbers and χ_aa, χ_bb−χ_cc in the fit, the lines cannot be assigned at all (each J transition is a 3–9 component multiplet spanning MHz). A rebuild from this SRS would produce a tool that cannot assign any nitrogen- or halogen-containing complex.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-HFS-001..004: (1) Hamiltonian terms for one or two coupling nuclei (χ_aa, χ_bb−χ_cc, off-diagonal where needed) with SPFIT parameter IDs; (2) quantum labels extended to F (and F1 for two nuclei) in the data model, .lin writer and UI; (3) hyperfine-pattern prediction from TORQ χ tensors (5 % accuracy band) for recognition; (4) option to fit hypothetical unsplit centre frequencies when components are blended. Decide (SCOPE-14) whether these terms are computed by SpycFit's own solver or by SPFIT.
findings.verifier_note: Verified 0 hits for hyperfine/quadrupole/chi_aa/eQq/nqcc in both src/cochem_spycfit and cochem_spycfit; in the SRS 'quadrupole' occurs only at l.165 (filler checklist), 1082 and 1157 (Ch7 intro, both copies), the .lin QN list (l.373/451) reads 'J, Ka, Kc, v, …' with no F, and the regex (l.462) names no quantum numbers. Method Matrix l.672 quote exact; of its six-system working set (l.3386-3391) four have nuclear-quadrupole hyperfine (Ar–oxazole 14N, H2CO–HCl Cl, NH3–HCOOH 14N, C6H6–HCN 14N) plus (D2O)2 deuterium, so 'half' is an understatement and BLOCKER is warranted for a 5–10-atom-complex engine.

findings.claim: The SRS defines SpycFit as a stateless batch 'data sink' that flushes memory after one fit, which is the wrong product class for an assignment campaign that is inherently stateful, multi-session and weeks long; Ch9 and the code (DAG commits, time-travel) already contradict Ch1.
findings.evidence: l.60: "SpycFit ingests the data, performs the diagonalization and fitting matrices generation, writes the final output constants (.fit / .par files) to a designated egress node, and immediately flushes its physical memory. It holds zero persistent state"; l.1455: "The Voila kernel maintains the persistent state of the active quantum mechanical Hamiltonian and the corresponding experimental datasets"
findings.why_it_matters: Beyond the internal contradiction (another lens), this is a scope decision: a batch engine is designed around a job payload and an egress file; a workbench is designed around a project (spectrum, peak list, candidate species, assignments, fit history) that is saved, reopened and branched. The fix agent must know which to build; the Method Matrix workflow (QS-1 and assignment) and the old plan both describe a project-based interactive tool.
findings.recommendation: State in Chapter 0: 'SpycFit is a project-based interactive workbench; a project (spectrum, peak list, species catalogs, assignments, fit history, outputs) is persisted in a versioned on-disk bundle and may be reopened and branched. A headless batch mode (fit a given .lin/.var) is a secondary CLI entry point.' Delete §1.3 air-gap and §1.4 statelessness text; move any deployment-security requirements to BASE.
findings.verifier_note: l.60 ('immediately flushes its physical memory. It holds zero persistent state') and l.1455 ('The Voila kernel maintains the persistent state') verified verbatim, plus l.1521 'ensuring reproducibility across sessions'; code confirms the workbench model: src/cochem_spycfit/core_engine/cochem_spycfit_state.py l.2 'Immutable FitState model and DAG CommitManager' with branch_from() at l.185, and src/cochem_spycfit/cochem_spycfit_ml_storage.py (path correction: not under core_engine/) l.8 'DAGCommitManager: ... branching, time-travel reversion'. TORQ SRS l.25 ('SpycFit owns spectral assignment and fitting ... optional notebook/Voila interaction managed through BASE') and old plan Stage 3 ('The UI pauses and presents the user') both describe an interactive project tool, so an agent following Ch1 would delete the state engine while one following Ch9 would build it: BLOCKER stands.

findings.anchor: SRS l.539, 555, 570, 601 (only SR-* IDs); tests/* ; src/cochem/*
findings.claim: The SRS has no requirement-ID scheme, no verification method per requirement and no traceability matrix, while the tests and code trace to ~40 REQ-* IDs that exist only in prompt files outside the repo and in the foreign src/cochem tree.
findings.evidence: grep over SRS: 'acceptance' 0 hits, 'traceab' 0, 'verification method|verified by' 0, 'shall' 6, 'must' 52, 'System Requirement' 10 (5 distinct, each duplicated). REQ-* IDs: tests 167 + tests/qc 96 occurrences (40 distinct), SRS 0, src/cochem_spycfit 0, src/cochem 225.
findings.why_it_matters: An audit/fix/replace agent cannot decide whether a module is in or out of contract, whether a test proves anything, or what 'done' means. Every REQ-* the tests cite is unfalsifiable against this SRS, which is exactly how the prior swarm's 'malicious compliance' was able to pass.
findings.recommendation: SRS v2 must impose: (1) every normative statement gets an ID SPYC-<AREA>-NNN (AREA in {ING, HAM, FIT, PICK, OBS, UI, EGR, NFR}); (2) each requirement carries a verification method (analysis/inspection/test), the owning module path (src/cochem_spycfit/...), and >=1 acceptance-test ID V-NNN; (3) a machine-readable docs/traceability.yaml (req_id -> [test_id] -> module) checked in CI: a test marked @pytest.mark.req('SPYC-...') whose ID is absent from the SRS fails collection, and an SRS requirement with zero linked tests fails the build; (4) all REQ-QC/TOPOS/TORQ/CORE/BM/THM/ML/HW/DIST IDs are declared out of scope and removed from this repo.
findings.verifier_note: All counts reproduce (SRS: 'acceptance' 0, 'traceab' 0, 'verification method|verified by' 0, shall 6, must 52, REQ- 0; REQ-* in tests 167, tests/qc 96, 40 distinct IDs, src/cochem 225, src/cochem_spycfit 0; zero pytest.mark.req; no Perfected_SRS prompt files in repo). One evidence correction: the 10 'System Requirement' hits are 4 distinct IDs (SR-4.2.1/4.3.1/4.3.2/4.4.2) each duplicated at l.539/635, 555/651, 570/666, 601/697, not 5. With no IDs, verification methods or trace matrix the SRS cannot function as a contract, which is the brief's BLOCKER definition; the SPYC-<AREA>-NNN / V-NNN / traceability.yaml recommendation mirrors the TORQ SRS style the brief holds up as the model.

findings.claim: Three independent Watson A-reduction Hamiltonian builders inside src/cochem_spycfit give three different Delta-K=+-2 matrix elements for the delta_J/delta_K terms; at most one can agree with the SRS operator (l.35/551), and no test exercises a nonzero delta_J or delta_K against an external reference.
findings.evidence: jax_builder.py:656: 'delta_xy - 2.0 * delta_j_small * j_jp1 - delta_k_small * (k_source * k_source + k_target * k_target)'; jax_driver.py:122: '-delta - dJ * j_jp1 - 0.5 * dK * (k_source * k_source + k_target * k_target)'; ml_engine.py:412: '0.25 * (B - C) * coupling_term - dJ * j_factor * coupling_term - dK * (k_upper**2 + (k_upper + 2.0)**2) * coupling_term'
findings.why_it_matters: From the SRS operator -2 delta_J P^2(P_x^2-P_y^2) - delta_K[P_z^2,(P_x^2-P_y^2)]_+ with (P_x^2-P_y^2)=(P_+^2+P_-^2)/2, the textbook element is {(B-C)/4 - delta_J J(J+1) - (delta_K/2)[(K+2)^2+K^2]} x sqrt(...) (Gordy & Cook Table 8.14 / Watson 1977). jax_builder doubles both delta terms; ml_engine doubles delta_K; jax_driver has textbook magnitudes but flips the sign of (B-C)/4 relative to the delta terms, i.e. fits -delta_J,-delta_K. Fitted quartic constants would be wrong or sign-inverted relative to literature, and the three code paths would give different frequencies for the same parameter set. I did not run the code (jax not installed); the claim is algebraic and should be re-derived by the physics lens.
findings.recommendation: SRS v2 must write out the I^r (and III^r/III^l) matrix elements explicitly for A- and S-reduction (diagonal and Delta-K=+-2, +-4) and add acceptance test V-HAM-001: 'For a published parameter set with nonzero quartic (and sextic) constants (e.g. H2CO or SO2 ground state, or propylene oxide), eigenvalue differences SHALL agree with SPFIT/SPCAT output to <= 1 kHz for J <= 20'. Require exactly ONE Hamiltonian builder in the package; delete the others.
findings.verifier_note: Algebra confirmed: jax_builder uses delta_xy = 0.25*(X_eff-Y_eff) (l.586) with no further 1/2, so l.661-665 (not 656-660) doubles both delta_J and delta_K; ml_engine l.412-416 doubles delta_K; jax_driver l.128-132 (not 122-126) and its numpy twin l.191-194 use -delta, flipping the sign of (B-C)/4 relative to the delta terms, i.e. fitting -delta_J/-delta_K (textbook element confirmed by arxiv.org/pdf/1308.4076). The claim 'no test exercises nonzero delta against an external reference' must be replaced by a stronger verified fact: tests/test_cochem_spycfit_jax_driver.py:20-50 labels H2O constants/lines 'authentic literature', yet all six fixture frequencies reproduce the sign-flipped jax_driver model to 0.000 MHz while the real 1_10-1_01 and 1_11-0_00 lines are 556936.0 and 1113343.0 MHz (fixture 557194.310 and 1113080.950; textbook convention gives 556953.9/1113321.3), so the fixture was back-computed from the buggy code; additional rigid-rotor builders exist in autofit_engine.py:377 and boltzmann_synthesizer.py, strengthening the 'exactly one builder' recommendation.

findings.evidence: l.55 "pushes immutable, serialized JSON/HDF5 payloads across the boundary into an ephemeral, read-only ingestion vault"; l.1702 "The Host Warden dynamically assigns the TORQ job to available high-performance compute nodes." Repo-wide grep (both SpycFit trees, BASE, TORQ src): job_board 0, Warden 0, Genesis 0 (src), cochem_spyc_schema 0, v4.2.0 0, cochem.spycfit 0; TORQ src contains 0 occurrences of 'spycfit'.

findings.anchor: SRS l.60 (dup l.129) vs l.1455, l.1521 (dup l.1540, l.1606); .gitignore l.26-29; ingest.py l.17
findings.claim: 'Stateless ... zero persistent state' is incompatible with an interactive multi-session assignment workflow, and the SRS never says where session state lives; the code has four ad hoc state stores.
findings.evidence: l.60: "immediately flushes its physical memory. It holds zero persistent state regarding the origin of the data." vs l.1521: "appended to a JSON-serialized artifact exclusion manifest, ensuring reproducibility across sessions." Code: spectra_fit.zarr (ingest.py l.17), spycfit_telemetry.json and fit_provenance.json (.gitignore l.27-28), core_engine/cochem_spycfit_state.py, LevelDB cache (SRS l.207).
findings.why_it_matters: Assignment of a dense CP-FTMW spectrum is a multi-hour, resumable human workflow. Without one defined session artifact the fix agent cannot implement save/resume, reproducibility, provenance, or the HITL state machine, and will keep inventing stores.
findings.recommendation: Define SPYC-SESSION-001: a single versioned FitSession artifact (HDF5 or JSON+arrays) under the BASE artifact root holding: bundle reference+SHA-256, experimental data reference+SHA-256, assignments with status (PROPOSED/APPROVED/REJECTED/GHOST/MANUAL), weights/exclusion windows, parameter vector with fixed flags, reduction and representation, fit results (covariance, rms, N, M), SPFIT run references, append-only event log. Kernel memory is a cache of this file; one writer; delete the stateless clause.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at l.60/129, l.1521/1606 and l.1455/1540 are exact and the four code stores are real, but the anchor 'ingest.py l.17' does not exist: the line is src/cochem_spycfit/intake/cochem_spycfit_ingest.py l.17 ('persists the state matrix to spectra_fit.zarr'; store name at core_engine/cochem_fit_registry_manager.py l.60), with fit_provenance.json written by interfaces/cochem_vibspyc_snap.py l.398/898, spycfit_telemetry.json by serialization/cochem_spcat_bridge.py l.1232, and FitState/CommitManager in core_engine/cochem_spycfit_state.py; LevelDB exists only in SRS l.207 (no plyvel/leveldb in code). Add to the recommendation that BASE already carries a duplicate 'DAG FitState' Pydantic schema (CoChem-BASE/src/cochem_base/cochem_spycfit_ml_schema.py), so SPYC-SESSION-001 must name a single owner and retire the other.

findings.anchor: SRS l.70 (dup l.139); TORQ SRS l.332; pyproject.toml l.7
findings.claim: The version gate is defined on the application's git tag, whereas TORQ specifies a versioned bundle schema agreed through a consumer contract test; TORQ also does not 'push' anything.
findings.evidence: l.70: "TORQ is programmed to only push payloads to SpycFit instances matching a specific, hardcoded semantic version (e.g., `v4.2.0`). If a Git tag mismatch occurs during deployment, the boundary refuses the connection." TORQ-EXP-004 l.332: "SpycFit export SHALL use a versioned schema agreed through a consumer contract test." pyproject.toml l.7: version = "0.1.0".
findings.why_it_matters: Coupling interoperability to an app release tag breaks on every release and is not what the producer implements; the producer writes a bundle file, nothing connects or refuses.
findings.recommendation: SPYC-IF-002: bundle /meta carries schema_version (semver); SpycFit declares the supported major version(s); mismatch raises an explicit CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED-class error naming both versions; the SpycFit app version is recorded in provenance only.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.70 (dup l.139) quote is exact; TORQ-EXP-004 at TORQ SRS l.332 reads verbatim 'SpycFit export SHALL use a versioned schema agreed through a consumer contract test'; pyproject.toml l.7 is version = "0.1.0". TORQ's §3 flowchart (l.97) ends at 'Artifact store and immutable manifests --> SPCAT inputs / SpycFit bundle / report', i.e. a file export with no push, connection or refusal, and CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED is a real TORQ error class (TORQ SRS l.388), so the SPYC-IF-002 recommendation is consistent with the producer.

findings.anchor: SRS l.447-453 (draft l.369-375), l.60; TORQ SRS l.324; Method Matrix l.3422, l.3444
findings.claim: Pickett file roles are wrong and incomplete: the .int file (signed dipoles, temperature, partition function) is never mentioned anywhere in the SRS, .var is dropped in the final chapter, and SPFIT inputs/outputs are conflated.
findings.evidence: l.447: "mandated to flawlessly process the holy trinity of Pickett extensions" (.lin/.cat/.par). l.60: "writes the final output constants (.fit / .par files)". SRS grep '\.int\b' = 0 hits. TORQ-EXP-002 l.324: "Distinguish SPCAT prediction inputs (parameter `.var`/supported parameter input and intensity `.int`) from generated `.cat`, SPFIT observed transition `.lin`, fitted parameter `.var`". Method Matrix l.3422: "It is a `.par` + `.int` pair that runs unmodified through SPCAT".
findings.why_it_matters: The ecosystem's declared deliverable is a .par+.int pair; a consumer that cannot write an .int cannot produce a catalog, and 'never manufacture observed lines' (TORQ-EXP-002) requires the .lin role to be strictly observed/APPROVED only.
findings.recommendation: Replace the table with the six-file role table: .par (SPFIT parameter input, rewritten by SPFIT), .lin (observed assigned lines; written by SpycFit only from APPROVED assignments), .fit (SPFIT report), .var (SPFIT output / SPCAT parameter input), .int (SPCAT intensity input: signed mu, T, Q, QNFMT; written from bundle dipoles + user T_rot), .cat (SPCAT output read for predictions); .egy/.str optional. Mandate pyckett-compatible readers/writers and the Kisiel CRIB traps (sign of quartic constants, spin rounding, parameter codes).
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified verbatim (SRS l.447 'holy trinity', l.60 '(.fit / .par files)', zero hits for '.int' in the SRS, draft l.375 '.var' dropped to '.par' at final l.453; TORQ-EXP-002 at l.324; Method Matrix l.3422 and l.3444 give exactly the six-file roles recommended). One correction to the recommendation: QNFMT is not an .int field — the .int option line is FLAGS TAG QROT FBGN FEND STR0 STR1 FQLIM TEMP MAXV followed by IDIP/DIPOLE lines (CDMS, https://cdms.astro.uni-koeln.de/classic/spcat-considerations), and QNFMT is a .cat output code derived from the .par/.var spin and vibrational settings; remove 'QNFMT' from the .int row. Severity stays MAJOR.

findings.anchor: SRS l.1082-1084 (dup l.1157-1159), l.1455 (dup l.1540); BASE manual l.789-790; Method Matrix l.3632
findings.claim: Three incompatible fitter architectures coexist: an in-process JAX LM fitter that replaces SPFIT (Ch7), 'SPFIT/SPCAT or PGOPHER backend wrappers' (Ch9), and the BASE manual's 'SpycFit does not implement its own rotational diagonalization' PGOPHER-only design; the governing science document says JAX is not to replace SPFIT.
findings.evidence: l.1084: "representing the entire forward model ... as a sequence of pure, differentiable JAX primitives"; l.1455: "the underlying numerical fitting engine (e.g., SPFIT/SPCAT or PGOPHER backend wrappers)"; manual l.789: "`SpycFit` does not implement its own rotational diagonalization routine. Instead, it securely interfaces with the industry-standard PGOPHER executable."; Method Matrix l.3632: "JAX and the GPU are retained for **DVR Hamiltonian diagonalisation and search-space pruning** ... and are **not** used to replace SPFIT."
findings.why_it_matters: The agent must know which fit is the fit-of-record that reviewers and the Method Matrix trust. Building a bespoke LM as the only fitter contradicts the PI's governing document and loses SPFIT's conventions and community verifiability.
findings.recommendation: SPYC-FIT-001: in-process forward model (Watson A/S + chi + effective internal rotation) for prediction, assignment, sensitivity and interactive what-if; SPYC-FIT-002: pinned SPFIT/SPCAT (via pyckett, subprocess) is the fit-of-record and the export path; SPYC-FIT-003: spectrum-equivalence test - in-process predictions agree with SPCAT .cat for the reference set within a stated tolerance (e.g. <=1 kHz) before any in-process result is shown; PGOPHER is an export target only (user-supplied spin weights). Remove Ch2's L-BFGS mention and Ch7's framing of replacing 'legacy' routines; update BASE manual Ch5.
findings.verifier_note: All four quotes verified verbatim (SRS l.1084, l.1455; BASE manual l.789; Method Matrix l.3632 'not used to replace SPFIT'), and the SRS actually holds four stances, since Ch5 l.599 calls SPFIT/SPCAT 'the non-linear least-squares fitting loop' and Ch6 l.1047 speaks of 'SPCAT/SPFIT emulators'. The L-BFGS mention is at l.187/272 and pyckett is the tooling the Method Matrix names at l.3446, so the recommendation is grounded. Side check item: l.1082's claim that legacy fitters use finite-difference gradients mischaracterizes SPFIT (eigenvector-based analytic derivatives, Pickett 1991, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 148, 371) — paper text was not retrievable online during verification, so quote-check before citing.

findings.anchor: SRS l.1668-1694 (dup l.1748-1774); TORQ SRS l.17, l.25, l.108; CoChem-TORQ/AGENTS.md
findings.claim: The SpycFit SRS prescribes TORQ and TOPOS internals (conformer search engines, a level-of-theory escalation ladder) and makes them fully autonomous, contradicting TORQ's recipe registry, decision register and the ecosystem's human-approval model.
findings.evidence: l.1674: "TORQ initiates a broader conformational search. The algorithm typically shifts from a stochastic conformer generator (e.g., crest/GFN2-xTB) to an exhaustive systematic dihedral sweep"; l.1687-1690: "Base Level: B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVP ... Escalation 3 (Golden Standard): CCSD(T)(F12*)"; l.1698: "operates completely autonomously". TORQ SRS l.25: "TOPOS owns global conformer discovery"; Planner row l.108: "No silent physical substitution"; AGENTS.md: "Do not substitute another electronic method for exact revDSD".
findings.why_it_matters: A SpycFit agent implementing §10.4 would be writing TORQ/TOPOS behaviour into the wrong repository, in direct conflict with TORQ's accepted decisions D01-D12, and would remove the human approval step TORQ-UI-001 requires before any new plan runs.
findings.recommendation: Keep the Refinement Request File strictly as an advisory output artifact (diagnostics + suggested request, schema versioned) handed to BASE via a cochem.module-handoff/1-style manifest; delete every sentence describing what TORQ does in response; state that a human approves any resulting TORQ plan. Replace the 5% automatic 'conformer rejected' rule with a flagged diagnostic consistent with Method Matrix Product A/B/C accuracy classes.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified at SRS l.1674, l.1687-1690 and l.1698 (the last sits in §10.5, just past the stated range, but is cited explicitly); TORQ SRS l.25 'TOPOS owns global conformer discovery', Planner row l.108, AGENTS.md l.10-11, decisions D01–D12 at l.19, and TORQ-UI-001 l.401 'approve plan' all check out, and the automatic rejection is at l.1650-1652 (ΔB > 0.05 → 'the structural configuration is rejected'). Additional conflict supporting the finding: SRS l.1674 names crest/GFN2-xTB as the generator while Method Matrix l.2482 rules 'Keep GOAT as the primary engine and add CREST as a second, independent search'.

findings.anchor: SRS l.1696-1702 (dup l.1776-1782); TORQ SRS l.102 (TORQ-ARC-002), l.350 (TORQ-OPS-001)
findings.claim: SpycFit is specified to write directly into another module's SQLite task database via a daemon, violating the single-authority rule, the TORQ state vocabulary, and the SRS's own diode.
findings.evidence: l.1700: "SpycFit transitions the current task state in the SQLite `job_board` from `FITTING_IN_PROGRESS` to `BLOCKED_AWAITING_THEORY`." l.1701: "The SpycFit daemon generates the RRF and injects a high-priority `TORQ_REFINEMENT_SWEEP` task into the Kanban queue". TORQ-ARC-002 l.102: "Only one authority commits task state." TORQ-OPS-001 states are draft/validated/needs_review/queued/running/collecting/validating/succeeded/partial/failed/cancelled/blocked.
findings.why_it_matters: Shared-DB writes from a second process are exactly the failure mode TORQ-OPS-002/005 are designed to prevent; the states named do not exist in the owner's state machine.
findings.recommendation: SPYC-EXPORT-00x: SpycFit has no daemon and never writes another module's database; it writes the RRF JSON plus a handoff manifest into its artifact directory; BASE's task service decides routing and owns state.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.1700-1701 verbatim; TORQ-ARC-002 l.102 ('Only one authority commits task state ... not shared multi-node writes to a SQLite file'), TORQ-OPS-001 l.350 state vocabulary (no FITTING_IN_PROGRESS / BLOCKED_AWAITING_THEORY), TORQ-OPS-002 l.367 and TORQ-OPS-005 l.377 all exist, and the SRS's own diode is at l.55. The 'Host Warden' of l.1702 appears nowhere in the BASE or TORQ repositories. The brief already records the Ch1-vs-Ch10 contradiction, but the cross-repo single-authority and state-machine violations are new, so this is not a duplicate.

findings.claim: Chapter 8 specifies a HITRAN/ExoMol absorbance-synthesis engine for 10,000 cm^-1 grids on 'edge devices', under a module namespace that matches neither package tree; none of it is part of a CP-FTMW assignment product.
findings.evidence: l.1254: "synthesis of theoretical absorbance spectra from foundational line-list databases (e.g., HITRAN, EXOMOL)"; l.1258: "deployability across diverse hardware environments-including edge devices"; l.1343: "**Module:** `cochem.spycfit.convolution`" (both trees are cochem_spycfit); l.1346: "must trigger the `trigger_diagnostic_audit` pipeline".
findings.why_it_matters: At 2-22 GHz, T_rot 1-2 K in a jet there is no pressure broadening and no wide grid; the only convolution needed is a stick spectrum to an instrument/Doppler lineshape for display. A 512 MB VRAM CI mandate would send the agent building GPU profiling for a non-problem.
findings.recommendation: Delete Ch8. Move one requirement into the UI chapter: 'stick spectrum -> Gaussian/Voigt instrument lineshape (FWHM in kHz, user-set), evaluated only over the visible window, CPU.' Remove the cochem.spycfit.* namespace.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes exact at l.1254 (HITRAN/EXOMOL absorbance synthesis), l.1258 (edge devices), l.1301-1305 ('must never exceed 512 Megabytes of peak VRAM ... enforced via continuous integration memory-profiling hooks'), l.1343 '`cochem.spycfit.convolution`' and l.1346, with duplicates at l.1352-1356/1399-1403/1441-1444; no cochem/spycfit directory exists in either tree. Method Matrix §2 (l.244) scopes the product to jet-cooled 2-22 GHz CP-FTMW, never mentions HITRAN/ExoMol synthesis (HITRAN appears only as a PGOPHER-readable format, l.3446), and TORQ-EXP-003 l.328 notes 'Thermal equilibrium conformer populations are not assured in a supersonic jet', so 296 K multi-temperature wide-grid absorbance with pressure broadening is out of scope; the stick-to-instrument-lineshape recommendation is the correct CP-FTMW display need.

findings.anchor: SRS l.173-175, l.207, l.243 (dup l.258-260, l.292, l.328); requirements.txt l.3; pyproject.toml l.13; TORQ SRS l.100; Method Matrix l.900
findings.claim: The GPU-first 'Hardware Gatekeeper / Spectral Registry' architecture (orchestrator interception, LevelDB AOT cache, silent CPU fallback, hard cupy-cuda12x dependency) is unmotivated for an I/O-bound fitting product and breaks the ecosystem's import and deployment rules.
findings.evidence: l.173: "It sits directly beneath the pipeline orchestrator, intercepting all physical tensor operations"; l.207: "serialized and written to a distributed LevelDB cache on the local disk"; l.243: "without the pipeline orchestrator ever being aware of the hardware swap"; pyproject l.13: "cupy-cuda12x" (never imported). TORQ-ARC-001 l.100: "Domain/numerical modules SHALL not require a running notebook, network, scheduler, proprietary binary, or GPU simply to import." Method Matrix l.900: "Anything input/output-bound - SPFIT/SPCAT fitting ... - gets nothing."
findings.why_it_matters: Students in Codespaces have no CUDA; a hard cupy dependency makes the package uninstallable there, and 'orchestrator never aware' hidden fallbacks contradict TORQ-GOV-001 truthful status. JAX also has no LevelDB or simultaneous dual-target AOT facility (verify against jax persistent compilation cache docs).
findings.recommendation: CPU-first numpy/scipy (optionally JAX-CPU) default; GPU only as a [gpu] extra with a measured benefit; delete Gatekeeper, Spectral Registry, LevelDB and dual-AOT text; if JAX is kept, specify jax's own persistent compilation cache directory under the scratch root; all device/precision failures are explicit errors.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes exact at SRS l.173, l.207, l.243 and additionally l.292 ('Dual-Target AOT Serialization ... Both executables are written to a distributed LevelDB cache on the local disk', self-contradictory); pyproject l.13 and requirements.txt l.3 pin cupy-cuda12x while no file imports cupy and the SRS never mentions cupy; TORQ-ARC-001 l.100 and TORQ-GOV-001 l.15 quotes verified. Method Matrix l.900 quote is exact ('Anything input/output-bound — SPFIT/SPCAT fitting ... gets nothing') and the same paragraph warns that silent CPU fallback 'is a *timing* hazard: always check the log for which module ran where'. JAX's documented persistent cache stores 'copies of compiled programs on disk' in a plain directory (or GCS), keyed by HLO + jaxlib version + XLA flags + device configuration, with no LevelDB and no dual-backend AOT facility (https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/persistent_compilation_cache.html), so the recommendation to use jax_compilation_cache_dir under the scratch root is sound.

findings.anchor: SRS l.403-409 (dup l.481-487), l.580-599 (dup l.676-695); TORQ SRS l.68-76 (TORQ-SCI-004), l.114 (TORQ-ARC-003); Method Matrix l.2199; src/cochem_spycfit/master.py l.19, l.25
findings.claim: SpycFit re-derives TORQ's observables (inertia tensor -> B_e with runtime AME masses, Gaussian VPT2 parsing -> B_0), duplicating TORQ's adapter/analysis layer with different mass tables and constants.
findings.evidence: l.580: "parses the *ab initio* anharmonic output (e.g., parsing the `freq=vpt2` block in Gaussian)"; l.596: "`AbInitioParser` extracts the $3 \times 3$ equilibrium inertia tensor and inverts it". TORQ-SCI-004 l.68: "A geometry alone SHALL yield equilibrium/geometry-derived constants, labeled with its method and stationarity status, never ground-state constants by renaming." master.py: hardcoded CONVERSION_FACTOR_MHZ = 505379.008 and import of MASS_DICT, while BASE provides C_ROT_MHZ_U_ANG2.
findings.why_it_matters: Two implementations of the same derivation with different constants/masses produce inconsistent priors and break TORQ-SCI-002 ('conversions from one versioned constants service'); parsing engine output is the engine adapter's job (TORQ-ARC-003 parse()).
findings.recommendation: SpycFit consumes B_e, B_0 (with delta-B_vib and label), distortion, signed mu, chi, LAM priors from the bundle with provenance; its only inertia mathematics is diagnostic (kappa, inertial defect, planar moments, Kraitchman r_s from fitted constants) using the shared BASE constants service. Delete AbInitioParser, VPT2Interface and PCA-32's runtime AME fetch (isotope masses arrive in /molecules with source/version).
findings.verifier_note: Quotes exact: SRS l.580 ('parsing the `freq=vpt2` block in Gaussian'), l.596 ('`AbInitioParser` extracts the 3x3 equilibrium inertia tensor and inverts it'), l.403-409 PCA-32 runtime-AME nuclear masses, with duplicates at l.481-487/676-695; TORQ-SCI-004 l.68-76, TORQ-ARC-001 l.100, TORQ-ARC-003 l.114 (parse()) and TORQ-EXP-004 l.332-338 ('/observables/<id> value dataset plus unit/frame/source/validation attributes') verified, and TORQ l.287 lists 'Vibration-corrected constants ... A0,B0,C0 with correction provenance' as a TORQ exporter product. src/cochem_spycfit/master.py l.19 imports MASS_DICT and l.25 hardcodes CONVERSION_FACTOR_MHZ = 505379.008 while BASE exposes _physical_constants.C_ROT_MHZ_U_ANG2 (used in src/cochem_geom/eval/metrics.py l.92). One caveat for the recommendation: TORQ SRS l.296 admits alpha/vibration-corrected constants 'remain unimplemented or independently unqualified', so SRS v2 should also state that SpycFit uses a labeled B_e prior with a delta-B_vib uncertainty when the bundle lacks B_0, never relabeling it (per TORQ-SCI-004), rather than parsing proprietary Gaussian output itself.

findings.anchor: SRS l.947-953, l.1035-1047; BASE .docs L2-T1.3 l.247-249; TORQ SRS l.56; Method Matrix l.3372
findings.claim: Chapter 6 duplicates BASE's Eckart/Kabsch aligner (including parsing raw Gaussian/CFOUR Cartesians) and omits the binding multi-basin gate; the one piece SpycFit legitimately needs - relabeling a/b/c for isotopologues and permuting constants/dipoles/chi - is buried.
findings.evidence: l.1039: "`GeometryParser` | Parsed X^(p), X^(s), and atomic masses W | Standardize raw Cartesian inputs from quantum chemistry backends (Gaussian/CFOUR)." .docs l.249: "*Target Module:* `src/cochem_base/intake/cochem_molsym_eckart_aligner.py`". Method Matrix l.3372: "Eckart alignment is applied within one symmetry-distinct basin or declared `n.a.`".
findings.why_it_matters: For tunnelling complexes (the product's class) single-reference Eckart alignment across equivalent minima is forbidden by the governing document; re-implementing alignment in the fitter invites exactly that silent error and diverges from the frame TORQ/BASE already recorded.
findings.recommendation: Consume frame attributes from the bundle (TORQ-SCI-002 l.56: 'Every tensor has axis order, shape, units, frame (orientation and origin) and atom order'). Keep only an AxisMapper requirement: parent<->isotopologue a/b/c permutation applied to constants, mu and chi with representation (I^r/III^l) tracked, plus an explicit n.a. gate when more than one permutationally equivalent basin is populated.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.1039 (GeometryParser 'Standardize raw Cartesian inputs from quantum chemistry backends (Gaussian/CFOUR)') and l.1043-1044 (KabschSVD, AxisMapper) duplicate a module that already exists at CoChem-BASE/src/cochem_base/intake/cochem_molsym_eckart_aligner.py (.docs l.247-249), and Gaussian is not even an ecosystem backend. Method Matrix l.3372 and the binding gate at l.764 ('Single-reference Eckart alignment must not be applied silently across equivalent minima') have no counterpart anywhere in SRS Ch6 l.943-1077 (grep for basin/tunnel/n.a. returns nothing). One caveat for the synthesizer: the Method Matrix gate is phrased for trajectory/ensemble averaging, so its application to isotopologue relabelling is an extension, but a sound one for complexes where substitution at one of n equivalent sites breaks the permutational equivalence.

findings.claim: The experimental-data ingress path is undefined: the SRS ingests only already-assigned .lin lines and theoretical priors, says data arrives 'exclusively from TORQ', yet the UI plots an experimental spectrum O(nu) whose format, units, resolution, uncertainty model and provenance are specified nowhere.
findings.evidence: l.353: "Raw or pre-processed microwave, millimeter-wave, or terahertz spectral line transitions, intrinsically bound to assigned quantum numbers." l.53: "receiving data exclusively from TORQ." l.1462: "plots the experimentally acquired spectrum, $O(\nu)$, overlaid with the theoretical predicted spectrum, $C(\nu)$."
findings.why_it_matters: An assignment tool's primary input is an unassigned CP-FTMW spectrum or peak list; without an ingress requirement the agent cannot build the core workflow, and the diode clause forbids the user from supplying it.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-EXP-001..004: accept (a) two-column spectrum (frequency MHz, intensity; declared instrument, resolution, calibration), (b) peak list (frequency, uncertainty, intensity), (c) existing .lin; record SHA-256, instrument, T_rot and frequency-calibration provenance [M]; peak-picking with user threshold and uncertainty assignment; all stored in the FitSession.
findings.verifier_note: All three quotes are verbatim (l.53, l.353/431, l.1462/1547); the only experimental input the SRS defines is the assigned .lin file (l.373/451) and a grep for peak-pick, calibration, resolution, unassigned or two-column returns nothing. The gap is tighter than the finding states: TORQ-EXP-002 (TORQ SRS l.324) says 'Never manufacture observed lines from predicted transitions', so the 'exclusively from TORQ' diode clause leaves no legitimate source at all for the O(nu) that Ch9 plots and masks (l.1509-1528).

SPFIT/SPCAT (and optional PGOPHER) provisioned per host through BASE's Stage-0 registry; each target has its own acceptance evidence (clean install, consumer contract test, SPCAT round-trip, UI journey on a reference complex).
findings.verifier_note: All quotes verified: SRS l.47/l.116 hardware-firewalled subnet, l.1258/l.1356 'edge devices and parallelized cluster nodes' with a 512 MB VRAM mandate, l.1453/l.1538 Voila web frontend; BASE README l.63-72 route table (l.72 Codespaces interface row), l.197 'TOPOS and TORQ domain development belongs to their respective repositories'; TORQ-DEP-003 at TORQ SRS l.417. findings.claim: The nine 'Improvements' sections are quota-driven generator output whose citations do not survive spot-checking: of 88 Improver lines, 66 purport a concrete suggestion; across ~45 citations checked, 7 cite works that do not exist, 8 have no title and cannot be verified, 9 cite real works for claims they do not make, >=11 cite real papers from unrelated domains (ImageNet SGD, VAEs, ICS firewalls), and >=8 contradict the SRS body; only ~9 items are actionable, in scope and non-contradictory.
findings.evidence: l.939: "[SPOOFING RISK DETECTED] The numeric quota of exactly 20 distinct, highly specific, and actionable improvement suggestions ... cannot be genuinely met without fabricating or stretching physical chemistry parameters." l.148 (x18): "Standard processing applied. Rationale: Procedural step. Citation: Internal protocol."
findings.why_it_matters: A fix/replace agent reading these lists as requirements would implement EWC, VAE regularization, optical data diodes, hardcoded IUPAC masses and mock-based CI in a least-squares microwave fitter, several of which directly contradict the body (PCA-32, zero-mock mandate, jacrev, statelessness). The Ch5 fallback line is the only honest output and proves the 20-item quota caused fabrication in Ch6/7/10. Chapter 8 has no Improvements section at all, confirming inconsistency of the generator.
findings.recommendation: Delete every '💡 Chapter N Improvements (AI Researched)' section from the SRS. Move the ~9 salvageable items (Ch3 #4; Ch6 #9 Demaison, #11 Kraitchman, #16 Oka inertial defect, #18 Pickett state labeling; Ch7 #9 covariance/FIM, #10 Transtrum, #11 Tikhonov; Ch10 #7 feedback schema, conditional) to an appendix titled 'Backlog: unverified suggestions, NOT requirements' with corrected citations (DOI/URL). Promote five to numbered requirements with a verification method: (1) physical-invariant pre-flight gate (A>=B>=C, I_c <= I_a+I_b, sigma>0); (2) inertial-defect/planarity bounds check with the Method Matrix sign rule; (3) deterministic K_a,K_c state labeling by eigenvector overlap with documented tie-break; (4) parameter standard errors and correlation matrix from chi2_r*(J^T W J)^-1 in the output; (5) Kraitchman r_s / r_m structure output if isotopologues are in scope. Add a document rule: no citation without DOI/URL and a one-line statement of what it supports.
findings.verifier_note: grep confirms 88 '**Improver:**' lines, nine Improvements headers (l.145/341/503/701/938/1054/1226/1619/1785) with none for Chapter 8, and the quotes at l.146, l.165 and l.939 are verbatim; web searches return no record of 'Zeng et al., End-to-End Differentiable Molecular Spectroscopy, JCP 2023' nor of 'Costes et al. 2006 STRFIT' (STRFIT is Kisiel's program), supporting the fabrication count. One evidence nit: the filler line 'Standard processing applied...' occurs 17 times (l.148-164), not 18. MAJOR is right, not BLOCKER: the items are unchecked suggestion checkboxes, not SHALL requirements, but several contradict the body (l.1064 hardcoded masses vs l.395 'no static mass floats'; l.1801 mock CI vs zero-mock mandate).

findings.evidence: l.391: "the SpycFit architecture strictly enforces the **Mendeleev Dynamic Atomic Mass Mandate (PCA-32)**." l.395: "no static mass floats may exist within the SpycFit computational graph. Instead, the ingestion engine must query the central Mendeleev Isotope Registry"
findings.why_it_matters: grep of ../CoChem-BASE shows PCA-32 only in swarm audit/ratification reports ('Council Rulings PCA-01, PCA-02, ... PCA-32'); no definition anywhere. src/cochem_spycfit/master.py:193-197 and init.py:146-148 contain literal masses ('1H': 1.007825, '12C': 12.000000, ...) at 1e-6 u, i.e. the code already does the opposite of the SRS and instead follows the contradictory Ch6 Improver (l.1064, 'Hardcode IUPAC Mass Constants'). findings.claim: The body mandates reverse-mode `jacrev` while admitting forward mode is optimal for N_obs >> M, then invents an uncited 'Lorentzian broadening regularization' of gradients to patch the eigh-VJP degeneracy NaNs that this choice causes; the Ch10 Improver cites Baydin et al. (2018) to prescribe forward mode instead. The standard, exact solution (SPFIT's Hellmann-Feynman Jacobian from eigenvectors) is already written at l.1194 but not adopted.
findings.evidence: l.1189: "While forward-mode autodiff (`jacfwd`) is traditionally optimal when $N_{obs} \gg M$, the architecture specifically leverages `jacrev` combined with JAX's `vmap`. Reverse-mode autodiff pulls gradients backwards from each scalar frequency output, requiring $N_{obs}$ backward passes." l.1196: "the custom VJP applies a Lorentzian broadening regularization scheme"
findings.why_it_matters: Baydin, Pearlmutter, Radul & Siskind, JMLR 18(153) (2018) §3 is correctly summarized by the Improver: with N_obs ~ 10^2-10^3 transitions and M ~ 10-30 parameters, forward mode (M JVPs) is cheaper than reverse (N_obs VJPs). More importantly, transition frequencies need only eigenvalue derivatives, dE_n/dtheta_j = <psi_n|dH/dtheta_j|psi_n> (Hellmann-Feynman; the SRS states this at l.1194), which contains no 1/(E_m - E_n) terms; the NaN problem arises only from differentiating eigenvectors through eigh. 'Lorentzian broadening' of a gradient is not a published technique and alters the model's derivatives, biasing the LM step. Pickett, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 148, 371 (1991) (SPFIT) computes exactly the H-F Jacobian. The body and its own Improvements list give the implementing agent opposite instructions.
findings.recommendation: Requirement: 'J_ij = <psi_i'|dH/dtheta_j|psi_i'> - <psi_i''|dH/dtheta_j|psi_i''> SHALL be computed from eigh eigenvectors and the operator matrices dH/dtheta_j (analytic for parameters linear in H, e.g. A,B,C,Delta_J...; jax.jacfwd permitted for non-linear parameters such as rho, F). Exactly degenerate levels SHALL be handled by diagonalizing dH/dtheta_j in the degenerate subspace (degenerate perturbation theory), not by regularization. J SHALL be validated against central finite differences to 1e-6 relative in CI.' Delete the custom-VJP/Lorentzian paragraph and the jacrev mandate.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at l.1189, 1196 and 1796 are verbatim, and the technical core is confirmed by execution: with jax 0.11.2 (x64) an eigenvalue-only function through jnp.linalg.eigh at an exactly degenerate pair returns finite Jacobians under BOTH jacfwd and jacrev ([[1,0],[2,0],[2,0]]) and a finite transition-frequency gradient, whereas an eigenvector-dependent output returns NaN -- so the NaN premise behind the custom VJP (l.1196) does not apply to frequency fits, and the finite values at degeneracy were basis-dependent (0,0 instead of the correct +/-1 for the in-subspace coupling), which vindicates the recommendation to use degenerate perturbation theory rather than regularization. One sub-claim must be dropped: 'Lorentzian broadening' of eigh gradients IS a published technique -- Liao, Liu, Wang & Xiang, Phys. Rev. X 9, 031041 (2019), h(t) = (t^2 + eps)/t, implemented in Grimme-lab tad-mctc eighb and the JAX 'eigh' package, whose docs concede it 'will induce small errors in the returned gradients' -- so the argument should be 'unnecessary for eigenvalue-only Jacobians and biasing', not 'unpublished'. The jacrev-vs-forward-mode contradiction overlaps an established fact in the brief, but the Hellmann-Feynman/Pickett-1991 prescription is new and MAJOR is appropriate for the fitter's core Jacobian.

findings.claim: Nine of the 20 Ch10 Improvers import neural-network training techniques into a 10-30-parameter least-squares fitter that has no network, weights, latent space or SGD loop (EWC l.1790, Kirkpatrick PNAS 2017; curriculum learning l.1797, Bengio ICML 2009; VAE latent regularization l.1798, Kingma & Welling 2014; gradient clipping l.1801, Pascanu 2013; multi-task loss weighting l.1794, Kendall CVPR 2018; large-minibatch SGD l.1789, Goyal arXiv:1706.02677; Behler-Parrinello surrogates l.1800; 'differentiable VPT2 via JAX MD' l.1787; ML force fields l.1788, Unke Chem. Rev. 2021); 'Mock Feedback CI/CD' (l.1802) contradicts the zero-mock mandate; 'Optical Data Diode' (l.1786, Stouffer et al. SP 800-82r2 - real ICS guidance, correct authors) contradicts §10.5 where SpycFit writes into TORQ's SQLite job_board; 'Martin, Spectrochimica Acta A (2021)' (l.1795) is MISATTRIBUTED (SAA 250, 119164 (2021) is Sarka, Poirier, Szalay & Csaszar); 'Saltzer & Schroeder' stateless Tier III (l.1805) contradicts Ch9 l.1540 and Ch10 l.1780.
findings.evidence: l.1790: "Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) to Prevent Catastrophic Forgetting. Rationale: Anchors weights critical to baseline ab initio data. Citation: Kirkpatrick et al., PNAS (2017)." l.1802: "Mock Feedback CI/CD Integration Testing. ... Citation: Fowler, MartinFowler.com (2006)."
findings.why_it_matters: All nine ML papers are real and were verified, but none applies: 'catastrophic forgetting' presupposes a trained network; a Levenberg-Marquardt fit of A, B, C, Delta_J... has nothing to consolidate, no curriculum, no latent manifold, and no exploding recurrent gradients. .github/copilot-instructions.md mandates 'No Synthetic Benchmarking or Mocking' and the anti-spoof linter rejects the token 'mock', so l.1802 is unimplementable under the project's own rules. A hardware data diode cannot carry the bidirectional Kanban writes of §10.5 (l.1780-1782), so the Improver and the body cannot both be true. None of these items belongs in a rotational-spectroscopy SRS.
findings.recommendation: DELETE all 20 items. BACKLOG only #7 (versioned JSON schema for any SpycFit->TORQ feedback; Pezoa et al., WWW 2016 is a fine reference) conditional on the ecosystem first resolving whether SpycFit may emit feedback at all (Ch1 diode vs Ch10 RRF/Kanban). Move #18 (Barone, J. Chem. Phys. 122, 014108 (2005), VPT2) to the TORQ SRS, where VPT2 belongs. Resolve the statelessness contradiction in the body rather than by an Improver.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at l.1790 and l.1802 are verbatim and all 20 items sit at l.1786-1805 as numbered. Crossref doi:10.1016/j.saa.2020.119164 confirms Spectrochim. Acta A 250, 119164 (2021) 'On neglecting Coriolis and related couplings...' is Sarka, Poirier, Szalay & Csaszar and no 2021 SAA paper by Martin on Coriolis resonance exists (Martin's resonance test is JCP 103, 2589 (1995) / SAA 53, 1039 (1997)), so l.1795 is misattributed; copilot-instructions.md l.34 ('No Synthetic Benchmarking or Mocking') and ci_tools/anti_spoof_linter.py l.31-38 (bans token 'mock') make l.1802 unimplementable. The diode/Kanban (SRS l.55/124 vs l.1780 'SpycFit transitions the current task state in the SQLite job_board') and stateless/kernel-state (l.1805 vs l.1540 'The Voila kernel maintains the persistent state') contradictions are real; the mock item overlaps a brief-established fact but the out-of-domain ML analysis and misattribution are new, and MAJOR is correct for material internal contradictions.

findings.claim: The only acceptance benchmark named in the SRS, 'the established millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide', is real (Mesko, Zou, Carroll & Widicus Weaver, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 335, 49 (2017), 70 GHz-1 THz, SPFIT/XIAM, V3 = 893 cm-1) but is mentioned only in passing with no dataset, tolerance or pass criterion, and it is a 10-atom monomer at mm-wave rather than a 5-10-atom complex at 2-22 GHz as scoped by Method Matrix §2.
findings.evidence: l.137: "successful passage through a sterile CI/CD pipeline that rigorously tests the non-linear optimizer against known spectral benchmarks (e.g., the established millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide)."
findings.why_it_matters: VERIFIED existence (doi:10.1016/j.jms.2017.02.003; cm-wave data also in Swalen & Herschbach, J. Chem. Phys. 27, 100 (1957) and Creswell & Schwendeman, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 64, 295 (1977)). The CI workflow runs no tests (brief), so the sentence is currently false. Without a defined benchmark catalogue the fix/replace agent has no objective pass criterion, and propylene oxide alone exercises neither hyperfine structure, nor weakly bound complex tunnelling, nor the 2-22 GHz CP-FTMW regime.
findings.recommendation: Add an acceptance-benchmark section with IDs and tolerances, e.g. V-BM-01: propylene oxide ground-state .lin from Mesko et al. 2017 (and cm-wave lines) -> recovered A, B, C and quartic constants within 3 sigma of published values, weighted RMS <= 1.0 x quoted uncertainties, A/E splittings reproduced with V3 within 1%; V-BM-02: a 14N-hyperfine case; V-BM-03: a weakly bound complex with tunnelling from the Method Matrix system class; V-BM-04: round-trip against SPFIT/SPCAT on identical .par/.lin with predicted frequencies agreeing to <= 1 kHz. Make these the CI gate referenced in §1.5.
findings.verifier_note: Quote is verbatim at both l.68 and l.137 (draft and final Ch1) and propylene oxide appears nowhere else in the SRS. Mesko, Zou, Carroll & Widicus Weaver, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 335, 49 (2017), 70 GHz-1 THz, V3 = 893 cm-1, and Swalen & Herschbach 1957 (microwave, <=40 GHz) are confirmed by web search; .github/workflows/cochem_spycfit_ci.yml contains only a `find` for *.h5/*.lin/*.fit/*.parquet/*.lock, so the 'rigorously tests ... against known spectral benchmarks' sentence is currently false; Method Matrix §2.1 scopes 5-10-atom complexes at 2-22 GHz and 1-2 K, so a 10-atom monomer at mm-wave is a valid but insufficient benchmark. Creswell & Schwendeman 1977 could not be located and should be checked before citing, but it is peripheral to the finding; the recommended V-BM catalogue is sound (published V3 values span 892.7-898.7 cm-1, so a 1 % tolerance is realistic).

findings.anchor: SRS 0 hits for 'Wang'/'parity block'; l.1187, l.1196; code src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_jax_builder.py l.10, 196, 453-487, 962; cochem_autofit_engine.py l.8
findings.claim: The SRS never requires the standard Wang (E+, E−, O+, O−) symmetry factorisation of H(J), which is the mechanism that (a) yields the K_a/K_c parity labels NUM-01 says are missing, (b) removes the intra-block near-degeneracies that motivate the custom 'degeneracy regularisation' VJP, and (c) gives the dipole-type selection rules; the code implements it unspecified.
findings.evidence: SRS l.1187: 'the difference between two eigenvalues obtained by diagonalizing an effective Hamiltonian matrix H(θ)'; l.1196: 'Spectroscopic Hamiltonians frequently exhibit degeneracies or near-degeneracies (e.g., K-level clustering)'. Code cochem_jax_builder.py l.10: 'Parity sub-block decomposition (Wang symmetrized basis: E+, E-, O+, O-) for 16x faster diagonalization'.
findings.why_it_matters: Without symmetry blocking, eigenvalues of the full (2J+1) matrix have no parity labels, so (J,K_a,K_c) assignment is ambiguous (NUM-01) and near-degenerate K-doublets appear as 'degeneracies' that the SRS then patches with a non-standard VJP (PHYS-26, NUM-03). SPFIT/PGOPHER block by symmetry as a matter of course; the fix/replace agent needs this stated as a requirement with a reference, not left to a code docstring.
findings.recommendation: Add: 'For each J the rigid+distortion Hamiltonian SHALL be constructed in the Wang basis and diagonalised in the four E±/O± blocks (Gordy & Cook Ch. 7, Table 7.5); eigenvalues within a block SHALL be labelled by energy order, and (K_a,K_c) SHALL be assigned from block symmetry and order (prolate/oblate limit correlation). Acceptance: energies and labels for a reference molecule agree with SPFIT/SPCAT output to <1 kHz for all J≤J_max.' Cross-reference this as the resolution of NUM-01 and the reason the degeneracy VJP of §7.3.1 is unnecessary.
findings.verifier_note: SRS has 0 hits for 'Wang'; the five 'parity' hits (l.799/800/917/918/988) concern torsional A/E selection rules and det(R), not K-parity blocking; l.1187 and l.1196 quotes are exact, and src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_jax_builder.py l.10, l.196 (use_parity_blocks), l.456-487 (build_wang_transformation_matrix) and l.962-964 implement it with no SRS requirement. Physics checks out: near-prolate/oblate K-doublet partners differ in K_c (or K_a) parity and fall in different Wang blocks, so blocking removes the systematic 'K-level clustering' near-degeneracies of l.1196, and because the fit depends on eigenvalues only, the Hellmann-Feynman derivative has no (E_m-E_n)^-1 term (JAX eigh gradients are correct for eigenvalue-only functions: https://lightrun.com/answers/google-jax-eigh-gradients-can-be-wrong), making the Lorentzian-broadened VJP (the pyscfad 'eigh' recipe, https://pypi.org/project/eigh/) unnecessary. Minor nuance for the recommendation: accidental intra-block near-degeneracies remain possible, so state 'Wang blocking plus an eigenvalue-only (Hellmann-Feynman) derivative rule' rather than blocking alone.

findings.claim: Chapter 9 conflates two data models: the fit residual of Ch7 is over the discrete assigned line list (ν_obs,i − ν_calc,i), whereas Ch9's 'residual pane' R(ν)=O(ν)−C(ν) is a continuous intensity difference, and 'ghost peak' masking of a frequency window is said to zero weights w_i in an LM χ² that contains no term for unassigned spectral features.
findings.evidence: l.1562: 'R(ν) = O(ν) − C(ν)'; l.1564: 'This pane is critical for the spectroscopist to identify misassigned quantum numbers'; l.1599-1604: 'highlight arbitrary frequency windows. These selected regions invoke a callback that modifies the diagonal statistical weight matrix W used in the Levenberg-Marquardt fitting routine ... w_i → 0'. Ch7 l.1165: χ² over 'N_obs ... experimental and calculated transition frequencies'.
findings.why_it_matters: The spectroscopist's O−C plot is per assigned line (obs−calc in kHz vs J or frequency), which is what reveals misassignments; a continuous O(ν)−C(ν) is dominated by intensity-model, lineshape and unassigned-species errors and cannot show a 20 kHz frequency residual. A masking action whose effect on the fit is undefined cannot be implemented or tested; the agent would have to invent the link between spectral regions and χ² terms.
findings.recommendation: Define three objects with explicit relations: experimental spectrum O(ν); experimental peak list {ν_k, σ_k, I_k, flags}; assigned line list {(ν_obs,i, σ_i, QN', QN'')} ⊂ peak list. Require two residual views: (1) per-line o−c table/plot in kHz with σ_i error bars and >3σ flags (the fit residual), (2) the overlay O(ν) vs stick/convolved C(ν). Redefine masking as acting on the peak list (exclude peak k from assignment candidates) and on assigned lines (set w_i=0 with reason code), never on frequency windows of O(ν) alone.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at l.1562-1564 and l.1599-1604 are exact; §9.2.1 l.1549 defines C(nu) as a Voigt-convolved intensity spectrum, whereas Ch7 l.1165-1171 and Ch10 l.1718-1722 ('N is the number of assigned transitions') define the residual over the discrete assigned line list, so two incompatible residual objects coexist with no stated relation. Within §9.4.1 the text moves in three consecutive lines from 'arbitrary frequency windows' to 'the corresponding weight ... w_i -> 0' to an 'exclusion zone [nu_min, nu_max]' (l.1599-1604) without defining which chi-square index i a window selects; grep finds no peak-list or per-line o-c object anywhere in Ch9 (only 'local peak-finding' as a backend verb at l.1568 and 'assigned quantum numbers' in a tooltip at l.1577).

findings.chapter: Ch5 §5.5.1 vs Ch7 §7.1-7.3 vs Ch9 §9.3.2 (solver integration gap)
findings.claim: The LAM Hamiltonian is specified with a separate LAPACK (dsyevd/zheevd) CPU solver while Ch7 requires the 'entire forward model' to be differentiable JAX; V3, V6, F and ρ are therefore outside the Jacobian/θ vector of Ch7 and absent from the Ch9 slider set, so the SRS provides no mechanism to fit the barrier it says SpycFit 'extracts'.
findings.evidence: l.909: 'factorized using high-performance LAPACK routines (dsyevd for symmetric real A-state blocks, and zheevd for Hermitian complex E-state blocks)'; l.1159: 'representing the entire forward model—from Hamiltonian matrix construction to eigenvalue extraction and transition frequency calculation—as a sequence of pure, differentiable JAX primitives'; l.1764: 'SpycFit extracts the approximate experimental internal rotation barrier (e.g., V3 or V2)'. Slider table l.1585-1590 lists only A,B,C, quartics, T_rot, widths, dipoles.
findings.why_it_matters: Internal-rotation and tunnelling parameters are the point of the LAM chapter for this product class; if their solver is not in the fitted model there is no path from assigned A/E lines to a fitted V3, and the Ch7/Ch9 machinery silently excludes them. TRACE-06 found exactly this in code (scipy, non-differentiable, σ=0 only); the SRS caused it.
findings.recommendation: State one forward model: θ = {rotational, distortion, hyperfine, LAM (V3,V6,F,ρ or XIAM-set), state offsets}; the LAM Hamiltonian SHALL be built and diagonalised in the same framework as the rigid-rotor part with Hellmann–Feynman derivatives for every θ_k; the UI SHALL expose LAM parameters; alternatively state explicitly that LAM fitting is delegated to XIAM/BELGI via wrappers and SpycFit only ingests their output (then delete §5.5.1).
findings.verifier_note: The gap is real but the LAPACK sentence (l.909/791) is weak evidence, since jnp.linalg.eigh on CPU itself dispatches to LAPACK syevd/heevd and the SRS never says 'separate' or 'non-differentiable'; the decisive contradiction is l.761/879 ('The accurate determination of V3 and V6 is treated as a primary fitting objective within the SpycFit optimization engine') and l.930 ('Pre-computed or fitted [rho_a, rho_b, rho_c]') versus Ch7 l.1162 (theta exemplified only by rotational, distortion and quadrupole constants) and the slider table l.1585-1590 (no LAM parameters). Code corroborates the outcome: src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_jax_builder.py l.873 'evals, evecs = scipy.linalg.eigh(h_coupled)' in the IAM block is non-differentiable. Change: move the primary anchor to l.761/879, l.930, l.1162 and l.1585-1590 and cite the LAPACK sentence only as supporting ambiguity; severity and the one-forward-model-or-delegate-to-XIAM recommendation stand.

findings.chapter: Cross-cutting (Ch7, Ch8, Ch9, Ch2) — missing computational-domain requirement; OLD_PLAN premise
findings.anchor: SRS 0 hits for J_max/E_max/frequency window; OLD_PLAN_architectural_changes l.45; OLD_PLAN_workflow l.7; code cochem_autofit_engine.py l.241
findings.claim: No requirement states the computational domain (J_max, K_a max, energy cut-off, frequency window, catalog temperature) that fixes matrix sizes, catalog completeness and the partition-function sum; the OLD_PLAN's 'J=0 up to J=80 ... enormous matrices' premise is physically wrong for a 1-2 K, 2-22 GHz jet spectrum and is the unexamined origin of the GPU/VRAM/mmap obsession the review criticises.
findings.evidence: OLD_PLAN arch l.45: 'Calculating rotational states from J=0 up to J=80 across multiple vibrational states generates enormous matrices. SpycFit must implement strict memory-mapped file (mmap) reads and JAX host-to-device streaming'. Code autofit l.241: 'j_max: int = Field(default=6, ge=1, le=15, description="Maximum rotational quantum number J")'.
findings.why_it_matters: For B+C ≈ 2-6 GHz at T_rot 1-2 K, populated levels are J ≲ 10 and matrices are ≤ ~11×11 per Wang block; J=80 is a mm-wave/room-temperature regime. Without a stated domain the agent cannot size anything, Q_rot(T) truncation is undefined (PHYS-18), and performance claims (NUM-16) cannot be checked. The review should have used OLD_PLAN l.45 as the root of NUM-06/07/08/09 rather than treating those as independent errors.
findings.recommendation: Add 'Computational domain' requirements: J_max default = smallest J with Boltzmann population < 10⁻⁴ at T_rot (cap 30, user-overridable); E_max and ν window [2,22] GHz default; Q_rot by direct summation to convergence < 10⁻⁶; state that all matrices fit in L2 cache and that GPU is out of scope (ties to NUM-08). Record in the plan that OLD_PLAN §4 is superseded.
findings.verifier_note: SRS has 0 hits for J_max/E_max/2-22 GHz/a numerical T_rot (the only 'frequency windows' are the masking text at l.1514/1599); OLD_PLAN architectural_changes l.45 and workflow l.7 quotes are exact ('J=0 up to J=80 ... enormous matrices ... mmap'), and code defaults j_max=6 (cochem_autofit_engine.py l.241) and J_max=10 (cochem_jax_builder.py l.190) confirm the small-J regime; Method_Matrix.md l.248 fixes the domain at 2-22 GHz and 1-2 K.
