Recommendation must add: before deleting src/cochem_base, either declare `cochem-base` as a versioned dependency in pyproject or remove those four imports; the TORQ-EXP-004 HDF5 contract covers data, not these code imports.

findings.chapter: Ch7 §7.3, §7.3.1 (contradicted by Ch7 and Ch10 improvement lists)
findings.claim: The Jacobian strategy — reverse-mode jacrev through jnp.linalg.eigh plus a custom 'Lorentzian broadening' VJP for degeneracies — is the wrong tool: the Watson Hamiltonian is linear in its parameters, so the exact Jacobian is the Hellmann–Feynman expectation value from eigenvectors already in hand, with no differentiation through the eigensolver and no degeneracy singularity; the SRS also concedes jacfwd is optimal and overrides it, and its own improvement lists (l.1229, l.1796) recommend forward mode.
findings.evidence: l.1189: "While forward-mode autodiff (`jacfwd`) is traditionally optimal when N_obs ≫ M, the architecture specifically leverages `jacrev` combined with JAX's `vmap`. Reverse-mode autodiff pulls gradients backwards from each scalar frequency output, requiring N_obs backward passes." l.1117 (draft): "computes the full Jacobian in a single backward pass" (false).
findings.why_it_matters: H(θ) = Σ_k θ_k O_k for A, B, C, Δ_J … so ∂H/∂θ_k = O_k is a fixed matrix and J_ik = ⟨ψ_u|O_k|ψ_u⟩ − ⟨ψ_l|O_k|ψ_l⟩ costs M matrix–vector products per level after the one eigendecomposition already needed for the forward pass. This is exactly what SPFIT does (Pickett 1991). jacrev needs N_obs VJPs vs jacfwd's M JVPs (N_obs ≈ 100–1000 ≫ M ≈ 10–25), and 'jacrev combined with vmap' is literally how jacrev is implemented, not an optimisation; the code encodes the inverted rule (jacrev when m ≥ n). The degeneracy argument is also misdirected: for eigenvalue-only outputs the eigenvector cotangent is a symbolic zero and the 1/(E_m−E_n) terms are never evaluated (JAX issue reports eigenvalue-only losses differentiate correctly); exact degeneracies within a Wang block do not occur for an asymmetric rotor, and 'Lorentzian broadening' of a VJP biases the gradient rather than fixing anything.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite §7.3: 'J_ik SHALL be computed as ⟨ψ_u|∂H/∂θ_k|ψ_u⟩ − ⟨ψ_l|∂H/∂θ_k|ψ_l⟩ from the eigenvectors of the forward diagonalisation; ∂H/∂θ_k is the analytic operator matrix for parameters entering H linearly and is obtained by jax.jacfwd of the Hamiltonian-builder (matrix-valued, M JVPs) for nonlinear parameters (F, ρ, V3 in the IAM). Differentiating through eigh is prohibited. For an exactly degenerate pair the derivative SHALL be the eigenvalues of ∂H/∂θ projected on the degenerate subspace.' Acceptance: J agrees with central finite differences to 1e-6 relative on the propylene-oxide benchmark. Remove the custom-VJP and Lorentzian-regularisation text and reconcile l.1229/l.1796.
findings.verifier_note: Finding stands and is strengthened by an empirical test (jax 0.11.2, x64): jacrev and jacfwd of eigvalsh on the J=2..15 Watson-type H(θ)=A·Jz²+B·Jx²+C·Jy² produce no NaN and equal the Hellmann-Feynman expectation to 1e-14 even at exact B=C degeneracy, so the SRS l.1196 'catastrophically produce NaN' claim and the Lorentzian custom VJP are unfounded; however at exact degeneracy autodiff returns the basis-dependent ⟨ψ|∂H/∂B|ψ⟩ (9.5, 9.5) instead of the degenerate-PT values (4.5, 14.5), which Wang blocking removes, so the recommendation's degenerate-subspace rule is correct. Code l.327-330 inverted rule (jacrev when m≥n) and l.1117/1189/1229/1796 quotes confirmed (l.1117 is hedged by a parenthetical). Revision to the recommendation: V3 enters the IAM Hamiltonian linearly (V3/2·(1−cos3α)); only F and ρ are nonlinear parameters needing jacfwd of the builder.

findings.claim: The SRS never defines the parameter covariance matrix, parameter standard errors, correlation matrix, weighted RMS, or fit statistics as computed quantities or as required outputs, and gives no convergence criterion, λ schedule, iteration limit, or rank-deficiency handling for the LM loop.
findings.evidence: l.1663: "`diagnostic.metrics` | `Object` | Contains final χ²_r, parameter correlation matrix, and ΔB_α values." — the only mentions of a correlation matrix (l.1644, 1663, 1743) are consumers; 'covariance' appears 8× (Ch6 Kabsch cross-covariance, Ch10 undefined); 'uncertaint' 11×, all input-side σ_i. l.60: "writes the final output constants (.fit / .par files)".
findings.why_it_matters: A spectroscopic fit without 1σ uncertainties and correlations is unpublishable and un-reviewable; the Method Matrix deliverable (§18, l.3422) is a .par/.var + .int pair, and the .var carries parameter uncertainties and the correlation block. Without a stated stopping rule and rank-deficiency policy the 'deterministic' engine (Ch1) is not reproducible and an implementing agent will invent them.
findings.recommendation: Add requirements: Cov = s²·(JᵀWJ)⁻¹ with s² = χ²/(N−M), reported both scaled and unscaled (SPFIT convention); σ_θ = √diag(Cov); ρ_ij = Cov_ij/(σ_iσ_j); outputs SHALL include N, M, N−M, χ²_r, σ_fit = √(χ²/(N−M)), RMS of unweighted residuals in kHz, max |o−c|/σ, the full correlation matrix, and the per-line o−c table in Pickett .fit layout; .var written with Pickett formatting. LM control: λ_0, increase/decrease factors, acceptance rule, convergence when |Δχ²|/χ² < 1e-8 or max|Δθ_k/σ_k| < 1e-3, max iterations, and 'if JᵀWJ is rank-deficient at the stated tolerance the fit SHALL stop and name the null-space combination' (never silently pseudo-invert). Restore the old plan's constraint (OLD_PLAN l.46): diagonal quartic constants Δ_J, Δ_K, D_J, D_K are bounded non-negative with a logged penalty.
findings.verifier_note: SRS defines no covariance, σ_θ, correlation or fit-statistics outputs: 'covariance' appears 6× (l.970/974/979 Kabsch cross-covariance, l.1204 Sobol output covariance, l.1644/1724 as an undefined consumer), not 8× as stated, and 'correlation matrix' only as a consumer at l.1644/1663/1724/1743; the only stopping rule is l.1643 'after k Levenberg-Marquardt iterations without converging to a predefined tolerance' with k and tolerance undefined, and the λ schedule at l.1179 is qualitative. The implementation already invents the unspecified behaviour the finding warns about (cochem_jax_fitter.py:689 'cov_raw = jnp.linalg.pinv(h_inv_target) * reduced_chi2'). OLD_PLAN l.46 non-negativity penalty for diagonal quartic constants and Method Matrix §18 (l.3421 '.par + .int pair that runs unmodified through SPCAT') confirmed.

findings.claim: The 'PrecisionViolationError' trap that 'intercepts' any float32/bfloat16 cast is not implementable in JAX as described; FP64 in JAX is a single process-global flag that must be set before the first array is created, and explicit 32-bit casts remain legal under it. The rationale given (NMR/FT-ICR) is also the wrong domain.
findings.evidence: l.187: "Any downstream module attempting to cast the spectral tensors to `float32` or `bfloat16` triggers a fatal `PrecisionViolationError`, trapping the operation before tensor corruption occurs." l.179: "In high-field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) or … FT-ICR MS … Δν ≈ 10^-3 Hz against carrier frequencies of 10^8 Hz"
findings.why_it_matters: JAX exposes no per-op interception hook; an agent told to build this will fake it (the code sets `jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)` in 25 module-level places, which is fragile because the flag only takes effect if nothing has been traced yet). FP64 is genuinely required here — ~10 GHz frequencies fit to ~1 kHz (1e-7) and eigenvalue differences of 10⁴ MHz subtract to kHz — but the SRS argues it from the wrong physics, so a reviewer cannot tell that the conclusion is right.
findings.recommendation: Replace with implementable requirements: (1) `jax_enable_x64=True` and `jax_default_dtype_bits='64'` set exactly once in the single package entry point before any JAX import side effects, verified by a start-up assertion; (2) `jax_numpy_dtype_promotion='strict'` so mixed-dtype arithmetic raises TypePromotionError; (3) a CI static check that runs `jax.make_jaxpr` on every jitted public entry point and fails on any `convert_element_type` to a float narrower than 64 bits; (4) dtype assertions (float64/complex128) on all pytree leaves at module boundaries. State the true rationale (kHz residuals on GHz frequencies; eigenvalue-difference cancellation).
findings.verifier_note: Claim confirmed: l.187/272 'triggers a fatal PrecisionViolationError, trapping the operation before tensor corruption occurs' has no JAX interception hook, PrecisionViolationError appears 0 times in src/, and the repo sets jax_enable_x64 at module level in 27 places across 25 files; l.179 rationale is NMR/FT-ICR. Verified in jax 0.11.2: x.astype(jnp.float32) is legal under x64, jax_numpy_dtype_promotion='strict' raises TypePromotionError on float64+float32, and jax.make_jaxpr exposes convert_element_type (so the CI check is feasible). Revision to recommendation (1): the flag jax_default_dtype_bits does not exist in current JAX (config exposes only jax_enable_x64, jax_explicit_x64_dtypes, jax_numpy_dtype_promotion), so drop it and keep: enable_x64 once at the single entry point, strict promotion, jaxpr CI scan, and float64/complex128 asserts at module boundaries.

findings.anchor: SRS l.205-208, l.290-293, l.326; repo requirements.txt l.1-2 (jax==0.4.13)
findings.claim: 'Persistent XLA Bytecode Caching' into a 'distributed LevelDB cache on the local disk', 'dual-target AOT' for gpu and cpu compiled simultaneously, bypassing 'the Python interpreter and JIT tracing phases', and '~15 s to <50 ms' do not correspond to anything JAX provides; the numbers are unverifiable and the pinned JAX version predates the export API the design would need.
findings.evidence: l.292-293: "Both executables are written to a distributed LevelDB cache on the local disk. … bypasses the Python interpreter and JIT tracing phases entirely, loading the compiled bytecode directly into device memory. This reduces the time-to-first-flop from ∼15 seconds to <50 milliseconds."
findings.why_it_matters: JAX's persistent compilation cache (jax_compilation_cache_dir) is a directory of files keyed by SHA-256 of the non-optimised HLO + jaxlib version + XLA flags + device configuration (GPU name string): tracing/lowering MUST run on every process start to compute the key, and entries are device-specific. A CUDA executable cannot be compiled on a CPU-only Codespace (no backend), so 'simultaneous dual-target AOT' is impossible on Setup 1. jax.export serialises StableHLO and compiles on the consumer side (landed as jax.export in 0.4.30, 2024-06-18; the repo pins 0.4.13, 2023-06-22); jax.experimental.serialize_executable pickles executables and its docs say never to load untrusted data — incompatible with Ch1's 'sterile' narrative. For J ≤ 30 Hamiltonians compile time is ~1 s, not 15 s. 'Distributed … on the local disk' is self-contradictory.
findings.recommendation: Delete §2.4. If a cache is wanted: 'The engine MAY enable JAX's built-in persistent compilation cache via jax_compilation_cache_dir; no bespoke cache, no serialised executables, no cross-host sharing. Compile time SHALL be reported as a non-functional metric with the target: first fit of ≤ 500 lines, M ≤ 25, J ≤ 30 completes in ≤ 10 s wall on a 2-core CPU runner.' Replace the pin with a JAX version that is tested (see NUM-11).
findings.verifier_note: Quotes l.292-293 and l.326 ('15-second JIT recompilation penalty', 'distributed LevelDB cache on the local disk') exact; JAX docs (docs.jax.dev/en/latest/persistent_compilation_cache.html) confirm the cache key is the non-optimised HLO + jaxlib version + XLA flags + device configuration including the GPU name string, with no LevelDB or AOT, and jax.experimental.serialize_executable source states 'It is not safe to call this API with untrusted inputs. Do not do this.' Changelog confirms jax.export public in 0.4.30 (June 18, 2024) and 0.4.13 dated June 22, 2023; the 0.4.13 tarball has no jax/export or jax/experimental/export (nuance: it does ship precursors jax/experimental/jax2tf/jax_export.py and serialize_executable.py, so the version argument is weaker than the rest). Measured J=30 eigvalsh and jacfwd jit compile in 0.17-0.26 s on CPU, supporting '~1 s, not 15 s'. 'Setup 1'/Codespace is not in the SRS (only .docs arch spec l.737); the recommendation's 'no cross-host sharing' is a policy choice since JAX does allow NFS-shared caches.

findings.claim: The 'transparent CPU fallback' (trap CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY mid-stream, retarget a 'specific graph node' to CPU, pin memory and stream back over PCIe, 'AVX-512 vectorization and OpenMP threading') is infeasible in JAX and factually wrong for the named production CPU.
findings.evidence: l.327-328: "routed through the system's multi-core host CPU leveraging AVX-512 vectorization and OpenMP threading. … the Gatekeeper pins the memory and asynchronously streams the output back to the GPU via the PCIe bus. Downstream operations resume on the GPU accelerators without the pipeline orchestrator ever being aware"
findings.why_it_matters: A jitted JAX computation executes wholly on one device; there is no per-node retargeting. OOM surfaces as XlaRuntimeError RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED at compile/execute and XLA preallocates 75 % of VRAM by default, so the '< 85 % / > 85 % / > 100 % VRAM' routing thresholds (l.334-336) are meaningless. XLA:CPU uses its own (Eigen) thread pool, not OpenMP. The Method Matrix (l.650) states the i7-13700K is 'AVX2 only' — consumer Raptor Lake has no AVX-512. An agent implementing this will produce dead code paths that cannot be exercised in CI.
findings.recommendation: Delete §2.6 and the Gatekeeper. Replace with a device policy: 'Default device is CPU. GPU execution is opt-in by configuration for the whole fit; the engine SHALL fail loudly on allocation errors rather than migrate work. No claims about SIMD width or threading model are made in the SRS.'
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified verbatim at SRS l.236-251 (draft) and l.321-337 (final): 'AVX-512 vectorization and OpenMP threading', 'pins the memory and asynchronously streams the output back to the GPU via the PCIe bus', and the <85%/>85%/>100% VRAM routing matrix (l.333-337). Method_Matrix.md l.650 states the production CPU (i7-13700K) is 'AVX2 only', and a jitted JAX/XLA computation runs on a single platform with no per-node CPU retargeting, so the Gatekeeper fallback as specified cannot be implemented; this is distinct from the already-established 'Ch2 is about NMR' fact.

findings.chapter: Cross-cutting (Ch2, Ch7 §7.3, Ch8) vs ecosystem deployment targets
findings.anchor: SRS l.1124, l.199/284, l.249-251; repo requirements.txt l.1-3, pyproject.toml dependencies; Method_Matrix.md l.650, l.776-777, l.818, l.3632
findings.claim: The SRS is GPU-centric ('orders of magnitude faster on GPU/TPU') while the real targets are CPU-only GitHub Codespaces/Actions runners (Setup 1) and an RTX 3090 whose FP64 rate is no better than its host CPU; the SRS mentions neither target nor the hard `cupy-cuda12x` dependency the repo carries, and the problem size makes GPU irrelevant.
findings.evidence: l.1124: "executing orders of magnitude faster on GPU/TPU accelerators than traditional CPU-bound finite-difference implementations." requirements.txt: "cupy-cuda12x==12.2.0". SRS occurrences: 'cupy' 0, 'Codespace' 0, '3090' 0. Method Matrix l.776: "Setup 1 | GitHub Actions, GitHub Classroom (50 seats), GitHub Codespaces. CPU only."; l.650: "RTX 3090 … FP64 = 35.6/64 = 0.556 TFLOPS, against roughly 0.61–0.64 TFLOPS AVX2 FP64 from the eight P-cores"
findings.why_it_matters: At T_rot ≈ 2 K (kT/h = 41.7 GHz) with B ≈ 0.5–2 GHz the populated levels have J ≲ 10; Wang sub-blocks are ≤ 6×6 (≤ 16×16 even at J = 30). Batched tiny FP64 eigh on a 1/64-rate consumer GPU is slower than LAPACK on the CPU because kernel-launch latency dominates. The Method Matrix (l.3632) sanctions JAX/GPU only for DVR diagonalisation and explicitly 'not … to replace SPFIT', noting a SPFIT fit costs 20–30 ms. `import cupy` fails on a host without an NVIDIA driver, so the package cannot be installed and imported on Setup 1; and CuPy and JAX in one process contend for VRAM because XLA preallocates 75 %.
findings.recommendation: Add a Deployment & Performance section: (1) conformance target = Linux x86-64, 2 cores / 8 GB RAM, no GPU (Codespaces/Actions); (2) GPU support, if any, is an optional extra (`[cuda]`) and never a correctness or performance requirement; (3) remove CuPy entirely (JAX already covers GPU); (4) NFR: a full LM fit (≤ 500 lines, M ≤ 25, J ≤ 30, with uncertainties) completes in < 5 s on the conformance target and is measured in CI; (5) delete all 'orders of magnitude', 'GPU/TPU', 'massive SIMD payload' language or mark it unverified.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: SRS l.1124 'orders of magnitude faster on GPU/TPU accelerators'; grep counts cupy=0, Codespace=0, 3090=0 in the SRS; requirements.txt l.3 'cupy-cuda12x==12.2.0' and pyproject.toml list CuPy as a hard dependency while ZERO Python files in the repo import it (dead dependency); Method_Matrix.md l.650 ('the GPU is no faster than its host CPU in double precision'), l.776 ('Setup 1 ... CPU only') and l.3632 ('not used to replace SPFIT') all read as claimed. One wording nuance: the cupy-cuda12x wheel pip-installs fine on a CPU host, it is `import cupy` that fails (cupy v12.2.0 __init__.py wraps `from cupy import _core` and re-raises 'Failed to import CuPy'), so 'cannot be installed and imported' should read 'cannot be imported'.

findings.claim: Ch2 sizes the convolution engine for 16–32 GiB NMR tensors on 4090/A100 cards while Ch8 forbids the same engine from exceeding 512 MB of VRAM 'regardless of line-list density or grid resolution'; the two are mutually contradictory, the chunk formula is undefined (η, '3+η'), and neither is scaled to a CP-FTMW spectrum, which is a few MB.
findings.evidence: l.1303: "must never exceed 512 Megabytes of peak VRAM during the synthesis of any single molecule's spectrum, regardless of the line-list density or the wavenumber grid resolution." l.317: "3D HNCA (Protein NMR) | 2048 × 1024 × 1024 | 32.0 GiB | Depth-wise Slicing (Stride = 128)" l.310: "η accounts for the FFT workspace expansion" (never defined)
findings.why_it_matters: A 2–22 GHz spectrum at 25 kHz spacing is 8×10⁵ points = 6.4 MB in float64; a 5–10-atom complex at 2 K has 10²–10³ lines. Even the naive outer product (8×10⁵ × 10³ × 8 B = 6.4 GB) is avoidable because each line affects only ±5 FWHM ≈ 20–100 grid points, so windowed accumulation is O(N_lines × window) ≈ 10⁵ operations. 'Overlap-Save' is a long-signal FIR technique irrelevant to summing narrow lines. 'Regardless of density/resolution' is unsatisfiable (the output alone is N_ν × N_T × 8 B). An agent will build elaborate, untestable machinery for a problem that does not exist in this product.
findings.recommendation: Delete §2.5 and §8.3. Replace with: 'Spectrum synthesis SHALL use windowed line-by-line accumulation (scatter-add) with a cutoff at ±k·FWHM, k configurable (default 10), or a bin-then-FFT path when all lines share one profile. Memory NFR: peak RSS ≤ 2 GB for N_ν ≤ 10⁷ and N_lines ≤ 10⁵ on the CPU conformance target; measured in CI.' Remove all NMR/MS/HITRAN/EXOMOL sizing tables.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified: l.1303 and l.1401 'must never exceed 512 Megabytes of peak VRAM ... regardless of the line-list density or the wavenumber grid resolution'; l.317 '3D HNCA (Protein NMR) ... 32.0 GiB'; l.310 'η accounts for the FFT workspace expansion' with η never given a value. The contradiction is even sharper than stated: the Ch2 table at l.315 runs a '1D Ultra-Res Mass Spec 2^26 ... 1.0 GiB' tensor as 'Unified Execution (No Chunking)', i.e. twice the Ch8 ceiling for the same spectral-synthesis subsystem (§2.3 l.276-284 describes the identical line-convolution task). The 2-22 GHz / 25 kHz arithmetic (8e5 points, 6.4 MB float64) is correct.

findings.claim: The lax.scan specification requires dynamic 'active line subset' selection inside the scan body, which JAX's static-shape model forbids, and its claim that peak memory is 'perfectly flat, decoupled entirely from N_ν' is false (stacked outputs scale with N_ν; reverse-mode AD through scan stores per-iteration residuals).
findings.evidence: l.1430: "Identifies the active local subset of the line-list that contributes non-zero absorbance to ν_chunk (utilizing a spatial bounding-box threshold to prune lines far outside their Voigt wings)." l.1435: "the peak VRAM remains perfectly flat, decoupled entirely from the total grid size N_ν. The final complete spectrum is dynamically constructed via the concatenation of the returned output sequence blocks."
findings.why_it_matters: Inside scan every array has a static shape, so 'pruning' can only be masking (evaluate all N_lines per chunk → per-iteration memory C_ν × N_lines × 16 B, no compute saving) or a pre-sorted line list with a fixed max-lines-per-chunk window via dynamic_slice; the SRS specifies neither, and the code confirms masking ('static masked batching'). With the SRS's own N_lines = 10⁶ and 512 MB, C_ν ≈ 8 points per chunk → ~10⁵ serial iterations. If Ch7's jacrev is applied through this scan, XLA stores all per-iteration intermediates (memory ∝ N_ν) unless jax.checkpoint is mandated.
findings.recommendation: Specify the memory model explicitly: 'lines SHALL be sorted by ν₀; each grid chunk processes a fixed window of at most L_max lines selected by dynamic_slice; peak device memory = C_ν·L_max·bytes·n_intermediates + N_ν·N_T·8 B, and both C_ν and L_max are derived from a stated budget.' State that gradients of the convolved spectrum are not required (the fit is on line positions; Ch9 sliders re-synthesise), so no AD passes through the scan; if ever needed, jax.checkpoint on the scan body is mandatory.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified at l.1430 ('Identifies the active local subset ... spatial bounding-box threshold to prune lines') and l.1435 ('peak VRAM remains perfectly flat, decoupled entirely from the total grid size N_ν ... concatenation of the returned output sequence blocks'); the stacked scan output alone is N_ν·N_T·8 B, refuting the flat-memory claim. Code confirms masking, not pruning: src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_convolver.py l.888-900 and l.936-940 compute `delta_nu = freq_chunk[:, None] - line_freqs[None, :]` over all N_lines per chunk, and the l.1081 'static masked batching' kernel uses `jnp.where(m_k, i_k, 0.0)` (l.1104); no dynamic_slice or sorted-window scheme exists in either copy (the two trees' convolver files are byte-identical).

findings.anchor: SRS l.1345/1443, l.1289/1387; repo requirements.txt l.1; code physics_core/cochem_convolver.py:367-405, convolver.py:463
findings.claim: The SRS prescribes `jax.scipy.special.erfcx` for the Voigt profile; the Faddeeva primitive is `wofz` (erfcx works only via the complex identity w(z) = erfcx(−iz)), neither function's availability under the pinned jax==0.4.13 is established, and the 'approximated' wording is wrong because the Re w(z) form is exact.
findings.evidence: l.1443: "Must strictly utilize `jax.lax.scan` for traversal and `jax.scipy.special.erfcx` (or equivalent optimized Faddeeva approximations) for Voigt profile generation." l.1387: "it is approximated utilizing the real part of the Faddeeva function w(z)"
findings.why_it_matters: Current JAX docs list both `jax.scipy.special.erfcx` and `wofz` (real or complex input), but neither appears in the JAX changelog, so the first supporting version is unverified; the repo pins jax 0.4.13 (2023-06-22), which almost certainly lacks both. The two code copies diverge: one implements a 32-term Weideman rational approximation in JAX (legitimate but with no stated accuracy), the other calls non-differentiable scipy.special.wofz. An implementing agent cannot satisfy 'strictly utilize erfcx' and 'or equivalent' simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite: 'The Voigt profile SHALL be evaluated as Re[w(z)] with w from `jax.scipy.special.wofz` on a JAX version ≥ the pinned minimum that provides it, or by a Weideman (N ≥ 32) / Humlíček approximation whose maximum relative error ≤ 1e-6 over 0 ≤ Im z ≤ 10, |Re z| ≤ 20 is verified in CI against scipy.special.wofz.' Replace 'approximated' with 'computed exactly as'. Raise and pin the JAX version accordingly.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified (l.1443 'Must strictly utilize ... jax.scipy.special.erfcx', l.1387 'approximated utilizing the real part of the Faddeeva function'), and the external claim is now proven rather than suspected: inspecting PyPI sdists, jax 0.4.13 (pinned), 0.4.38, 0.5.3, 0.6.2, 0.7.2, 0.8.3, 0.9.2 and 0.10.0 define neither erfcx nor wofz; 0.10.1 adds a real-only erfcx that raises 'erfcx does not support complex-valued inputs.'; complex erfcx and wofz first ship in jax 0.10.2 (JAX CHANGELOG.md never mentions either, as the finding said). Severity raised MINOR→MAJOR because the SRS 'Required Primitive' does not exist in the pinned toolchain and the repo's own `true_voigt_profile` (cochem_convolver.py:547-568, `jsp.erfcx(u)` with complex u) is a dead path (AttributeError on 0.4.13, ValueError on 0.10.1); anchor should add cochem_convolver.py:547-568, there are THREE divergent Faddeeva implementations (Weideman l.367-405, jsp.erfcx l.547-568, scipy wofz convolver.py:463), and the recommendation's pin should read 'jax >= 0.10.2'.

findings.claim: The quantum-number validity gate tests only K_a + K_c > J + 1; the correct rule is K_a + K_c ∈ {J, J+1} with 0 ≤ K_a, K_c ≤ J.
findings.evidence: "a transition terminating in a non-physical quantum state where $K_a + K_c > J + 1$) triggers an immediate `SpycFitQuantumViolation` exception"
findings.why_it_matters: For an asymmetric rotor each J has exactly 2J+1 levels labelled by (K_a,K_c) with K_a + K_c = J or J+1 (Gordy & Cook §7.2; King, Hainer & Cross 1943). The SRS rule admits e.g. J=5,K_a=0,K_c=0 or K_a=7,K_c=−2 and a Hamiltonian/assignment engine fed such labels will silently map them onto wrong eigenstates. Also the K_a+K_c rule is representation-independent, but SPFIT's doc notes 'K_a + K_c = N+1' for l>0 symmetric-top quanta — the gate must apply to asymmetric-top quanta only.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: 'Reject any state with K_a < 0, K_c < 0, K_a > J, K_c > J, or K_a + K_c ∉ {J, J+1}; for hyperfine quanta additionally require |J−I| ≤ F ≤ J+I (and the sequential-coupling triangle rules).' Add unit tests with positive and negative cases.
findings.verifier_note: Quote verified at SRS l.387 and l.465: the only test is 'K_a + K_c > J + 1', which admits K_a + K_c < J, negative K, and K > J; the correct asymmetric-rotor labelling K_a + K_c in {J, J+1} with 0 <= K_a, K_c <= J is standard (King-Hainer-Cross), and the recommendation is sound. One correction to the supporting remark: Pickett's documentation says 'For asymmetric top quanta with l = 1, Ka + Kc = N+1' and 'with l = -1, Ka + Kc = N' (encoding vibrational angular momentum in asymmetric-top labels, not symmetric-top quanta), while symmetric-top quanta are 'N K v J F1 F' with signed K for parity; both facts still support restricting the gate to asymmetric-top labels, so severity and recommendation are unchanged.

findings.claim: The roles and contents of the Pickett files are misdescribed (.cat is an SPCAT output, not an ingestion input; .int/.egy/.fit omitted; '.cat intensities Sμ²' and '.par Bayesian uncertainties' are wrong) and no SPFIT parameter-code, sign, representation or spin-weight mapping is given, contrary to TORQ-EXP-002.
findings.evidence: "holy trinity of Pickett extensions ... `.cat` ... calculated intensities ($S\mu^2$) ... `.par` ... Parameter File ... Bayesian uncertainties" (l.447-453); Ch9: "import an existing CoChem `.cat` or `.par` file representing the impurity" (l.1609)
findings.why_it_matters: SPFIT reads .par + .lin and writes .fit/.var/.bak; SPCAT reads .var + .int (dipoles, QROT, TEMP default 300 K, STR0/STR1 cutoffs) and writes .cat/.egy/.str/.out. .cat LGINT is 'Base 10 logarithm of the integrated intensity in units of nm² MHz' at TEMP, not Sμ². Nothing in .par/.var is Bayesian. SPFIT parameter values are coefficients of the OPERATORS ('parameters requested really signify the operator that will multiply the parameter'), so code 200 holds −Δ_J, 1100 −Δ_JK, 2000 −Δ_K, 40100 −δ_J (or +d₁ in S-reduction), 41000 −δ_K, 50000 +d₂; the representation is chosen by the SIGN of NVIB on option line 3 ('positive, prolate rotor ... negative, oblate rotor'), and nuclear-spin weights enter through WTPL/WTMN/EWT/IAX. The TORQ SRS (TORQ-EXP-002) requires exactly this mapping and warns 'Names alone are insufficient to convert conventions'. Without it a JAX-side Watson fit and an SPFIT .par cannot be interconverted and any 'SPFIT emulator' (l.1047) is unverifiable.
findings.recommendation: Add §3.2 'Pickett interface contract': table of file roles (inputs vs outputs), the .int line-2 fields, a verified operator/parameter mapping table with signs for A- and S-reductions (quartic and sextic), the NVIB-sign representation rule, WTPL/WTMN/EWT/IAX spin-weight mapping, and a 'spectrum-equivalence test': SpycFit eigenvalues from a .var must reproduce SPCAT .cat frequencies to <1 Hz for ≥3 reference molecules (one prolate, one oblate, one with hyperfine). Remove 'Bayesian' and 'Sμ²'.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at SRS l.447-453 verified; Pickett's spinv.pdf (CDMS mirror, text extracted) confirms LGINT = 'Base 10 logarithm of the integrated intensity in units of nm2 MHz' (not Sμ²), TEMP 'default is 300K', 'parameters requested really signify the operator that will multiply the parameter', 'sign NVIB = positive, prolate rotor (z = a, y = b, x = c) negative, oblate rotor (z = c, y = b, x = a)', the WTPL/WTMN/EWT/IAX fields, and its IDPAR digit scheme (TYP·100+KSQ·10+NSQ; TYP 4 = N+²+N−², TYP 5 = N+⁴+N−⁴) reproduces codes 200/1100/2000/40100/41000/50000, while the SRS gives no mapping and TORQ SRS l.324-326 requires 'exact parameter IDs, units, quantum numbers, axis representation, Watson reduction and spin conventions'. Revision (severity unchanged): soften the 'Bayesian' point — spinv states 'ERPAR is the parameter uncertainty' and 'ERRPAR defaults to a very large number for SPFIT', i.e. an a-priori constraint (tiny value = fixed parameter), so the SRS wording is non-standard rather than baseless and the recommendation should read 'replace with: a-priori constraint uncertainties in .par, fitted standard errors in .var'; and reading .cat is legitimate for overlays/impurity subtraction (SRS l.1609), so the defect is the undistinguished input/output roles and wrong field contents, not ingesting .cat per se.

findings.claim: The representation table mixes conventions (its 'III^l (z=c, x=a, y=b)' is III^r in the King–Hainer–Cross/Gordy–Cook convention) and the handedness flips the sign of the off-diagonal distortion constants; SR-4.2.1 (automatic switch) and SR-4.3.2/l.559 (INFO log vs 'must seamlessly branch') contradict each other.
findings.evidence: "| $\kappa = -1$ | Prolate Symmetric Top | Type $I^r$ ($z=a, x=b, y=c$) |" ... "| $0 < \kappa < 1$ | Oblate Near-Symmetric | Type $III^l$ ($z=c, x=a, y=b$) |" (l.533-536); "the system must seamlessly branch to the Watson S-reduction" (l.559) vs "emit an `INFO` telemetry log recommending the S-reduction" (l.570)
findings.why_it_matters: In the KHC/Gordy–Cook table I^r = (x,y,z)→(b,c,a), III^r = (a,b,c), III^l = (b,a,c). The SRS's I^r row follows that table but its III^l row gives the III^r mapping. The oxirane isotopologue study (arXiv:2201.09266) states explicitly that 'III^l and III^r differ only in signs of off-diagonal distortion parameters', so an agent coding the SRS table would produce δ_J/δ_K (or d₁/d₂) with the opposite sign from every III^l literature .par. Pickett's own documentation labels 'prolate rotor (z=a, y=b, x=c)' as I^r, which is I^l by KHC — the labels in the field are not self-consistent, which is exactly why the SRS must pin the convention by test, not by name. Automatically changing representation/reduction per κ (thresholds 0.9/0.95 are unreferenced) makes fitted constants non-comparable across runs and with the literature; κ is 'a conditioning diagnostic, not an automatic proof' (TORQ-EXP-002 note).
findings.recommendation: State one explicit axis mapping per representation with the KHC table reproduced, state that the handedness changes the sign of δ_J, δ_K, d₁, d₂, and make representation and reduction USER-SELECTED inputs recorded in provenance (default I^r/A for κ<0, III^r or III^l/S for κ>0, never switched silently). Replace SR-4.2.1/SR-4.3.2 by: 'If |κ| > 0.9 and A-reduction is selected, emit a WARNING; never change the user's choice.' Add the spectrum-equivalence test of PHYS-07 for each representation.
findings.verifier_note: PGOPHER asymsym.htm table gives Ir z=a,x=b,y=c; IIIr z=c,x=a,y=b; IIIl z=c,x=b,y=a (CMIstark/Gordy-Cook likewise 'I^r (x = b, y = c, z = a)'), so the SRS row 'III^l (z=c, x=a, y=b)' at l.536 is III^r; PGOPHER states 'changing between r and l only changes the sign of the off diagonal centrifugal distortion constants' and Müller et al. 2022 (arXiv:2201.09266 p.7) reads 'III^l and III^r differ only in some signs of off-diagonal distortion parameters'. Pickett's spinv.pdf indeed writes 'prolate rotor (z = a, y = b, x = c)' and 'Prolate basis is Ir, and oblate basis is IIIl' — I^l/III^r by KHC — so the SRS I^r row follows KHC while its III^l row copies Pickett's oblate wording: the table mixes the two conventions exactly as claimed. The contradiction is verified at l.559 ('κ ≤ −0.9 or κ ≥ 0.9 ... must seamlessly branch to the Watson S-reduction') vs l.570 ('If |κ| > 0.95 ... emit an INFO telemetry log recommending the S-reduction'); note SR-4.2.1 concerns representation (and already has a user override) while §4.3.2 concerns reduction, so the hard contradiction is intra-§4.3.2 and TORQ SRS l.326 ('κ ... is a conditioning diagnostic, not an automatic proof') is verbatim.

findings.claim: Permuting an isotopologue's rotational and centrifugal-distortion constants into the parent's axis labels is physically invalid; the reduced constants are defined in each species' own principal-axis system with A ≥ B ≥ C and z fixed by the representation.
findings.evidence: "applies this permutation operation to the rotational constants, centrifugal distortion parameters, and the electric dipole moment vector $\vec{\mu}$ of the isotopologue to lock them into the parent reference basis" (l.1025)
findings.why_it_matters: Watson's reduced Hamiltonian is not a tensor; its Δ/δ (or D/d) constants are tied to the choice z = a (I^r) or z = c (III) and transform between representations by the known I^r↔III^r formulas, not by a label permutation. After permutation one obtains a 'Hamiltonian' with A < B (violating the I^r assumption SPFIT and the SRS's own eq. at l.551 rely on) and distortion constants that are not Watson-reduced in any representation. The spectroscopic convention (and every .lin/.cat/.par in the literature) labels K_a, K_c and the a-, b-, c-type character in the isotopologue's OWN frame; what must be tracked is the opposite mapping — which parent dipole component becomes a-/b-/c-type in the isotopologue — so that predicted selection rules are correct. The row-wise argmax at l.1022 is also not guaranteed to be a permutation for the near-symmetric tops (κ → ±1) typical of complexes, and a det<0 Kabsch solution (l.988) for two r_e geometries means the TORQ geometry is the enantiomer and should be an error, not a silent flip.
findings.recommendation: Replace 6.3.3 with: 'Each isotopologue is fitted in its own PAS with A ≥ B ≥ C and the representation of PHYS-08; an axis-correspondence record (parent axis → isotopologue axis, from the eigenvector overlap with Hungarian assignment and a near-degeneracy warning when |O| < 0.9) is stored and used only to (a) re-express the parent dipole vector in the isotopologue frame to predict transition types, and (b) label equivalent transitions in reports.' Specify that det(R) < 0 raises an error. Remove permutation of distortion constants.
findings.verifier_note: Quote at l.1025 verified and l.1022 is a row-wise argmax with no permutation guarantee; that reduced constants cannot be relabelled across axis systems is shown directly by Müller et al. 2022 Table 1 (same oxirane data: D_K 26.07 kHz in III^l vs 2.96 kHz in I^r, D_JK −68.65 vs +50.47 kHz) and PGOPHER ('changing the representation changes the operator for Dk and the energy levels'), and l.1047 confirms the permuted set is fed to the fitter, so the claim stands at MAJOR (borderline BLOCKER for the near-prolate B≈C complexes of the Method Matrix where b/c switching is likely). Revision to the recommendation: det(R)<0 must NOT be an unconditional error — for planar or linear species the mass-weighted covariance C is rank-deficient, the sign of the smallest singular vector is arbitrary and the D-correction at l.990-993 is the correct standard Kabsch fix; raise an error only when det<0 occurs with a non-negligible smallest singular value (non-planar geometry = enantiomer or inconsistent input).

findings.claim: Chapter 6 spends its entire length on an SVD alignment that is a no-op for identical r_e geometries, while the structure-determination physics the domain actually needs (Kraitchman r_s with Costain errors, r_0/r_m^(1)/r_m^(2) least-squares fits, scaled-geometry isotopologue prediction) is absent from the body.
findings.evidence: "substituted species must be mathematically mapped back to the parent Eckart frame" (l.947); Kraitchman, STRFIT and r_m appear only as unchecked bullets: "Re-architect Kraitchman Substitution as a Pure Functional Evaluation" (l.1065)
findings.why_it_matters: Isotopic substitution does not move the nuclei in the Born–Oppenheimer approximation: the Cartesian coordinates are identical and the mass-weighted Kabsch rotation between parent and isotopologue is the identity; only the COM and the PAS orientation change, which a single diagonalization of the new inertia tensor handles. The real deliverables (Method Matrix §2.3, §6.10): predict isotopologue shifts to 0.02 % by scaling a trial geometry to the experimental parent constants (EVAL); r_s coordinates with Costain error 0.0015/|z| Å and the small-coordinate/imaginary-coordinate pathology; r_0, r_m^(1), r_m^(2) fits (STRFIT); and the explicit caveat that for a fluxional complex none of r_0/r_z/r_s/r_m is meaningful. None is specified. The Eckart condition quoted (l.951) is the condition for vibrational displacements about ONE reference; the architecture spec and Method Matrix §5.1/§3372 require Eckart embedding to be restricted to one symmetry-distinct basin or declared n.a. — also absent.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite Ch6 as 'Isotopologues and structure': (1) isotopologue constant prediction by parent-scaled geometry with 0.02 % acceptance; (2) Kraitchman r_s with Costain uncertainties and imaginary-coordinate flagging; (3) r_0 and r_m^(1)/r_m^(2) weighted fits with the Jacobian from PHYS Ch7; (4) a fluxionality flag that disables r_s/r_0 outputs for tunnelling complexes; (5) the single-basin Eckart gate. Keep the eigenvector axis-correspondence bookkeeping as a utility only. Add benchmark: Ar–oxazole r_s vs r_0 Ar–ring distance 3.447 vs 3.458 Å (Kraka et al. 1995).
findings.verifier_note: Grep of the SRS finds Kraitchman/STRFIT/r_m/Costain only in unchecked Ch6 'Improver' checkboxes (l.1065, 1066, 1069), and l.947-996 specifies a Kabsch alignment that reduces to R = I when parent and isotopologue share Cartesian coordinates (C = XᵀWX is symmetric positive semi-definite), i.e. a no-op under Born–Oppenheimer substitution. Every Method Matrix dependency is verbatim: l.264-278 (r_0/r_s/r_m table; Costain 'dz=0.0015/|z|'; 'For a genuinely fluxional complex none of r_0, r_z, r_s or r_m is physically meaningful'; Ar–oxazole 'substitution Ar–ring distance is 3.447 Å against 3.458 Å from the r_0 fit', Kraka et al. J. Phys. Chem. 99, 12466 (1995)), l.743 (scale trial geometry to parent, EVAL, 'Target 0.02 % on the shift'), l.764 and l.3372 (Eckart 'within one symmetry-distinct basin or declared n.a.').

findings.claim: The inertial defect Δ = I_c − I_a − I_b (sign rule) and the planar moments P_aa > P_bb > P_cc, which the Method Matrix makes a BINDING validation, are not required anywhere in the SRS body.
findings.evidence: "Enforce Planarity Conditions and Inertial Defect Bounds Checking. Rationale: Ensures SpycFit drops the task back to TORQ's dead-letter queue ..." (l.1070) — appears only as an AI 'improvement' checkbox; no requirement, equation, or output field exists.
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix §6.4: 'Validation rule, binding: if the computed and experimental inertial defects differ in sign, the structure is wrong, regardless of how well A, B and C agree.' Δ costs three subtractions with the 505379 constant and discriminates planar (|Δ| < 0.1 u Å²) from non-planar (e.g. −17.8 u Å²) complexes and reports the lowest out-of-plane mode; P_cc tells immediately whether a rare-gas atom sits in a symmetry plane. Omitting it removes the cheapest and most decisive conformer test from the Ch10 feedback logic (PHYS-04).
findings.recommendation: Add requirements: 'After every fit SpycFit SHALL compute Δ and P_aa, P_bb, P_cc from the fitted ground-state constants with uncertainties propagated from the covariance matrix, compute the same from each candidate theoretical structure (B₀^calc), and (a) reject a candidate whose Δ sign differs from experiment, (b) flag P-ordering violations, (c) report Δ for each vibrational satellite.' Define the constant and units (u Å², 505379.0 MHz u Å²).
findings.verifier_note: Grep for 'inertial defect', 'planar moment', 'P_aa'/'P_cc' and '505379' across the whole SRS returns only l.1070, an unchecked 'Improver' checkbox, so no requirement, equation or output field exists. Method Matrix l.693 reads verbatim 'Validation rule, binding: if the computed and experimental inertial defects differ in sign, the structure is wrong, regardless of how well A, B and C agree'; l.695 gives P_aa > P_bb > P_cc and 'For a rare-gas complex the change in P_cc on complexation says immediately whether the rare gas sits in a symmetry plane'; l.321 sets 'correct sign, always; magnitude to ~0.05 amu Å²'; l.3448 lists 'the inertial defect and the three planar moments' in the per-species deliverable checklist; l.373/545 give 505379.1/505379.0 MHz u Å².

findings.claim: Nuclear-spin statistical weights are hard-coded for one case (C₃v methyl top) with no mechanism for user-supplied weights derived from the molecular-symmetry (MS) group, which the Method Matrix requires for every system with equivalent nuclei.
findings.evidence: "SpycFit strictly enforces nuclear spin statistics based on the molecular symmetry group (PI group). For a generic $C_{3v}$ internal rotor with three identical spin-$1/2$ nuclei ... the spin statistical weights mapping to the spatial wavefunctions are:" (l.913)
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix §7 (binding): 'Feasibility is a dynamics judgement, not a software output'; 'determine the MS group from the set of feasible permutation-inversion operations, derive the spin statistical weights by hand, enter them into PGOPHER or SPCAT explicitly, and record the feasibility argument in the output. No package in this document's stack automates this.' In-scope systems — H₂O⋯X (ortho/para 3:1), NH₃⋯X, (H₂O)₂ (G16), Ar⋯C₂H₄, CH₃OH⋯Ar — all need weights other than the methyl-top table; wrong weights mean predicted lines that do not exist and intensity ratios that defeat assignment in a crowded CP-FTMW spectrum. SPCAT already has the input fields (WTPL, WTMN, EWT, IAX, VSYM).
findings.recommendation: Add: 'Spin statistical weights SHALL be a required user/TORQ input per symmetry species (with the MS group, the feasible operations and the derivation recorded in provenance) and SHALL map onto SPCAT's WTPL/WTMN/EWT/IAX fields; SpycFit SHALL NOT infer weights from a point group. A library of worked defaults (C₃v top on C_s frame, ortho/para H₂O, NH₃, G16 water dimer) MAY be offered but must be confirmed by the user.' Add to the Ch9 intensity formula an explicit g_I factor.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.913-918 verified: only the C₃v methyl-top table (A:4, E:2) is given, §5.6 (l.925-935) lists no spin-weight or MS-group input, and the only other weight is the generic g_i in the Ch8 partition function (l.1270-1272); the phrase 'strictly enforces nuclear spin statistics based on the molecular symmetry group (PI group)' implies automatic derivation, which Method Matrix l.755 ('Feasibility is a dynamics judgement, not a software output') and l.762 ('derive the spin statistical weights by hand, enter them into PGOPHER or SPCAT explicitly ... No package in this document's stack automates this') and l.3372 forbid, all verbatim. Pickett's spinv.pdf confirms SPCAT's 'WTPL, WTMN = statistical weights for even and odd state', EWT 'weight for states with E symmetry' and IAX exist for exactly this input. Minor wording: 'hard-coded for one case' slightly overstates — the SRS gives one worked example and no mechanism — but the consequence is identical.

findings.claim: The A:E weight table (4:2) and its 'parity enforcement' column are wrong as written: for a single methyl rotor the observed A and E components of a line have EQUAL weight (4:4 when the degenerate σ = ±1 pair is one line), and electric-dipole parity change applies to all species.
findings.evidence: "| $A$ | $4$ | $A \leftrightarrow A$ only. Strict parity enforcement ($+ \leftrightarrow -$). |" "| $E$ | $2$ | $E \leftrightarrow E$ only. No strict $+/-$ parity restrictions. |"
findings.why_it_matters: Three protons give 8 spin functions: I = 3/2 (A₁, 4) and two I = 1/2 doublets (E, 4). Counting the degenerate σ = ±1 E pair as one spectroscopic level gives total weight 4, hence the equal-intensity A/E doublets observed for acetaldehyde, methanol, 2-methylthiophene (and used as 'A-to-E ratio of unity' in astrophysical column-density work, arXiv:2603.21212). An implementer applying 4:2 per line predicts A lines twice as strong as E lines — a factor-2 systematic error in the intensity-guided assignment and in the 'next best transition' active-learning scores of the old plan. 'No parity restriction' for E is not a selection rule: for E1 transitions parity always changes; the correct G6 rules are by irrep (A₁↔A₁, A₂↔A₂ for μ_a, μ_b; A₁↔A₂ for μ_c; E↔E for all), cf. Hougen, Kleiner & Godfrey 1994. I am confident of the 1:1 doublet observation; the per-σ bookkeeping must simply be stated explicitly.
findings.recommendation: Replace the table with weights per observed level (A: 4; E (σ=±1 pair): 4, i.e. 2 per σ component) and state the counting convention; replace the 'parity' column with the G6 irrep selection rules per dipole component; cite the source of the weights (Method Matrix §7 requires it).
findings.verifier_note: Quote verbatim at SRS l.917-918 (identical in draft l.799-800). Core claim confirmed: three protons give 4 A1 + 2 E spin functions, so the A level and the doubly degenerate E level (σ=±1 pair) each carry total weight 4 (arXiv:2603.21212 'A-type I=3/2 weight 4, E-type total weight 4, A-to-E ratio unity'; CD3OH analogue 11:16, astro-ph/0311038), so 'E: 2' is at best an unstated per-σ weight and the parity column is not a selection rule. Two corrections to the recommendation: (a) the component-resolved irrep rules quoted (A1↔A1, A2↔A2 for μa,μb; A1↔A2 for μc) hold only for the torsion-vibration factor; for the full torsion-rotation species in G6 the E1 rule is A1↔A2, E↔E for every dipole component (space-fixed μ is Γ* = A2), with a/b/c-type carried by the Ka/Kc parity labels, so the SRS must state one labelling convention; (b) the reference is Hougen, Kleiner & Godefroid, J. Mol. Spectrosc. 163, 559 (1994), not 'Godfrey'.

findings.claim: The LAM chapter conflates PAM, IAM/RAM and 'the Woods method', writes the PAM Hamiltonian under the IAM label, misstates the ρ-axis geometry, and justifies a perturbative high-barrier method with a false computational-cost claim; it does not reference the XIAM/BELGI/RAM36 parameter sets the Method Matrix protocol mandates.
findings.evidence: "the Internal Axis Method (IAM) and its algebraic extension, the Woods method" (l.830); "the reference frame is constructed such that the coupling vector $\rho$ aligns with the internal rotation axis" (l.838); "For molecules where ... $V_3 > 300 \text{ cm}^{-1}$, the IAM exact diagonalization becomes computationally prohibitive for massive datasets" (l.883)
findings.why_it_matters: (i) H = H_rot + F(p_α − ρ·P)² + V(α) with ρ_g = λ_g I_α/I_g (l.840, l.855) IS the PAM Hamiltonian (Lin & Swalen 1959); in the RAM the z axis is rotated onto the ρ VECTOR (not the top axis; ρ ∦ λ because I_a ≠ I_b ≠ I_c) so that only ρP_z couples. (ii) Woods' 1966/67 'general program ... an extension of the internal axis method' is the ancestor of what is now called RAM; it diagonalises the torsional and rotational parts separately and treats off-diagonal terms perturbatively, valid only for high reduced barriers (s ≥ 20). The 'W_vσ = E + W⁽¹⁾·P + P·W⁽²⁾·P' expansion is Herschbach's PAM perturbation form, and D_pi2J/D_pi2K are XIAM parameters: three formalisms are blended under one name. (iii) The exact torsion–rotation matrix for J ≤ 20 and |m| ≤ 20 is of order 10³ per σ — milliseconds, not 'prohibitive'; XIAM and BELGI diagonalise exactly as routine. (iv) The in-scope regime includes V₃ = 11–50 cm⁻¹ (Method Matrix §6.8 anchors) where any high-barrier perturbation treatment fails; the Method Matrix protocol is 'fit V₃ to the observed splittings with XIAM (or BELGI/RAM36 if s is small)'.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite §5.2–5.4: define PAM, RAM and IAM correctly with the RAM rotation (angles θ, φ or XIAM's δ, ε), state H_RAM = A_RAM P_a² + ... + F(p_α − ρP_z)² + V(α) + torsion–rotation distortion terms (D_pi2J, D_pi2K, D_pi2−, D_c3J ...), adopt exact two-step diagonalisation for all barriers, drop 'Woods method' and the V₃ > 300 cm⁻¹ switch, and require parameter-level interoperability with XIAM and BELGI/RAM36 verified on 2-methylthiophene (V₃ = 197.7324(18) cm⁻¹, XIAM) and NH₃⋯HCOOH (195.18(7) cm⁻¹). Define s = 4V₃/(9F) and report it.
findings.verifier_note: All anchors verbatim: l.838 'coupling vector ρ aligns with the internal rotation axis' together with ρ_g = λ_g I_α/I_g (l.840) and F(p_α − ρ·P)² (l.855) is the Lin–Swalen PAM form labelled IAM (ρ ∦ λ for an asymmetric frame; the RAM puts z along ρ, as Method Matrix App. A.4 l.3652 itself states); l.883 'V3 > 300 cm⁻¹ ... computationally prohibitive' is refuted by basis arithmetic (J=20, |m|≤20 gives ~41×14 per σ), and the XIAM literature confirms Δπ2J/Δπ2K/Δπ2− are XIAM (combined-axis, RAM-then-PAM) parameters while the W_vσ expansion is Herschbach's PAM series. Method Matrix §6.8 l.721/725/729/731 confirms 197.7324(18) cm⁻¹ (XIAM), 195.18(7) cm⁻¹, low-barrier anchors 11.21745/36.63/49.37/55.77 cm⁻¹ and the binding protocol 'fit V₃ ... with XIAM (or BELGI/RAM36 if s is small)'; the SRS's own 'Typical Magnitude 100–1500 cm⁻¹' (l.876) contradicts those anchors.

findings.anchor: SRS l.828-830; Ch5 as a whole
findings.claim: The LAM chapter treats only C₃v methyl torsion; the dominant large-amplitude motions of the Method Matrix system class — intermolecular tunnelling (donor–acceptor interchange, rare-gas–molecule internal rotation, inversion) — have no Hamiltonian, no two-state coupling terms and no MS-group treatment.
findings.evidence: "specifically tailored for $C_{3v}$ rotors attached to $C_s$ or $C_1$ molecular frames" (l.830)
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix §2.1 defines the class as complexes 'with at least one large-amplitude intermolecular coordinate'; §6.9 gives tunnelling splittings from 6 MHz to 279,650 MHz within the water dimer alone and makes 'the barrier, the reduced mass, the tunnelling path, and the estimated splitting' a deliverable per row. Fitting such spectra requires the standard tunnelling-doublet effective Hamiltonian: two (or more) rotational states with energy separation ΔE and Coriolis-type interaction terms (F_ab, F_bc, F_ac, and their J-dependence), as implemented in SPFIT via vibrational-state coupling parameters, plus the G4/G8/G16 symmetry labels and ortho/para weights. Without it a floppy complex — the product's raison d'être — cannot be fitted at all.
findings.recommendation: Add §5.7 'Tunnelling complexes': multi-state Hamiltonian H = Σ_v H_rot(v) + ΔE_v + Σ Coriolis couplings (parameter list and SPFIT codes), symmetry labelling by MS group with user-supplied weights (PHYS-12), ingestion of TORQ's barrier/reduced-mass/path estimate as a prior with a factor-3 bound, and an acceptance case (e.g. Ar–H₂O or HCl–H₂O ground-state tunnelling doublets).
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.830 verbatim ('specifically tailored for C3v rotors attached to Cs or C1 molecular frames'); grep of the whole SRS for tunnel/Coriolis/interchange/inversion returns only methyl-torsion, Eckart and improver-list contexts, no multi-state ΔE/Fab/Fbc Hamiltonian or MS-group weights. Method Matrix l.248 defines the class 'with at least one large-amplitude intermolecular coordinate', l.735-737 gives the 6 MHz–279,650 MHz water-dimer range and the barrier/reduced-mass/path/splitting deliverable, and l.3389 lists the water dimer (with its tunnelling splittings) as row 4 of the six-system validation set, so the SRS as written cannot fit one of the governing acceptance systems. Minor nuance: 'cannot be fitted at all' overstates the case for complexes with quenched/unresolved tunnelling (fit as effective semirigid rotors), but is correct for resolved doublets.

findings.anchor: OLD_PLAN_architectural_changes l.46; OLD_PLAN_workflow l.19-20; SRS l.551, l.563 (no sign statement)
findings.claim: The old plan's hard penalty on 'negative diagonal distortion constants (D_J, D_K, Δ_J, Δ_K)' is physically wrong for Δ_K/D_K (and Δ_JK/D_JK), and would reject every SPFIT-convention .par because SPFIT stores −Δ_J, −Δ_JK, −Δ_K.
findings.evidence: "force a mathematically unphysical negative centrifugal distortion constant (strictly applying ONLY to diagonal constants such as $D_J, D_K, \Delta_J, \Delta_K$, not cross-term constants which can legitimately be negative)" (old plan l.46)
findings.why_it_matters: Only Δ_J (A) and D_J (S) are positive-definite in the semirigid-rotor limit (they are negative-definite combinations of the Kivelson–Wilson τ's, i.e. sums of squares of inertial derivatives; Gordy & Cook Ch. 8, Watson 1977). Δ_JK and Δ_K (and D_JK, D_K) are not sign-constrained: Δ_K = −τ_zzzz/4 − Δ_J − Δ_JK contains indefinite terms, Δ_JK < 0 is common (succinonitrile ground state Δ_JK = −27.79568 kHz, A&A 2016; several n-propanol conformers), and the signs of all five A-reduced constants depend on the representation (PHYS-08). In SPFIT the stored values are the operator coefficients (code 200 = −Δ_J etc.), so a 'reject negative' gate applied to a .par rejects correct physics. For floppy complexes effective quartic constants are also large and sometimes anomalous because they absorb LAM effects.
findings.recommendation: The SRS operator forms at l.551 and l.563 are correct and should be kept; add a sign table: 'Δ_J > 0 and D_J > 0 SHALL be enforced as soft bounds with a warning; no other distortion constant is sign-constrained. Signs are stated in Watson's convention (H_d = −Δ_J J⁴ ...) and converted to SPFIT storage (−Δ_J, −Δ_JK, −Δ_K, −δ_J, −δ_K; −D_J, −D_JK, −D_K, +d₁, +d₂) at the file boundary.' Remove the hard penalty from the plan.
findings.verifier_note: Old-plan quotes verbatim (architectural_changes l.46; workflow l.19-20); SRS l.551 and l.563 give the Watson operator forms with no sign statement anywhere (grep 'sign convention' empty). Only Δ_J/D_J are sign-definite; Δ_J + Δ_JK + Δ_K = −τ_zzzz/4 leaves Δ_K unconstrained and Δ_JK < 0 is common — succinonitrile ground state Δ_JK = −27.79568(51) kHz confirmed, but the source is A&A 2019 (aa35899-19), not 2016; correct the citation. SPFIT storage of the negated quartics confirmed by the Kisiel SPFIT crib sheet .par example ('200 ... /-DJ', '1100 ... /-DJK', '2000' for −DK), so a 'reject negative' gate applied to .par values rejects correct physics; the recommended soft-bound sign table is appropriate.

findings.claim: The intensity formula labels S_ij a 'Hönl–London factor' (closed forms that exist only for linear/symmetric tops), omits nuclear-spin weights, and leaves Q_rot(T_rot) and the default T_rot unspecified for the 1–2 K regime.
findings.evidence: "$S_{ij}$ is the line strength (Hönl-London factor)" (l.1553); "$Q_{rot}$ is the rotational partition function" (l.1555); "$T_{rot}$ ... Standard linear sliders. Triggers pure visual re-convolution" (l.1589)
findings.why_it_matters: For an asymmetric rotor the line strength is |⟨ψ'|Φ_Zg|ψ''⟩|² evaluated with the eigenvectors of the (reduced) Hamiltonian in the chosen representation (Cross, Hainer & King 1944), summed over M; an agent implementing textbook Hönl–London formulas gets b- and c-type intensities wrong exactly where the Method Matrix's 'dark conformer' and branch-existence logic (§6.1, ±0.1 D) depends on them. Nuclear-spin weights g_I (PHYS-12) and the torsional/tunnelling component weights are absent from the formula. At T_rot = 1–2 K, Q_rot must be a direct sum over J ≲ 10 including g_I and all LAM components (the classical (kT)^{3/2}(π/ABC)^{1/2} form is ~10 % off when A ≈ kT/h ≈ 20–40 GHz); the repository notebook currently uses 296 K.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: 'I_ij ∝ ν_ij · g_I · S_ij(ψ', ψ'', μ_g) · (e^{−E''/kT} − e^{−E'/kT}) / Q(T_rot), S_ij from direction-cosine matrix elements in the fitted eigenbasis (verified against SPCAT .str reduced dipole matrix elements), Q by explicit summation to convergence (TORQ-EXP-003), T_rot user input, default 1.5 K; non-Boltzmann two-temperature option.' Remove 'Hönl–London'.
findings.verifier_note: l.1549 formula contains no g_I or LAM-component weight; l.1553 'line strength (Hönl-London factor)', l.1555 bare 'Q_rot is the rotational partition function', l.1589 T_rot 'Standard linear sliders' with no default — all verbatim (identical in draft l.1464-1471); the only Q(T) definition in the SRS (l.1270) sits in the HITRAN/296 K IR chapter 8. Hönl–London closed forms exist for linear/symmetric tops (Herzberg); asymmetric-rotor line strengths require eigenvector-based direction-cosine elements (Cross, Hainer & King 1944; Schwendeman–Laurie, per NIST Monograph 70), so the label invites a wrong b/c-type intensity implementation. Repository notebook hard-codes temperature_k=296.0 (Start_SpycFit.ipynb l.86), and TORQ-EXP-003 (TORQ SRS l.328: report temperature, truncation, degeneracy, nuclear-spin convention, converge sums, avoid double counting) exists, so the recommendation's cross-reference is valid.

findings.claim: The VPT2 B₀ formula is correct but the chapter omits the Method Matrix's binding caveats (inverse-inertia-tensor averaging, unreliability of α for intermolecular modes, resonance deperturbation), names a non-existent Gaussian keyword, and prescribes inverting rather than diagonalising the inertia tensor.
findings.evidence: "parsing the `freq=vpt2` block in Gaussian" (l.580); "extracts the $3 \times 3$ equilibrium inertia tensor and inverts it to yield $A_e, B_e, C_e$" (l.596)
findings.why_it_matters: B₀ = B_e − Σ α_i(v_i + d_i/2) is right (Gordy & Cook §7), but: (i) Method Matrix §5.1 (binding) — for floppy coordinates the averaged constant is ½⟨μ_αα⟩ of the inverse tensor, 'any script that accumulates ⟨I⟩ and inverts it afterwards is wrong', with a 0.63 % bias at σ_R = 0.15 Å; the SRS has no such rule and no flag that α_r for intermolecular modes are the ones VPT2 gets wrong (§6.5). (ii) VPT2 α's from Gaussian/CFOUR/ORCA are affected by Fermi/Coriolis resonances; the SRS must say whether deperturbed α's or the code's resonance-handled ΔB are ingested and must verify each code's sign convention on a reference molecule. (iii) Gaussian's keyword is Freq=Anharmonic (VPT2 is the method); 'freq=vpt2' does not exist — a fabricated detail that will send a coder parsing for a block that is never printed. (iv) Principal constants come from the eigenvalues of I, not from the diagonal of I⁻¹ unless the geometry is already in the PAS.
findings.recommendation: Add to 4.4: 'ΔB_vib SHALL be ingested per axis with its provenance (code, level, resonance treatment) and sign convention verified by a reference test (e.g. H₂CO B₀ − B_e); for coordinates flagged floppy by TORQ, ΔB_vib SHALL come from inverse-tensor averaging (Method Matrix §5.1) or be marked n.a.; intermolecular-mode satellites are order-of-magnitude only.' Replace 'freq=vpt2' by the actual keywords per code (Gaussian Freq=Anharm, CFOUR ANHARM=VPT2, ORCA VPT2 module) and 'inverts' by 'diagonalises'.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at SRS l.580 ('parsing the `freq=vpt2` block in Gaussian') and l.596 ('inverts it to yield A_e, B_e, C_e') are verbatim; Gaussian's documentation (https://gaussian.com/freq/) names the option Freq=Anharmonic and no `freq=vpt2` keyword exists (VPT2 is ORCA `!VPT2` / CFOUR `ANHARM=VPT2`, Method Matrix l.2183), and SRS Ch3 l.486 itself says the tensor is 're-diagonalized', contradicting Ch4's 'inverts'. Method Matrix §5.1 l.545-557 ('Any script that accumulates ⟨I⟩ and inverts it afterwards is wrong', 0.628 %/22 MHz bias at σ_R = 0.15 Å) and l.701 ('the α_r for intermolecular modes are the ones VPT2 gets wrong') are binding and absent from §4.4; CFOUR's deperturbed-VPT2 module GUINEA is 'not part of the public release' (MM l.2167), so the SRS must state which α set is ingested. The inversion point is the weakest leg (inverting then diagonalising is what §5.1 prescribes for ⟨μ⟩) but the text stops at 'inverts', so it stands.

findings.claim: The only named benchmark (millimetre-wave propylene oxide) is a rigid chiral monomer; no acceptance case exercises the physics of the system class (complex with LAM, hyperfine, inertial defect, isotopologues, SPFIT round-trip).
findings.evidence: "rigorously tests the non-linear optimizer against known spectral benchmarks (e.g., the established millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide)"
findings.why_it_matters: The repository's fixtures are fabricated stubs; the SRS must supply the physical acceptance set so the fix/replace agent cannot pass on synthetic data. The Method Matrix already names anchored cases with published constants: Ar–oxazole (¹⁴N χ, r_s vs r_0), H₂CO–HCl (Cl quadrupole, quartics), C₆H₆–HCN, Ar–ketene (dipole components), NH₃⋯HCOOH (V₃ = 195.18(7) cm⁻¹), 2-methylthiophene (V₃ = 197.7324(18) cm⁻¹, XIAM), formamidinium formate (Δ = −0.243 u Å²), water dimer tunnelling.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Acceptance physics catalogue' listing ≥6 published .lin/.par sets with the fitted constants to be reproduced (frequencies to <1 Hz vs SPCAT, constants to within published uncertainties), one per physics module: rigid asymmetric top (propylene oxide), hyperfine (Ar–oxazole), internal rotor (2-methylthiophene via XIAM comparison), tunnelling dimer, isotopologue set with r_s/r_0 (Ar–oxazole), inertial-defect sign case. Mark 'synthetic benchmarking' as non-passing per the TEST mandate.
findings.verifier_note: Quote verified (l.68 draft, l.137 final); grep confirms propylene oxide is the only benchmark molecule named anywhere in the SRS, and every Method Matrix anchor cited exists with the stated values (l.3386-3391 table: Ar–ketene A=10447.9248 MHz with μ_a/μ_b and tunnelling, Ar–oxazole χ tensor and quartics, H₂CO–H³⁵Cl eQq and Δ_J/Δ_JK, water dimer 1→4 splitting, NH₃–HCOOH V₃=195.18(7) cm⁻¹, C₆H₆–HCN vs Ar₃–HCN; l.721 2-methylthiophene V₃=197.7324(18) cm⁻¹ XIAM; l.691 formamidinium formate Δ=−0.243 amu Å²), and the TEST mandate 'No Synthetic Benchmarking or Mocking' is at .github/copilot-instructions.md l.34. The finding overlaps the established fact 'no acceptance benchmark set', but the physics-specific catalogue tied to the Method Matrix system class is new content, so MAJOR stands. The recommendation's tolerance must change: SPCAT writes .cat FREQ as F13.4 in MHz (0.1 kHz print quantum; JPL catalog README https://spec.jpl.nasa.gov/ftp/pub/catalog/README), so 'frequencies to <1 Hz vs SPCAT' is unverifiable — specify agreement to the 0.1 kHz print quantum against SPCAT/SPFIT output and reserve a ≤1 Hz criterion for comparison against an independent FP64 eigen-solver reference.

findings.claim: Eleven blocks of LLM conversational chatter are embedded as body text, several of which assert that an adversarial audit was completed and logged, with no audit record in the document or repository.
findings.evidence: l.423 'I am still waiting for the full audit report from the Agent Council.' l.818-820 'The auditor successfully identified a critical physical chemistry hallucination ... has formally logged this to the project lessons file (`lessons.md`)'. l.1347 'I'm waiting for the Adversarial Auditor to review the chapter'.
findings.why_it_matters: These lines are not specification content, and the audit claims function as unverifiable acceptance evidence. The TORQ Implementation SRS 1.1 states the rule the ecosystem already adopted: 'conversational claims of completed audits ... are not acceptance evidence.' Note l.1347 is an additional leak not in the orchestrator's list.
findings.recommendation: Remove all eleven blocks. If an audit occurred, cite it as a dated document in a references section (reviewer, scope, findings, disposition). Add a document-control rule: no first-person or process narration in normative sections.
findings.verifier_note: The quotes at l.423, 818-820 and 1347 are verbatim and the TORQ Implementation SRS l.11 rule is exact ('Their conversational claims of completed audits, placeholders, and unverified performance assertions are not acceptance evidence'; see also l.507 'claimed agent audit cannot close a package'), and the l.820 lessons.md claim is unverifiable: no lessons.md exists in the SpycFit repo and the sibling CoChem-BASE/.docs/lessons.md and CoChem-TOPOS/.docs/lessons.md contain no entry on the Ch5 numeric-integration/free-rotor correction. Count correction: the ten cited anchors are ten contiguous blocks (18 first-person lines at l.73,75,253,422,423,602,604,606,817,818,820,1048,1050,1151,1152,1347,1531,1703); 'eleven' holds only if l.422 and l.423 are counted as separate turns, and l.342 ('Improver: I have addressed the Adversary's audit findings') and l.939 ('[SPOOFING RISK DETECTED]') are further process narration inside the Improvements sections that the recommendation should also name. Recommendation becomes 'remove all ten blocks plus l.342/939'; severity MAJOR stands because the Ch5 block functions as fabricated acceptance evidence in the document meant to be the audit baseline.

findings.claim: Pickett file roles are inconsistent and incomplete: the draft names .var, the final names .par, the output is said to be '.fit / .par', the impurity import accepts '.cat or .par', and the .int intensity file is never mentioned.
findings.evidence: l.375 '`.var` | Variance / Parameter File | ... alongside their current iteration values and Bayesian variances'; l.453 '`.par` | Parameter File'; l.60 'writes the final output constants (.fit / .par files)'; l.1524 'import an existing CoChem `.cat` or `.par` file representing the impurity'. '.int': 0 occurrences.
findings.why_it_matters: TORQ-EXP-002 fixes the roles (.par/.var/.int inputs; .cat/.lin/.var/.fit outputs) and forbids manufacturing observed lines from predictions. Reading an output as an input, or omitting .int, makes the SPFIT/SPCAT round-trip impossible. 'Bayesian variances' misdescribes least-squares standard errors.
findings.recommendation: Add a Pickett artifact table: extension, role (input/output), producer, consumer, format reference (SPFIT/SPCAT documentation), pinned executable version, acceptance test (SV-PICKETT round-trip). Include .int. Replace 'Bayesian variances' with 'parameter standard errors from the fit covariance'.
findings.verifier_note: Core claim verified: l.375 '.var | Variance / Parameter File ... Bayesian variances' vs l.453 '.par | Parameter File ... Bayesian uncertainties' (same role, different extension), l.1524/1609 'import an existing CoChem .cat or .par file', and '.int' has 0 occurrences; TORQ-EXP-002 (TORQ SRS l.324) names SPCAT inputs .var/.int vs generated .cat, observed .lin, fitted .var (it does not mention .par or .fit, so soften that paraphrase). Drop the '.fit / .par output' sub-point: per SPFIT documentation (spinv.html) SPFIT 'copies the par file to a bak file' and 'creates new text output files with extensions par, fit, var', so .par is legitimately both input and rewritten output. Remaining defects (.var/.par drift, .int omitted so a .par alone cannot drive SPCAT for the impurity subtraction, 'Bayesian' misdescribing least-squares standard errors) keep it MAJOR; recommendation stands.

findings.claim: The residual and chi-squared conventions are stated four times with two different energy-difference signs and no single definition of upper/lower state, residual sign, or weights.
findings.evidence: l.39 'nu_obs,i - (E''(p) - E'(p))/h'; l.108 'nu_obs,i - (E'(p) - E''(p))/h'; l.1090 'chi^2 = sum w_i [nu_exp - nu_calc]^2'; l.1640 'chi^2_r = 1/(N-M) sum ((nu_exp - nu_calc)/sigma)^2'.
findings.why_it_matters: The sign of O-C in the .fit output and in the residual pane must match SPFIT's convention or every comparison with literature fits is inverted. Two copies of Chapter 1 disagree on it.
findings.recommendation: One Definitions/Conventions section: E' upper, E'' lower; nu_calc = (E' - E'')/h in MHz; residual r_i = nu_obs,i - nu_calc,i; W_ii = 1/sigma_i^2; chi^2 and reduced chi^2 as single numbered equations referenced everywhere else.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: l.39 uses (E''(p) - E'(p))/h while l.108 uses (E'(p) - E''(p))/h; l.1090/1165 and l.1516/1601 use w_i, l.1640/1720 uses sigma_i directly; the SRS nowhere defines E' as upper / E'' as lower (only l.1277 'E'' is the lower state energy' in the HITRAN chapter), so under the standard convention l.39 yields a negative calculated frequency. Minor nuance: Ch7 l.1096 does define W_ii = 1/sigma_i^2, but Ch9 l.1516 reuses w_i without reference to it, so the 'no single referenced definition' point holds; the single Conventions-section recommendation is sound.

findings.claim: Representation and reduction selection is specified three incompatible ways: automatic by sign of kappa, automatic S-reduction branch at |kappa| >= 0.9, and advisory INFO log at |kappa| > 0.95 with user override.
findings.evidence: l.539 'shall automatically enforce a Type I^r representation for kappa < 0 and a Type III^l representation for kappa > 0'; l.559 'where kappa <= -0.9 or kappa >= 0.9 ... must seamlessly branch to the Watson S-reduction'; l.570 'If |kappa| > 0.95, the system must emit an INFO telemetry log recommending the S-reduction'.
findings.why_it_matters: Automatic switching changes the meaning of the fitted constants mid-campaign and breaks comparability with literature parameter sets. TORQ-EXP-002 already rules: 'kappa is a conditioning diagnostic, not an automatic proof of which reduction is best'.
findings.recommendation: SPYC-HAM-00x: reduction (A/S) and representation (I^r/III^l) SHALL be explicit inputs recorded in provenance, defaulting to the prior literature fit when one exists; kappa SHALL be reported as a diagnostic with one documented threshold. Delete the automatic branch at 0.9.
findings.verifier_note: All quotes are verbatim: l.539/635 'shall automatically enforce a Type I^r representation for kappa < 0 ... unless explicitly overridden by the user-defined `.spycfit` configuration payload'; l.559/655 'where kappa <= -0.9 or kappa >= 0.9 ... must seamlessly branch to the Watson S-reduction' (automatic, no override); l.570/666 'If |kappa| > 0.95 ... emit an INFO telemetry log recommending the S-reduction' with user override raising DegenerateSingularityWarning. Two thresholds (0.9 vs 0.95) and two modalities (automatic branch vs advisory) for the same decision; TORQ SRS l.326 reads exactly 'kappa ... is a conditioning diagnostic, not an automatic proof of which reduction is best'. PGOPHER's asymmetric-top help page (https://pgopher.chemistry.bristol.ac.uk/Help/asymham.htm) confirms constants must always be reported with their reduction and axis system, so auto-switching does change the meaning of fitted constants; recommendation is sound.

findings.claim: The Jacobian method is prescribed as design (jacrev through eigh) while the same document concedes jacfwd is optimal for this problem shape and elsewhere demands jacfwd, Hellmann-Feynman instead of AD, and 'exact analytical derivation' instead of AD.
findings.evidence: l.1189 'While forward-mode autodiff (`jacfwd`) is traditionally optimal when N_obs >> M, the architecture specifically leverages `jacrev`'; l.1796 'Implement Forward-Mode Auto-Differentiation for Jacobian Construction'; l.1058 'Instead of numerically unstable AD through the Hamiltonian eigensolver, utilize the Hellmann-Feynman theorem'.
findings.why_it_matters: 29148 5.2.5 asks for implementation-free requirements. The verifiable property is Jacobian accuracy and degeneracy safety, not the AD mode. Prescribing a contested design in the SRS locks the fix agent into one of several mutually exclusive mandates.
findings.recommendation: SPYC-FIT-00x: the Jacobian d(nu_calc)/d(theta) SHALL agree with central finite differences to relative 1e-6 on named test Hamiltonians, including near-degenerate K-doublets; derivative method is a design choice recorded in the design doc. Remove jacrev/jacfwd/Hellmann-Feynman language from the SRS.
findings.verifier_note: Verbatim: l.1106/1181 heading 'Analytical Jacobians via JAX Reverse-Mode Autodiff (`jacrev`)', l.1189 'While forward-mode autodiff (`jacfwd`) is traditionally optimal when N_obs >> M, the architecture specifically leverages `jacrev`', l.1058 Hellmann-Feynman 'Instead of numerically unstable AD', l.1055 'exact analytical derivation', l.1229 and l.1796 jacfwd. One nuance: l.1055/1058/1229/1796 are unchecked '- [ ] Improver' suggestions, not SHALL statements, so 'elsewhere demands' slightly overstates and this overlaps the brief's established fact (Ch10 Forward-Mode AD vs Ch7 jacrev); but the body itself prescribes an AD mode in a requirements document while conceding the alternative is optimal for the real regime (N_obs >> M for a ~300-line, <=15-parameter CP-FTMW fit), which is the 29148 5.2.5 defect. Recommendation is sound; suggest the near-degenerate test check d(nu_transition)/d(theta) rather than individual eigenvalue derivatives.

findings.claim: Non-functional targets are stated without quantity, conditions, hardware or measurement method, and the resource bounds contradict each other (512 MB universal VRAM cap vs 16-32 GiB tensors and 85%-of-VRAM routing).
findings.evidence: l.1303 'must never exceed 512 Megabytes of peak VRAM ... regardless of the line-list density or the wavenumber grid resolution'; l.1313 'chunk size ... calculated ... based on the active line-list size'; l.317 '32.0 GiB | Depth-wise Slicing'; l.293 '< 50 milliseconds'; l.321 'zero-downtime'; l.391 'sub-kilohertz precision'.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Sub-kilohertz', 'zero-downtime', '<50 ms' and 'never ... regardless' cannot be tested: no workload, no host, no definition of downtime for a batch fitter, and a universal quantifier over unbounded inputs. 29148 5.2.5 (verifiable, feasible) and 5.2.6 (consistent) fail.
findings.recommendation: NFR table with: quantity, unit, condition (named benchmark input), platform (see REQ-16), method (profiler/timer), tolerance, and [M]/[D]/[E] tag. Example: 'SPYC-NFR-PERF-001: on host H1 the propylene-oxide 300-line fit SHALL complete in <= 60 s wall (CPU) [M]'. Delete universal quantifiers.
findings.verifier_note: Every quote is verbatim (l.293 '< 50 milliseconds', l.321 'zero-downtime', l.391/469 'sub-kilohertz precision', l.317 '32.0 GiB | Depth-wise Slicing (Stride = 128)', l.1303/1401 'must never exceed 512 Megabytes of peak VRAM ... regardless of the line-list density or the wavenumber grid resolution', l.1313/1411 chunk size 'based on the active line-list size'). The contradiction is real: Ch2 §2.5 sizes convolution chunks to alpha=0.85*M_VRAM (l.308-310) with a >85%/>100%-of-VRAM routing table (l.334-336) while Ch8 caps the same convolution engine at 512 MB; and because l.1313 makes chunk size depend on the resident line list, 'regardless of line-list density' is unsatisfiable. Partly overlaps the established fact 'no NFR section with measurable targets', but the specific contradictory bounds and untestable quantifiers are new; recommendation is sound.

findings.claim: The operating environment is undefined and the few stated assumptions (AVX-512 hosts, RTX 4090/A100 accelerators) contradict the project's documented hardware (i7-13700K, AVX2 only; RTX 3090 24 GB with FP64 no faster than the host CPU).
findings.evidence: l.242 'leveraging AVX-512 vectorization and OpenMP threading'; l.219 'NVIDIA RTX 4090 or A100 40GB'; Method Matrix: 'i7-13700K ... AVX2 only ... RTX 3090 ... FP64 = 35.6/64 = 0.556 TFLOPS ... the GPU is no faster than its host CPU in double precision'.

Grep of the SRS finds no Python/OS/CUDA/JAX/HDF5 version, SPFIT/SPCAT named without version, PGOPHER and XIAM never mentioned; requirements.txt pins jax==0.4.13/jaxlib==0.4.13/cupy-cuda12x. Repo-wide grep excluding the SRS returns 0 files for all 11 listed terms plus HamiltonianFactory, WatsonAReductor, UnitTranslationLayer and 'Mendeleev Isotope Registry'; no *.spycfit or *schema*.json file exists; `job_board` appears only as `job_board.db` in CoChem-TORQ_Integration_Architecture.md l.22, never in code. Decisive extra evidence: in CoChem-BASE/.docs 'PCA-32' is defined as 'Atomic Swarm State & Chronometer Synchronicity Invariant Gate' (a swarm_state.json dual-write rule), so the SRS silently repurposes an existing governance label for a physics mandate; its only hint of meaning is leaked chatter at l.422 'physical chemistry accuracy (PCA-32)'.

findings.anchor: SRS l.1 (title only; no front matter); compare TORQ SRS l.1-30, 425-507
findings.claim: Against the ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 9.6 / IEEE 830 SRS outline, the document lacks purpose-and-scope with exclusions, definitions and acronyms, references, stakeholders and user classes, use cases, operating environment, assumptions and dependencies, external interface contracts, acceptance criteria, traceability, verification methods, and any document control.
findings.evidence: l.1 '# CoChem-SpycFit: Comprehensive Architecture & Software Requirements Specification' followed directly by chapters; grep for version/date/author/status/revision headers: none. Only user mention: l.1453 'the expert spectroscopist'. TORQ-EXP-004 bundle layout: never referenced.
findings.why_it_matters: The TORQ Implementation SRS shows the house style that is missing here: 1 'Document control, interpretation, and scope', defined SHALL/SHOULD/MAY, 15.2 acceptance catalog with pass conditions, 15.3 release scenarios, 16 work packages with definition of done, 17 decision register. Without these the SRS cannot gate the fix/replace agent's work.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the SpycFit SRS v2 skeleton in REQ-SKEL.
