Minimum: document control block; scope with exclusions; glossary; user classes (PI/spectroscopist, student, operator, autonomous agent); 6 use cases; external interfaces (TORQ bundle, Pickett files, BASE task service, PGOPHER/SPFIT/XIAM, CLI/API, UI); acceptance catalog; traceability matrices.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.1 title is followed directly by l.5 'Chapter 1' with no front matter, and grep for version/date/author/status/revision/document control/glossary/acronym/stakeholder/use case/user class/TORQ-EXP/bundle layout returns nothing; the TORQ SRS comparison is accurate (l.3 version+date, l.7 §1 'Document control, interpretation, and scope', l.13 SHALL/SHOULD/MAY definitions, l.21 §1.2 Intended users, l.433 §15.2 acceptance catalog incl. V-CONSUMER l.469, l.481 §15.3, l.489 §16, l.509 §17). Evidence correction: 'spectroscopist'/'the user' occur ~8 times in Ch9 (l.1453, 1455, 1479, 1492, 1514, 1524, 1526, 1530 plus duplicates), not only at l.1453, though still with no user-class definition. The finding largely restates the brief's established facts (no glossary/user classes/use cases/verification/traceability/document control); its net-new content is the 29148 outline mapping (web search confirms the 9-per-requirement/5-per-set characteristic structure behind 5.2.5/5.2.6; the 9.6 numbering was not independently confirmed) and the TORQ house-style comparison, so MAJOR is appropriate rather than BLOCKER.

findings.claim: The document is predominantly design and implementation prescription (class names, C++-style scoped identifiers in a Python project, LevelDB, jax.lax.scan, erfcx, Kabsch SVD, PCE surrogate, regexes) rather than externally verifiable requirements.
findings.evidence: l.1040 '`InertiaEngine::Center`'; l.1042 '`MathUtils::KabschSVD`'; l.292 'written to a distributed LevelDB cache'; l.1309 'The architecture mandates the use of `jax.lax.scan`'; l.1345 'Must strictly utilize `jax.lax.scan` for traversal and `jax.scipy.special.erfcx`'.
findings.why_it_matters: 29148 5.2.5 requires requirements to be implementation-independent where possible so that verification tests behaviour, not structure. None of the named classes exists in the code (0 grep hits), so the prescriptions also cannot be used to audit the implementation.
findings.recommendation: Split into SRS v2 (behaviour, interfaces, tolerances, acceptance) and a separate Architecture/Design Description. Each design mandate becomes either a requirement about an observable property (memory bound on named workload, Jacobian accuracy, alignment residual) or is dropped.
findings.verifier_note: All five quotes are verbatim (l.292 'written to a distributed LevelDB cache on the local disk', l.1040 `InertiaEngine::Center`, l.1042 `MathUtils::KabschSVD`, l.1309 'The architecture mandates the use of `jax.lax.scan`', l.1345 'Must strictly utilize `jax.lax.scan` ... `jax.scipy.special.erfcx`'). Grep restricted to *.py gives 0 hits for all 18 SRS-named identifiers (InertiaEngine, MathUtils, KabschSVD, AxisMapper, HamiltonianFactory, WatsonA/SReductor, SpycFitOrchestrator, VPT2Interface, ZeroPointCorrectionEngine, AbInitioParser, GeometryParser, HamiltonianBuilder, AlignmentCore, build_spectra_chunked, SpycFitQuantumViolation, DegenerateSingularityWarning, trigger_diagnostic_audit); the only file containing any of them is the SRS. Nuance for the synthesizer: the library-level tokens do occur in code (lax.scan 7 files, erfcx 3, jacrev 2, jacfwd 3, Kabsch 19), so the 'cannot audit' argument applies to the class-name prescriptions, not every mandate; 29148 clause mapping is 2011 'Implementation free' = 2018 'Appropriate', both under 5.2.5.

findings.claim: Modal verbs are undefined and used inconsistently (3 unique 'shall', ~25 'must', 0 'should'), and most obligations are bundled several-per-sentence inside narrative paragraphs.
findings.evidence: l.387 one sentence: 'sweeps the file, extracts the raw substring slices, dynamically casts them to localized `float64` and `int32` tensors, and verifies that nu_obs > 0 and sigma_exp > 0. Any line violating ... triggers an immediate `SpycFitQuantumViolation`'; l.570 SR-4.3.2 bundles evaluate-kappa, emit-log, proceed-with-warning.
findings.why_it_matters: 29148 5.2.5 'singular' (one requirement per statement) and 5.2.4 (requirements construct) are unmet; a bundled statement cannot be individually traced, prioritised, or marked pass/fail. TORQ SRS 1.1 defines SHALL/SHOULD/MAY; this SRS defines nothing.
findings.recommendation: Define SHALL (release requirement), SHOULD (recommendation, deviation recorded), MAY (optional). Rewrite each 'must' sentence as numbered single-obligation requirements. Target: every normative statement is one SHALL with one verifiable predicate.
findings.verifier_note: Exact-word counts: 'shall' 6 occurrences on 6 lines = 3 unique after chapter duplication (l.525/621, 539/635, 570/666); 'must' 57 occurrences on 52 lines (finding's ~50 is close); 'should' 0; 'may' 5, also undefined. No modal definition anywhere in the SRS, whereas TORQ Implementation SRS l.13 reads '`SHALL` denotes a release requirement; `SHOULD` a recommendation whose deviation must be explained in the run record; `MAY` an optional capability.' Quotes at l.387 (sweeps/extracts/casts/verifies/raises in one sentence) and l.570 SR-4.3.2 (evaluate κ + emit INFO log + proceed with DegenerateSingularityWarning) are verbatim and each bundles ≥3 obligations.

findings.claim: The 'Improvements (AI Researched)' checkbox sections are filler, unfulfilled claims, a spoofing-fallback message, title-only citations without a bibliography, and items that contradict the body or the project's rules.
findings.evidence: l.148-164 18x 'Standard processing applied. Rationale: Procedural step. Citation: Internal protocol.'; l.342 'produced the final, verified list of 20 improvements' (no list follows); l.939 '[SPOOFING RISK DETECTED]'; l.1802 'Mock Feedback CI/CD Integration Testing'; l.1790 'Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) to Prevent Catastrophic Forgetting'.
findings.why_it_matters: Checkbox wish-lists are not requirements; several directly contradict the body (l.1064 hardcoded masses vs PCA-32; l.1796 jacfwd vs l.1181 jacrev; l.1802 mocks in a zero-mock project) and introduce irrelevant ML concepts (EWC, curriculum learning, latent-space regularisation) into an LM fitter. Citations are unverifiable as given (author-year only, several 2025-2026).
findings.recommendation: Delete all ten sections. Any item worth keeping becomes a numbered requirement with Source, or an entry in a decision/backlog register. Add a References section with full bibliographic entries for every citation retained.
findings.verifier_note: One count correction: 'Standard processing applied. Rationale: Procedural step. Citation: Internal protocol.' occurs 17 times (l.148-164), not 18; l.147 and l.165 are different filler lines. All other evidence verbatim: l.342 'produced the final, verified list of 20 improvements' with no list; l.939 '[SPOOFING RISK DETECTED]'; l.1790 EWC; l.1802 'Mock Feedback CI/CD Integration Testing' versus copilot-instructions l.34 'No Synthetic Benchmarking or Mocking'; l.1064 'Hardcode IUPAC Mass Constants' versus l.395 'no static mass floats may exist'; l.1796 forward-mode AD versus l.1181 '## 7.3 Analytical Jacobians via JAX Reverse-Mode Autodiff (`jacrev`)'. No '# References'/'Bibliography' heading exists; 1× 'et al., 2025' and 2× 'et al., 2026'. MAJOR stands because the sections contradict the body and project rules, not merely hygiene.

findings.anchor: SRS l.72/141, 369/447, 1150/1222; word counts across file
findings.claim: The text is an essay, not a specification: adjectival assurances dominate ('strict' 83, 'highly' 38, 'massive' 25, 'rigorous' 25, 'guarantee' 17, 'absolute' 14, 'catastrophic' 11) and it issues guarantees that are false for a local least-squares method.
findings.evidence: l.369 'mandated to flawlessly process the holy trinity of Pickett extensions'; l.72 'mathematically provable and computationally secure terminal spectral assignments'; l.1150 'guarantees a robust, deterministic path to convergence, eliminating the manual trial-and-error parameter toggling historically required by spectroscopists'.
findings.why_it_matters: Adjectives cannot be verified (29148 5.2.5 unambiguous/verifiable). The convergence guarantee is untrue (Levenberg-Marquardt is local; Ch1 l.41 itself says the landscape is 'riddled with local minima') and would mislead a fix agent into treating non-convergence as a bug rather than an expected, reportable outcome.
findings.recommendation: Strip evaluative adjectives. Each claim becomes a measurable requirement (e.g., 'SHALL report convergence status, final reduced chi^2, condition number and correlation matrix; SHALL never report success when the step tolerance is not met') or is deleted.
findings.verifier_note: Adjective counts reproduce within noise (strict/strictly 78 vs claimed 83; highly 38; massive 25; rigorous/rigorously 25; guarantee/guarantees 17; absolute 14; catastrophic 11). Quotes verbatim: l.369/447 'mandated to flawlessly process the holy trinity of Pickett extensions'; l.72/141 'mathematically provable and computationally secure terminal spectral assignments'; l.1150/1222 'guarantees a robust, deterministic path to convergence, eliminating the manual trial-and-error parameter toggling'. The self-contradiction is real: l.41/110 'this optimization landscape is frequently riddled with local minima', and Levenberg–Marquardt is a local method, so the convergence guarantee is false as written.

findings.claim: SpycFit is said to receive data exclusively from TORQ yet is also required to parse raw Gaussian/CFOUR/ORCA outputs and extract VPT2 alpha constants itself, duplicating stages that the TORQ SRS assigns to TORQ.
findings.evidence: l.53 'receiving data exclusively from TORQ'; l.358 'deserializers for `.hd5` (HDF5) and `.json`' for 'CFOUR, Gaussian, ORCA'; l.580 'parses the ab initio anharmonic output (e.g., parsing the `freq=vpt2` block in Gaussian)'; TORQ-SPEC-001 table: 'VPT2 ... vibration-rotation interaction constants' and 'Vibration-corrected constants ... A0,B0,C0' are TORQ stages.
findings.why_it_matters: Duplicated ownership of B0 derivation means two implementations can disagree on the same prior and nobody owns the discrepancy. The repo already shows the symptom: 15,745 LOC of foreign TORQ/TOPOS/BASE code copied into src/cochem/.
findings.recommendation: SPYC-ING-001: SpycFit SHALL consume only (a) the versioned TORQ HDF5 bundle per TORQ-EXP-004 (consumer contract test V-CONSUMER owned jointly) and (b) user experimental files. Delete Ch4 4.4 (VPT2 extraction) or reduce it to 'read A0/B0/C0 with correction provenance; refuse Be mislabelled as B0'.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.53/122 'receiving data exclusively from TORQ' versus l.358/436 'deserializers for `.hd5` (HDF5) and `.json`' for 'CFOUR, Gaussian, ORCA', l.580/676 'parses the *ab initio* anharmonic output (e.g., parsing the `freq=vpt2` block in Gaussian)', l.515 'ingest raw *ab initio* tensors' and l.1039 'Standardize raw Cartesian inputs from quantum chemistry backends (Gaussian/CFOUR)' — all verbatim. TORQ Implementation SRS TORQ-SPEC-001 table assigns 'VPT2 ... vibration–rotation interaction constants' and 'Vibration-corrected constants ... A0,B0,C0 with correction provenance' to TORQ, and TORQ-EXP-004 says 'SpycFit export SHALL use a versioned schema agreed through a consumer contract test'. src/cochem/ measured at 15,745 LOC in 81 .py files. Recommendation is consistent with TORQ-SCI-004 ('never ground-state constants by renaming').

findings.claim: Governance and CI statements are written as present-tense facts that the repository contradicts, and name benchmarks only by example.
findings.evidence: l.68 'sterile CI/CD pipeline that rigorously tests the non-linear optimizer against known spectral benchmarks (e.g., the established millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide)'; l.1305 'enforced via continuous integration memory-profiling hooks'; l.1346 'must trigger the `trigger_diagnostic_audit` pipeline'.
findings.why_it_matters: CI runs only a `find`; pytest.ini runs one file of 11 tests; `trigger_diagnostic_audit` has 0 hits in the repo. An SRS that describes aspirations as existing controls gives a fix agent false confidence and no concrete gate. 'e.g.' means no benchmark is actually required.
findings.recommendation: SPYC-GOV-001 (mirroring TORQ-GOV-001): every advertised capability SHALL have a requirement ID, tests and recorded results; claimed audits are not evidence. SPYC-OPS-00x: CI SHALL execute the full named test manifest and the benchmark set in REQ-SKEL with published tolerances; release blocked otherwise.
findings.verifier_note: All three quotes are verbatim at SRS l.68/137, l.1305/1403 and l.1346/1444; `.github/workflows/cochem_spycfit_ci.yml` contains a single `find` step and no test or profiler invocation, `pytest.ini` has `testpaths = tests/test_provenance_fair_security_suite.py`, and `trigger_diagnostic_audit` has 0 hits anywhere in the repo outside the SRS. TORQ-GOV-001 exists verbatim at CoChem-TORQ_Implementation_SRS.md l.15, so the mirroring recommendation is sound; one addition: propylene oxide (C3H6O, a 10-atom single molecule, 'millimeter-wave') sits at the edge of the Method Matrix domain (2-22 GHz CP-FTMW, 5-10 atom complexes), so the required benchmark set should include at least one true vdW/H-bonded complex in-band.

findings.claim: The spin-statistical-weight table is ambiguous (per-component vs total E weight, no MS group stated, odd parity statements) and therefore cannot be verified.
findings.evidence: l.797-800 '| A | 4 | A <-> A only. Strict parity enforcement (+ <-> -). |' / '| E | 2 | E <-> E only. No strict +/- parity restrictions. |'
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix 7 makes MS-group spin statistics binding and notes PGOPHER requires user-supplied weights; an ambiguous table will produce wrong relative intensities in the one place the ecosystem flagged as critical. Physics lens should confirm against Lin & Swalen (1959) / Gordy & Cook; my confidence on the physics is moderate.
findings.recommendation: State the MS group (G6 for a C3v top on a Cs frame), weights per torsional level (not per species label), and an acceptance test comparing SpycFit intensities with XIAM/BELGI or PGOPHER output for a named methyl-rotor molecule.
findings.verifier_note: Quote at l.797-800/915-918 is verbatim and the SRS contains no other spin-statistics requirement (grep: only l.793-795/911-913; the 'statistical weight' at l.1514/1599 is fit weighting). Physics: 2^3=8 proton spin functions decompose as 4A + 2E-per-component, so 'E = 2' is correct only per degenerate component — read as a single E species it halves E-line intensities (A:E 2:1 instead of the correct 1:1), and the 'parity' column cannot be checked because no MS group is named (G3 for a C1 frame, G6 for Cs with the top axis in-plane, G12 for C2v — not G6 universally). Severity raised to MAJOR because a hard-coded 'generic C3v' table contradicts Method Matrix l.762 ('Required manual step in every workflow that involves equivalent nuclei: determine the MS group ... derive the spin statistical weights by hand, enter them into PGOPHER or SPCAT explicitly, and record the feasibility argument') and gives no route for two systems in the Method Matrix's own validation set (l.3380-3393): the water dimer (row 4, G16) and NH3–HCOOH (row 5, Roehling/Hill/Daly/Kukolich 2024, XIAM5, 20 A + 16 E lines, V3 = 195.18(7) cm^-1), which is the natural acceptance test.

findings.claim: Of 15 sampled normative statements spanning all chapters, 4 are testable as written, 2 partially, and 9 are unverifiable because they lack a quantity, a defined artifact, a bounded domain, or an observable outcome.
findings.evidence: l.59 'result in an immediate, silent drop of the task back to TORQ's dead-letter queue'; l.236 'autonomic, zero-downtime CPU Fallback Protocol'; l.405 'the latest AME ... at runtime'; l.1303 'must never exceed 512 Megabytes ... regardless of the line-list density or the wavenumber grid resolution'.
findings.why_it_matters: 29148 5.2.5 requires each requirement to be verifiable by a stated method (test, analysis, inspection, demonstration). 'Silent' behaviour is by definition unobservable and contradicts the ecosystem's truthful-failure rule (TORQ-DATA-002, V-FAIL).
findings.recommendation: Assessment: (1) l.19 air-gap: NOT testable (deployment prose) -> restate as 'no network calls during fit', Test under no-route namespace. (2) l.58 SHA-256 check: Testable once 'batch'/'vault' defined -> Test (tampered byte rejected, stable code). (3) l.59 silent drop: NOT verifiable; rewrite as explicit failure record -> Test. (4) l.68 CI benchmarks 'e.g.': NOT testable -> name dataset+tolerance, Test. (5) l.187 FP32 cast trap: PARTIAL -> Test at API boundaries + Inspection (global interception infeasible in JAX). (6) l.208 '<50 ms': NOT verifiable without host/workload -> Demonstration [M] on named host. (7) l.236 zero-downtime: NOT testable -> 'on injected OOM, CPU result equals GPU within 1e-10' -> Test. (8) l.387 Ka+Kc>J+1 rule: Testable for the one rule; 'e.g.' leaves set open -> enumerate rules, Test. (9) l.405 'latest AME': NOT reproducible -> pinned edition+digest, Inspection+Test. (10) l.539 SR-4.2.1: Testable -> Test (needs .spycfit schema). (11) l.570 SR-4.3.2: Testable -> Test, after deleting conflicting l.559. (12) l.789 m_max>=21 to 1e-6 MHz: PARTIAL -> Analysis+Test with named molecule, F, J range, reference code. (13) l.1141 Sobol<1e-6: NOT verifiable (bounds, PCE order undefined) -> Test on constructed case once parameterised. (14) l.1303 512 MB universal: NOT verifiable -> bounded named workloads, Test (profiler) + Analysis. (15) l.1643 tau_critical/k: NOT verifiable -> define in config schema, Test. Every requirement in v2 carries a Verification field with one of Test/Analysis/Inspection/Demonstration and an SV-* ID.
findings.verifier_note: All 15 sampled statements read verbatim at the cited line pairs, and the l.559-vs-l.570 conflict is real (l.559 'must seamlessly branch to the Watson S-reduction' at |κ|≥0.9 versus SR-4.3.2 'emit an INFO telemetry log recommending the S-reduction' at |κ|>0.95). The 'immediate, silent drop' at l.59/128 does contradict the ecosystem rule: TORQ-DATA-002 l.142 ('A missing quantity SHALL be represented as an explicit absent state ... with a reason') and V-FAIL l.465 ('produce truthful status'). Only caveat: the 29148 subclause number (5.2.5) could not be confirmed online; the verifiability characteristic sits in clause 5 of 29148:2018, so cite the characteristic rather than the subclause until checked.

findings.claim: No usable requirements baseline exists; a v2 Implementation SRS in the TORQ house style is required before any agent audits or replaces code.
findings.evidence: TORQ SRS l.14 'Requirements are identified as `TORQ-<area>-<number>`. Acceptance tests are identified in 15.'; l.489 '## 16. Implementation work packages and definition of done'. SpycFit SRS: 4 IDs, 0 acceptance tests, 0 work packages, 0 decisions.
findings.why_it_matters: The fix/replace agent needs a contract with identifiers, acceptance tests, named benchmark data and a definition of done; otherwise the next round of work will again be judged by prose.
findings.recommendation: SECTIONS: 0 Document control (version, date, author, status, revision history, superseded docs: this SRS, OLD_PLAN_20260807_*, .docs arch spec marked BASE-origin). 1 Introduction: 1.1 purpose; 1.2 scope IN/OUT (Method Matrix 2.1-2.2; adjacent IR/Raman as gated profile); 1.3 product perspective (BASE/TOPOS/TORQ/SpycFit data flow); 1.4 stakeholders and user classes; 1.5 definitions, acronyms, symbol table (Be/B0, A/S reduction, I^r/III^l, Pickett file roles, Product A/B/C, [M]/[D]/[E]); 1.6 references (full bibliography); 1.7 conventions (SHALL/SHOULD/MAY; MHz, cm^-1, K, D; constants service; pinned AME edition). 2 Scientific products and invariants (what SpycFit claims and does not; accuracy ladder for touched quantities per MM 3.1). 3 Use cases: UC-1 assign new CP-FTMW spectrum from TORQ bundle; UC-2 refine existing SPFIT fit; UC-3 isotopologue campaign; UC-4 internal-rotation fit; UC-5 upstream refinement request; UC-6 publication export. 4 External interfaces: 4.1 TORQ HDF5 consumer contract (TORQ-EXP-004 layout, version, V-CONSUMER); 4.2 Pickett files (.par/.var/.int in; .cat/.lin/.var/.fit out; pinned SPFIT/SPCAT); 4.3 BASE task-service and UI hosting; 4.4 PGOPHER/XIAM/STRFIT cross-validation tools; 4.5 CLI/API; 4.6 HITL UI. 5 Functional requirements by area. 6 NFRs (FP64, determinism/reproducibility, resource bounds on named hosts [M], truthful failure, provenance, installability). 7 Data requirements (records, missingness semantics, provenance). 8 Verification: evidence classes; acceptance catalog SV-*; benchmark manifest; release scenarios. 9 Work packages and definition of done (WP00 truthful baseline: one package tree, remove foreign code, fix pytest.ini/CI, remove committed junk). 10 Traceability matrices (req->source, req->test, test->code). 11 Decision register D-SPYC-nn (own fitter vs wrapper; mass convention; feedback path; LAM method; UI scope; IR/Raman profile). 12 Appendices (Hamiltonian conventions, glossary, historical docs). ID SCHEME: SPYC-<AREA>-NNN with AREA in GOV, SCOPE, DATA, ING, MASS, HAM, LAM, ISO, FIT, INT, ASSIGN, UI, EXP, FB, NFR, OPS, VAL; acceptance tests SV-<NAME>; decisions D-SPYC-nn. MANDATORY FIELDS PER REQUIREMENT: id; title; statement (one SHALL, one predicate); rationale; source (Method Matrix section/row, TORQ-EXP/SPEC id, User Manual section, PI decision); priority (Core / Research profile / Optional, per TORQ completion levels); verification method (Test/Analysis/Inspection/Demonstration); acceptance test id SV-* with pass condition and tolerance; dependencies/profile; status (proposed/approved/implemented/verified); change history. MINIMUM BENCHMARK DATASETS (named, with source, pinned reference constants, tolerance): (1) propylene oxide, semi-rigid asymmetric top, public SPFIT .lin/.par/.cat, A-reduction regression (fitted constants within 1 sigma of SPFIT; RMS O-C <= 1.1x published sigma_fit); (2) H2CO-HCl (Fraser et al. 1987; 6 atoms): 35Cl/37Cl quadrupole eQq, quartic distortion, planar cis geometry, inertial-defect sign gate; (3) Ar-oxazole (Kraka et al. 1995; 9 atoms): 14N chi tensor, dipole-type selection (b/c-type only), isotopologue axis handling; (4) SO2...HF / SO2...DF (Andrews et al. 1986; 5 atoms): D spin-spin coupling, chi(D), planar moments; (5) NH3...HCOOH (Roehling et al. 2024; 9 atoms): in-domain V3 benchmark, A/E splitting fit cross-validated with XIAM, V3 reported with +/-14% bound; (6) methanol or acetaldehyde: code-validation (non-domain) internal-rotation case against BELGI/XIAM reference energies; (7) water dimer (Mukhopadhyay/Cole/Saykally 2015; 6 atoms): tunnelling splittings must be labelled 'estimate only'; MS-group spin weights; (8) an isotopologue set (13C/D/18O of one of the above) for Kraitchman r_s with Costain error and shift accuracy 0.02%; (9) constructed exact cases (closed-form symmetric-top energies; rigid rotor vs SPCAT for identical .par/.var) for kernel verification per TORQ 15.1; (10) a TORQ-produced HDF5 bundle fixture (generated by the actual TORQ exporter, not hand-written) for V-CONSUMER; (11) negative controls: an EXOMOL/HITRAN line list and an NMR dataset must be refused with a stable out-of-scope error. Each dataset carries a preregistered tolerance frozen before evaluation (TORQ D10) and a reference-tool version (SPFIT/SPCAT, PGOPHER, XIAM, KRA/STRFIT).
findings.verifier_note: Inventory confirmed: the SpycFit SRS has four unique SR-IDs (l.539/555/570/601, duplicated at l.635-697) and zero hits for 'acceptance test', 'work package', 'definition of done', 'decision register' or 'traceability'; TORQ SRS l.14 and l.489 read as quoted. Three corrections to the benchmark list: (a) dataset 4 is misattributed — SO2···HF/DF with H19F spin–spin and D quadrupole coupling is Fillery-Travis & Legon, J. Chem. Phys. 85, 3180 (1986), DOI 10.1063/1.451829 (first report Chem. Phys. Lett. 123, 4), not 'Andrews et al. 1986'; (b) dataset 2's 'inertial-defect sign gate' cannot run on H2CO–HCl because A was 'not determined, fixed at 42 GHz' (Method Matrix l.3384; Legon 1996 only estimated it from R-branch lines) and the Method Matrix exclusion rule (l.3395) bars validating against a theory-influenced constant — move that gate to a planar system with a fitted A (SO2···HF or Ar–oxazole); (c) the list should be anchored to Method Matrix §17's existing six-system working set (l.3380-3393: Ar–ketene, Ar–oxazole, H2CO–H35Cl, water dimer, NH3–HCOOH, C6H6–HCN vs Ar3–HCN), which the proposal reproduces without citing and omits two of (Ar–ketene with measured μ_a/μ_b and tunnelling; the C6H6–HCN/Ar3–HCN topology-discrimination pair). Severity MAJOR stands.

findings.claim: The SRS never states the experimental platform or frequency range, and the only concrete references it gives (millimeter-wave, terahertz, radio-astronomy, the propylene oxide benchmark, committed fitted frequencies at 0.78–1.09 THz) all lie outside the Method Matrix scope of 2–22 GHz CP-FTMW.
findings.evidence: l.353: "Raw or pre-processed microwave, millimeter-wave, or terahertz spectral line transitions"; l.68: "known spectral benchmarks (e.g., the established millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide)"; l.45: "proprietary, unpublished experimental radio-astronomy or laboratory microwave data"
findings.why_it_matters: Frequency range determines J_max (≈ 10–30 at 2 K in 2–22 GHz, not the J=80 of the old plan or the high-J sextic/octic regime), which distortion order is determinable, whether Doppler or pressure broadening applies, and what the acceptance benchmark must be. 'CP-FTMW', 'chirped', '2–22 GHz' and '1–2 K' each have 0 hits in the SRS. Propylene oxide is a single semi-rigid chiral molecule, not a weakly bound complex, and its mm-wave spectrum does not exercise the floppy-complex physics the Method Matrix targets.
findings.recommendation: Add to Chapter 0: 'Experimental domain: broadband chirped-pulse FTMW, 2–22 GHz (extensible to 26 GHz), supersonic jet, T_rot 1–2 K, Doppler-limited linewidth ~50–100 kHz, frequency accuracy ≤ 10 kHz.' Replace the propylene oxide benchmark with an acceptance set drawn from the Method Matrix's own anchors: Ar–oxazole (Kraka 1995, b/c-type with 14N hyperfine), formamidinium formate (Zhou 2019, 3.7–14.3 GHz), H2CO–HCl (Fraser 1987, Cl hyperfine), ammonia–formic acid (Roehling 2024, V3 internal rotation), SO2⋯DF (D quadrupole), plus one methyl-rotor molecule for A/E regression. Delete 'millimeter-wave, or terahertz' from l.353/431 or mark as out-of-scope ingest tolerated but untested.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: l.45/114 'radio-astronomy or laboratory microwave data', l.68/137 'millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide', l.353/431 'microwave, millimeter-wave, or terahertz'; spectral_output/fitted_frequencies.txt l.3-5 are 782699.6, 847183.8, 1087861.4 MHz (0.78-1.09 THz); 'CP-FTMW', 'chirped', '2-22', 'jet', 'supersonic' each have 0 hits and the only three 'GHz' hits (l.486, 601, 697) are unit mentions, never a range, while Method_Matrix l.248 fixes 2-22 GHz CP-FTMW at 1-2 K. The proposed benchmark set matches the Method Matrix anchor table (l.3384-3392: Ar-ketene, Ar-oxazole 3-21 GHz with 14N chi, H2CO-HCl Fraser 1987, (H2O)2, NH3-HCOOH Roehling V3) and Ar-oxazole is confirmed as Kraka et al., J. Phys. Chem. 99, 12466 (1995).

findings.claim: The ghost-peak chapter models unassigned lines as contamination from reaction mixtures, discharge, pump oil, LO harmonics, 'residual Argon' and 'solvent', which is a mm-wave absorption-cell or condensed-phase picture; in a jet spectrum of a complex the unassigned lines are monomers, their isotopologues, other conformers, vibrational satellites and carrier-gas complexes, i.e. the next assignment targets rather than noise.
findings.evidence: l.1509: "ghost peaks—signals originating from impurities, precursor molecules, pump oil, or known instrumental artifacts (e.g., local oscillator harmonics)"; l.1524: "a known chemical species (e.g., residual Argon or a known solvent)"
findings.why_it_matters: Argon is an atom and has no rotational spectrum; 'solvent' does not exist in a supersonic expansion. The Method Matrix (l.699) states that for a van der Waals complex 'satellites are the second-strongest features in the spectrum, not exotica.' A tool that trains the user to mask residual lines as ghosts will mask the vibrational satellites, the 13C species and the second conformer that a campaign needs to assign.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite §9.4 as 'Residual-line bookkeeping': every observed peak carries a status in {assigned-to-species-k, candidate, excluded-with-reason}; the subtraction feature (l.1526-1530) is kept but re-targeted at known monomer and monomer-isotopologue catalogs (user-supplied .cat/.var or from the CDMS/JPL compiler already in code) rather than 'solvent'; add a requirement that the residual peak list after each fit is exported as the input to the next species/conformer/satellite assignment pass.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes are exact at l.1509/1594 ('reaction mixtures or broadband discharge experiments ... pump oil ... local oscillator harmonics') and l.1524/1609 ('residual Argon or a known solvent'); Method_Matrix l.699 reads verbatim 'satellites are the second-strongest features in the spectrum, not exotica'. Argon has no rotational spectrum, so the example is physically wrong; one evidential sentence is overstated (residual water/solvent vapour can co-expand and show lines in a jet), but that only strengthens the recommendation to retarget subtraction at known monomer catalogs rather than 'solvent'. Discharge/reaction-mixture CP-FTMW is a real use case but lies outside the Method Matrix system class, so the residual-line bookkeeping rewrite is the right fix.

findings.claim: T_rot appears eight times in the SRS but is never given a value or range, the text hedges between 'expansion' and 'cell', and the shipped entrypoint and UI code default to 296 K, so the one thermodynamic parameter that defines the product's intensity model is unconstrained.
findings.evidence: l.1471: "T_rot is the rotational temperature of the expansion/cell."; l.1504: "Thermodynamic / Line Profile | T_rot, Δν_D, Δν_C | Standard linear sliders."; ui.py l.205: "temperature_k: float = Field(default=296.0, gt=0.0, description=\"Rotational temperature in Kelvin (> 0)\")"
findings.why_it_matters: At 1–2 K only J ≲ 10–20 levels are populated for a complex with B+C ≈ 2 GHz; at 296 K the predicted spectrum has hundreds of J levels and the intensity pattern used for conformer discrimination and dark-conformer flagging is wrong. The Method Matrix fixes T_rot at 'roughly 1–2 K' (l.248) and TORQ-EXP-003 warns thermal-equilibrium conformer populations are not assured in a jet (two-temperature model). A 296 K default is a silent physics error in a HITL tool.
findings.recommendation: Add requirement: 'T_rot SHALL default to 1.5 K, be user-settable in 0.5–20 K, and be stored with every synthesized catalog and every fit; a separate conformational temperature T_conf (default: pre-expansion nozzle temperature) SHALL weight conformer populations (two-temperature model per TORQ-EXP-003).' Delete 'cell' from l.1471. Fix the notebook and ui.py defaults in the same change.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: T_{rot} appears on exactly 8 SRS lines (1464, 1471, 1504, 1526, 1549, 1556, 1589, 1611) with no numeric value or range anywhere (the only temperature value in the SRS is T_ref = 296 K at l.1266/1364); l.1471/1556 says 'expansion/cell'; ui.py l.205 'temperature_k: float = Field(default=296.0 ...' and notebook cell 3 'temperature_k=296.0' are exact; Method_Matrix l.248 says 'roughly 1-2 K'. The recommendation's citation must be corrected: TORQ-EXP-003 (TORQ Implementation SRS l.328) says only 'Thermal equilibrium conformer populations are not assured in a supersonic jet' and does not define a two-temperature model, so the T_conf requirement should be stated as SpycFit's own (citing the standard conformational-cooling literature) and TORQ-EXP-003 cited only for the non-equilibrium warning. Severity stays MAJOR.

findings.claim: Chapter 10 specifies the behaviour of other products (TORQ's DFT escalation ladder, CREST conformer search, torsional Hamiltonian diagonalization) inside the SpycFit SRS, names infrared spectra as a SpycFit input, and assigns conformer search to TORQ when the ecosystem assigns it to TOPOS.
findings.evidence: l.1628: "converge theoretical rotational and rovibrational parameters against experimental microwave or infrared spectra"; l.1686-1687: "TORQ escalates the level of theory, applying an automated fallback hierarchy: 1. Base Level: B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVP"; TORQ SRS l.25: "TOPOS owns global conformer discovery. SpycFit owns spectral assignment and fitting."
findings.why_it_matters: A SpycFit requirement cannot bind TORQ to a method ladder; the ladder also conflicts with the Method Matrix's recommended rows (r2SCAN-3c / ωB97M-V frozen-monomer recipes, junChS; l.84-87) and spend order (l.76). The infrared mention re-opens the vibrational scope the old plan explicitly closed. The agent would either implement TORQ logic in SpycFit or wait on a TORQ feature nobody specified.
findings.recommendation: Reduce Ch10 to SpycFit's side of the contract only: (1) a 'Refinement Request' record schema (trigger type, fitted constants with uncertainties, ΔB per axis, correlation matrix, assigned line count, suspected missing physics) written to the SpycFit output bundle; (2) a requirement that BASE, not SpycFit, routes it. Delete §10.4 and §10.5. Delete 'or infrared'. Replace 'TORQ initiates a broader conformational search' with 'TOPOS (via BASE) may be asked for additional candidates'.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified verbatim: SRS l.1628/1708 'microwave or infrared spectra', l.1674/1754 'TORQ initiates a broader conformational search ... crest/GFN2-xTB', l.1686-1687 'TORQ escalates the level of theory, applying an automated fallback hierarchy: 1. Base Level: B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-TZVP', l.1700-1702 SpycFit writes to the SQLite job_board; TORQ Implementation SRS l.25 states 'TOPOS owns global conformer discovery ... BASE owns ... durable task services' and that TORQ discovery adapters must not be 'silently run during refinement'. None of the ladder's methods appear in the Method Matrix recommended rows (l.84-87 R2 ωB97M-V/QZ+CP+VPT2, junChS; l.2320 r²SCAN-3c → ωB97X-D4/ωB97M-V), and ωB97X-D is explicitly flagged out-of-domain at MM l.2906 (36.34 pm RMSD on rare gases); the recovered plan (OLD_PLAN_architectural_changes l.3, l.60) reframes IR as the legacy mode and pivots SpycFit to microwave-only, so the 'infrared' input re-opens closed scope.

findings.claim: Chapter 4 puts the VPT2 α-constant parsing and B_e → B_0 vibrational correction inside SpycFit, parsing Gaussian 'freq=vpt2' text output, when the ecosystem assigns delivery of B_0 (and its uncertainty) to TORQ's export bundle and Gaussian is not a CoChem engine.
findings.evidence: l.676: "The extraction engine parses the ab initio anharmonic output (e.g., parsing the freq=vpt2 block in Gaussian) to identify the vibration-rotation interaction constants"; l.695: "register the base experimental predictors (A_0, B_0, C_0) used as the initial seed for the SPFIT/SPCAT non-linear least-squares fitting loop"
findings.why_it_matters: The Method Matrix's central v4 clarification (l.284-293) is that B_e and B_0 are different specifications and that each tier row states which it delivers; TORQ-EXP-004 defines /observables with unit/frame/source attributes for exactly this. Re-deriving B_0 in SpycFit duplicates TORQ, hides the provenance tag ([M]/[D]/[E]) that the Method Matrix requires on every number, and couples SpycFit to Gaussian/CFOUR text formats it should never see. It also conflicts with Ch6 improvement l.1063 which asks TORQ to supply the ZPVE mapping.
findings.recommendation: Replace §4.4 with: 'SpycFit SHALL consume A_0,B_0,C_0 (or A_e,B_e,C_e plus ΔB_vib) with declared uncertainty, provenance tag and frame from the TORQ bundle (/observables, TORQ-EXP-004) and SHALL NOT parse quantum-chemistry program output. Where only B_e is supplied, SpycFit SHALL widen the search window by the Method Matrix ΔB_vib band (0.1–0.7 %) and label the prediction as B_e-based.' Keep §4.2-4.3 (κ, representation, A/S reduction) as the fitting-Hamiltonian spec.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified (SRS l.676/580 'parsing the freq=vpt2 block in Gaussian', l.695/599 B_0 seed); TORQ SRS l.287 lists 'Vibration-corrected constants ... A0,B0,C0 with correction provenance' as a TORQ stage product, TORQ-SCI-004 (l.68-73) owns the B_0 = B_e − Σα(v+½) convention, and 'Gaussian'/'freq=vpt2' has 0 hits in both the TORQ SRS and the Method Matrix (TORQ engines at l.37 are ORCA, CFOUR, GPU4PySCF, MLFF) — so the claim stands. Recommendation must change: the proposed widening band '0.1–0.7 %' is the semi-rigid ΔB_vib figure (MM l.286); for the floppy complexes that are this product's system class the Method Matrix gives B₀ de novo at 1–2 % (l.291, l.306), so SRS v2 should make the B_e-only widening rigidity-class dependent (0.1–0.7 % semi-rigid, 1–2 % floppy) and tie it to the Product-class window of SCOPE-12.

findings.anchor: l.710, 712, 765, 789, 828, 830, 883, 907; Manual l.789; OLD_PLAN_workflow l.13; Method_Matrix l.248, 327
findings.claim: The LAM chapter specifies a methyl-rotor (C3v, V3 100–1500 cm⁻¹, IAM/Woods) solver for 'biologically and astrochemically relevant molecules', whereas the Method Matrix system class is intermolecular large-amplitude motion in weakly bound complexes with tunnelling splittings knowable only to a factor of 3, and the three SpycFit artifacts prescribe three incompatible LAM strategies (own IAM solver; PGOPHER only; TORQ Sinc-DVR handoff).
findings.evidence: l.710: "biologically and astrochemically relevant molecules exhibit Large Amplitude Motion (LAM), most notably low-barrier internal rotation (e.g., methyl torsions)"; Method Matrix l.248: "with at least one large-amplitude intermolecular coordinate"; l.327: "Tunnelling splitting | factor of 3 | estimate only"
findings.why_it_matters: For Ar–HCl-type or (H2O)2-type complexes the LAM is a bending/exchange tunnelling path with a non-C3v molecular symmetry group, not a methyl top; an IAM solver with hardcoded A=4/E=2 weights (l.913-918) cannot describe it. The fix agent cannot tell whether to write a torsion-rotation eigensolver, drive PGOPHER, or ingest DVR splittings. Only methyl-containing partners (e.g., methanol complexes) need §5 as written.
findings.recommendation: Split LAM scope explicitly in SRS v2: (a) 'Internal rotation of a C3v top' — keep a reduced §5 but make it an effective-Hamiltonian fitting capability (rho-axis or IAM parameters, F, V3, ρ, Dpi2J...) with regression against a published methyl-rotor fit; (b) 'Intermolecular tunnelling' — specify an effective two-state/doublet model (ΔE tunnelling splitting as a fitted parameter with Coriolis-type interaction terms), a splitting-search UI step (SCOPE-24), and ingestion of TORQ-supplied splitting estimates tagged 'factor-3'. State which engine (own JAX, SPFIT, PGOPHER) is the fitter of record for each case (see SCOPE-29).
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified: SRS l.710/828 'biologically and astrochemically relevant molecules ... methyl torsions', l.917-918 hardcoded A=4/E=2 weights, l.789/907 m_max ≥ 21 truncation, l.791/909 own LAPACK dsyevd/zheevd solver; the three incompatible strategies are real — Manual l.789 'SpycFit does not implement its own rotational diagonalization routine. Instead, it securely interfaces with the industry-standard PGOPHER executable', OLD_PLAN_workflow l.13 'extracts ... A/E tunneling splittings pre-calculated by TORQ' (Sinc-DVR); MM l.248 and l.327 read exactly as quoted. One nuance for the synthesis, not a refutation: C3v internal rotation is itself in-domain (MM l.326 uses the NH3–HCOOH V3 benchmark, ±14 %), so the reduced §5(a) must be retained as the recommendation already proposes; the defect is the complete absence of the intermolecular-tunnelling model (0 hits for 'tunnel' outside the methyl context) and the undefined fitter of record.

findings.claim: Chapter 6 applies single-reference Kabsch/Eckart alignment and parent-frame remapping to isotopologues unconditionally, which the Method Matrix forbids for the fluxional complexes that are this product's system class, and the chapter never states for which species (semi-rigid vs tunnelling) it is valid.
findings.evidence: l.947: "substituted species must be mathematically mapped back to the parent Eckart frame"; Method Matrix l.764: "Single-reference Eckart alignment must not be applied silently across equivalent minima."; l.270: "For a genuinely fluxional complex none of r_0, r_z, r_s or r_m is physically meaningful"
findings.why_it_matters: Isotopologue work is the core of a complex-structure campaign, but for a tunnelling dimer the Eckart frame is discontinuous across equivalent minima and Kraitchman returns a 'vibrationally averaged, symmetry-lowered fiction' (Method Matrix l.270). An agent implementing Ch6 (and the Kraitchman module already in code) without the basin-count gate will report structures that the governing document says are meaningless. This overlaps the physics lens but is a scope statement: the chapter must say which molecules it is for.
findings.recommendation: Add to Ch6 a scope gate requirement: 'Before Eckart alignment or Kraitchman/r_0 fitting, SpycFit SHALL read the equivalent-minimum (basin) count from the TORQ bundle; if >1 basin is sampled, structure fitting SHALL be disabled or restricted to one symmetry-distinct basin with an explicit note, per Method Matrix §7.' Restrict §6.3 axis-permutation logic to the predicted-constant side (relabelling a,b,c of a predicted isotopologue) and state that fitted constants are never remapped.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified (SRS l.947 'mapped back to the parent Eckart frame', l.959 Kabsch-Umeyama SVD, l.1047 downstream fitters 'operate entirely ignorant of structural distortions'); Ch6 (l.943-1047) contains 0 occurrences of tunnel/basin/equivalent-minima/semi-rigid, and MM l.270 and l.764 read exactly as quoted ('can only be formulated for a semi-rigid molecule ... must not be applied silently across equivalent minima'). Recommendation must change: a 'basin count' is NOT currently a field SpycFit can 'read from the TORQ bundle' — the TORQ Implementation SRS exports no such record (its only 'basin' is QTAIM basin-charge, l.459); the count exists only as the MM T4O-1d protocol output (l.3077) and the manual MS-group feasibility record required at MM l.766. SRS v2 must therefore add the basin-count/MS-group-feasibility record to the TORQ-EXP-004 consumer contract as a required input, and also strip the Ch6 l.1036 GeometryParser 'Gaussian/CFOUR' ingestion (same scope leak as SCOPE-08).

findings.anchor: SRS (0 hits for 'Method Matrix', '[M]', '[D]', '[E]', 'Product A/B/C'); README l.22; Method_Matrix l.66-72, 333
findings.claim: The SRS does not use the Method Matrix's Product A/B/C classification, its [M]/[D]/[E] provenance tagging, or its accuracy specification table, although the README claims the tags and the code's triage module already classifies by Product class.
findings.evidence: README l.22: "All calculations are automatically tagged with [M], [D], and [E] provenance arrays."; Method Matrix l.66: "Step 0 — which product are you building? Answer this before anything else; it changes what is reachable by an order of magnitude."
findings.why_it_matters: Product class determines the search window SpycFit must open around a predicted line (Product A: ±60–240 MHz at 12 GHz; Product B/C: ±4–12 MHz), which is the single most important parameter of the assignment UI. Without the tags, SpycFit cannot distinguish a measured parent constant from a de novo one when it widens windows for isotopologues, and cannot propagate the Method Matrix's rule that [D]/[E] values may not be the sole support for an accuracy claim.
findings.recommendation: Add requirement SPYC-WIN-001: 'Every predicted constant SHALL carry its Product class and [M]/[D]/[E] tag from the TORQ bundle; SpycFit SHALL derive the default search window from Method Matrix §3.1 (Product A floppy: 1–2 % of B; Product B: 0.03–0.06 %; Product C isotopologue shift: 0.02–0.1 %) and display it as an uncertainty band on every predicted line.' Cite Method_Matrix.md v4 §2, §3.1, §6, §7 in the SRS front matter as governing.
findings.verifier_note: Verified 0 hits in the SRS for 'Method Matrix', '[M]', '[D]', '[E]', 'Product A/B/C'; README l.22 and MM l.66/l.333 read exactly as quoted, and the recommended window numbers match MM l.74 and the §3.1 table (l.303-310). The code claim is confirmed and strengthened: src/cochem_spycfit/intake/cochem_spycfit_triage.py l.123-130 defines a 'Method Matrix v4' ProductClass enum but assigns classes by substitution count (A = parent, B = singly-substituted, C = multiply-substituted; l.815-817), contradicting the Method Matrix's definitions (l.69-72: A = nothing measured, B = measured parent/analogue, C = difference) — exactly the drift an SRS definition would have prevented; cochem_autofit_engine.py l.563 builds a ±1 % Product-A window citing 'Method Matrix §1.3', a document the SRS never references.

findings.claim: The SRS never defines SpycFit's output artefact set: Ch1 says it writes '.fit / .par', Ch3 only parses and swaps `.var` for `.par` between versions, `.int` (the SPCAT intensity input) has 0 hits, and nothing says which files are inputs to SPCAT versus outputs of SPFIT, which TORQ-EXP-002 makes a binding distinction.
findings.evidence: l.60: "writes the final output constants (.fit / .par files) to a designated egress node"; TORQ SRS l.324: "Distinguish SPCAT prediction inputs (parameter .var/supported parameter input and intensity .int) from generated .cat, SPFIT observed transition .lin, fitted parameter .var ... Never manufacture observed lines from predicted transitions."
findings.why_it_matters: A spectroscopist's deliverable is the .lin (assigned observed lines with uncertainties), the final .var/.par (constants), the .cat (prediction) and the .fit (residuals); these are also what a referee checks. The old plan (Stage 5) had this; the SRS dropped it. Without an output contract the fix agent cannot write the round-trip test TORQ-EXP-002 demands, and the 'never manufacture observed lines' rule — exactly the failure mode of the fabricated tests the brief documents — is unstated in SpycFit.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Outputs' section: SpycFit SHALL write, per species and fit iteration, .lin (observed, assigned, with σ and comment of source peak), .par/.var (parameters, SPFIT parameter IDs, units MHz, reduction and representation flags), .int (dipoles, T, Q, J_max for SPCAT), .cat (prediction), .fit (residuals), plus a JSON/HDF5 result bundle; it SHALL never write a predicted frequency into a .lin; and it SHALL round-trip through the pinned SPFIT/SPCAT binaries in CI.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes exact: SRS l.60/129 "writes the final output constants (.fit / .par files)", Ch3 table says `.var` at l.375 but `.par` at l.453, `.int` has 0 hits, TORQ SRS l.324 is TORQ-EXP-002 verbatim. The gap is worse than stated: Method Matrix §18 l.3422 defines the bench deliverable as "a `.par` + `.int` pair that runs unmodified through SPCAT, plus the resulting `.cat`", and per the CDMS SPFIT/SPCAT documentation .par/.lin are SPFIT inputs while .fit/.var are its outputs, so l.60 names an input file as the output. Old plan arch l.35 and workflow Stage 5 l.33 did list .lin/.par/.cat/.fit, confirming the SRS dropped it.

findings.chapter: Ch9 §9.2 (HITL workflow step: predict with search window)
findings.claim: The HITL chapter has no 'prediction with uncertainty window' step: the calculated spectrum C(ν) is drawn as a single stick/curve with no per-line search window derived from the constants' uncertainty and Product class, which is the first thing a spectroscopist needs when searching a broadband spectrum.
findings.evidence: l.1462: "plots the experimentally acquired spectrum, O(ν), overlaid with the theoretical predicted spectrum, C(ν). The theoretical spectrum is dynamically regenerated upon any perturbation of the system state."; Method Matrix l.74: "At 12 GHz: ±0.1 % = ±12 MHz · ±0.5 % = ±60 MHz · ±1 % = ±120 MHz · ±2 % = ±240 MHz."
findings.why_it_matters: A Product-A prediction for a floppy complex is 1–2 % off; at one line per MHz that is 60–240 candidate experimental lines per predicted transition (Method Matrix l.74). Without a window rendered per line (scaled by J, Ka dependence through the Jacobian the SRS already computes in Ch7), the user cannot tell a 'miss by 100 MHz, still consistent' from a wrong conformer.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-HITL-001: 'For every predicted transition SpycFit SHALL display a frequency search window computed by propagating the declared constant uncertainties (or Product-class default band) through ∂ν/∂θ, and SHALL list the experimental peaks falling inside each window ranked by predicted intensity and resolvability.' This is already partially coded (navigator, resolvability) and must be specified.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes exact (SRS l.1462/1547; MM l.74 and l.331 window conversion). The only 'window' in the SRS is the lasso masking "arbitrary frequency windows" at l.1514/1599; Ch10 l.1648 uses a 1-3 % band only as a post-fit rejection threshold, never as a per-line search window, and Ch7 l.1084 already provides the Jacobian needed. 'Already partially coded' verified: cochem_autofit_engine.py l.190-205 defines ProductASearchWindow (±120/±60/±60 MHz defaults) and physics_core ships cochem_spycfit_navigator.py and cochem_spycfit_resolvability.py, none of which any SRS text specifies.

findings.chapter: Ch9 §9.2.2 (HITL workflow step: peak picking / experimental line list)
findings.claim: The SRS never specifies ingestion of a raw broadband spectrum into an experimental peak list (frequency, uncertainty, intensity, SNR, blend flag); 'peak-finding' appears only as a rendering optimization, and Ch3 assumes experimental lines arrive already assigned.
findings.evidence: l.1483: "Dynamically queries the backend for local peak-finding and recalculates local Voigt convolution to prevent browser memory exhaustion on broadband spectra"; l.353: "Experimental Observables: Raw or pre-processed microwave ... spectral line transitions, intrinsically bound to assigned quantum numbers."
findings.why_it_matters: The input to an assignment campaign is an unassigned spectrum; 'intrinsically bound to assigned quantum numbers' describes the output. Peak picking with a frequency uncertainty model (centroid error vs SNR; typical CP-FTMW 5–10 kHz) determines the σ_i that Ch7's χ² weights use, so leaving it unspecified makes every fit statistic undefined. The viewport code already calls scipy.signal.find_peaks without a specified uncertainty model.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-EXP-001/002: 'SpycFit SHALL ingest a broadband spectrum (frequency/intensity arrays, declared frequency axis calibration) and produce a peak list with centroid frequency, σ_ν from an SNR-based model with a user-settable floor (default 10 kHz), intensity, FWHM and blend flag; the user SHALL be able to add/remove/merge peaks. Optionally ingest an externally produced peak list.'
findings.verifier_note: Quotes exact at l.1483/1568 and l.353/431 ("intrinsically bound to assigned quantum numbers"); no SRS text specifies spectrum ingestion, calibration, or peak-list σ, and even the old plan (workflow l.16) had the user supply a pre-assigned .lin. Code confirms: cochem_spycfit_ui_viewport.py l.26/406-408 calls scipy.signal.find_peaks for drag-snapping only, with sigma_predict_mhz=0.0 hardcoded (l.373) and no SNR/centroid-error model. The 5-10 kHz figure is consistent with the literature: a 2-8 GHz CP-FTMW study reports ~5 kHz SNR-dependent accuracy at <10 kHz resolution (RSC suppdata d0cp01141j), so a 10 kHz default floor is sound.

findings.chapter: Ch9 (HITL workflow step: pattern recognition / Loomis-Wood / AUTOFIT)
findings.anchor: SRS 0 hits for 'Loomis', 'pattern', 'search window', 'AUTOFIT'; src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_autofit_engine.py l.1-8; Method_Matrix l.339
findings.claim: The SRS contains no pattern-recognition step (Loomis-Wood plots, J-progression/series search, AUTOFIT triples) even though the Method Matrix names AUTOFIT as 'a complete, cheap, published route to an assignment' and the code already contains an AUTOFIT engine that no document specifies.
findings.evidence: Method Matrix l.339: "0.3–1 % plus a documented brute-force triples search is a complete, cheap, published route to an assignment."; autofit_engine.py l.2: "CoChem-SpycFit: Automated AUTOFIT Triples Combinatorial Pattern Matching Engine."
findings.why_it_matters: Between 'predict' and 'assign' the spectroscopist finds a-type J+1←J series by their near-constant (B+C) spacing, K-stacks by Loomis-Wood, and bootstraps constants from three lines; this is the step that converts a 1 % prediction into an assignment. Omitting it leaves the UI as a viewer with sliders (l.1492-1496), which is not how assignments are made.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-PAT-001..003: (1) Loomis-Wood/series display: given a selected line and a (B+C) or (B+C)/2 spacing, plot residual-vs-J panels; (2) AUTOFIT triples search over the Product-class window with constraints A>B>C, κ∈[-1,1], inertial-defect sign, dark-axis exclusion (|μ_g|<0.1 D), scoring by number of windowed peaks matched; (3) proposed-assignment review list feeding SCOPE-19. Specify the existing autofit_engine against these.
findings.verifier_note: Verified 0 hits in the SRS for 'Loomis', 'pattern' (case-insensitive), 'search window' and 'AUTOFIT'; MM l.339 and autofit_engine.py l.2 quotes exact; the 1,183-line AUTOFIT engine is mentioned in no .md/.txt/.ipynb/.json anywhere in the repo. MM l.3632 (AUTOFIT at 35-50 triples/s/core using SPFIT per fit) and MM l.3595 (Stage D dark flag |μ|<0.1 D) match the code header and the recommendation's constraints. Minor anchor note: the slider table sits at l.1500-1505 (and 1584-1589), not l.1492-1496, but both are in §9.3 and the 'viewer with sliders' characterization holds.

findings.chapter: Ch9 §9.3; Ch7 (HITL workflow step: fit → re-predict loop)
findings.claim: The SRS replaces the spectroscopist's fit → inspect residuals → re-predict iteration with manual parameter sliders and a one-shot automatic LM, and never specifies the iteration bookkeeping (which lines are in the fit, which are excluded and why, σ_fit, >3σ outlier flags, parameter correlation, determinability) that drives the next round of assignment.
findings.evidence: l.1492: "When a spectroscopist drags a slider to modify a rotational constant (A, B, C) or centrifugal distortion constant (D_J, D_JK, etc.), a full diagonalization is bypassed during the drag event."; l.1222: "eliminating the manual trial-and-error parameter toggling historically required by spectroscopists."
findings.why_it_matters: Nobody fits a rotational spectrum by dragging D_J in 1 Hz steps (l.1503); they fit, read the .fit residuals, re-predict, search the next J or K series, and decide which constants to float (A/S choice, when to free Δ_K or add sextics). Without a specified loop with its statistics, the agent will build a toy and the Sobol freezing of Ch7 becomes an unaccountable black box that silently fixes constants the user wanted to float.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-FIT-001..006: (1) explicit float/fix per parameter with defaults by stage (A,B,C first; quartics when N_lines and J-range permit); (2) after each fit display σ_fit (kHz), N_lines, per-line O−C/σ with >3σ flagged, parameter correlations >0.9 flagged; (3) re-predict automatically with updated windows; (4) a fit history (commit DAG already in code) with revert; (5) Sobol/sensitivity pruning only as advisory, never silent; (6) SPFIT parity check on demand. Demote sliders to a 'what-if' view labelled non-authoritative.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes l.1492 (dup. l.1577) and l.1222 exact; D_J '1 Hz steps' at l.1503/1588. Ch7 §7.2-7.4 (l.1163-1222) specifies only inner LM iteration plus automatic Sobol pruning (S_T<1e-6 'aggressively pruned', l.1213-1214) with no float/fix control, σ_fit, outlier flags, re-predict or fit history; the sole χ²_r/correlation mentions (l.1640-1644, 1663) are RRF trigger metrics sent to TORQ, not user-facing fit bookkeeping, and §9.4.1 persists only ghost-peak exclusions. Recommendation is sound; code already labels the sliders 'What-If' (interfaces/__init__.py l.5).

findings.claim: Chapter 6 covers only geometric axis alignment of an isotopologue; the SRS has no isotopologue campaign workflow: predicting isotopologue shifts by scaling to the fitted parent (0.02 % accuracy), natural-abundance species lists with expected intensities, deuteration with D hyperfine, LOIO leverage, and r_s/r_0 structure fitting with Costain errors.
findings.evidence: Method Matrix l.309: "Isotopologue shifts Δ(A,B,C) | 0.02 % | 0.02–0.1 % | geometry error cancels in the shift; obtained by scaling to the experimental parent, not by a better method"; old plan l.25: "Implement the Leave-One-Isotopologue-Out (LOIO) cross-validation statistical method."
findings.why_it_matters: Isotopic substitution is how a complex's structure is actually determined; the campaign step is: parent fit → scaled prediction of each 13C/18O/15N/34S/D species (window ±0.02–0.1 %) → search at 1 % natural abundance intensity → assign → fit each species with distortion constants fixed to parent → r_s/r_0 fit. None of this is in the SRS; the code has Kraitchman and the old plan had LOIO, but the SRS dropped both.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-ISO-001..005: (1) generate isotopologue list from formula with natural abundances and intensity scaling; (2) predict each species' constants as parent_fit × (TORQ_iso / TORQ_parent) with Product-C window; (3) fit species with quartics fixed to parent unless N_lines justifies floating; (4) structure fitting (r_s Kraitchman with Costain errors, r_0 least squares) gated by the basin-count rule of SCOPE-10; (5) LOIO leverage report. Keep Ch6 §6.3 only as the axis-relabelling utility these steps call.
findings.verifier_note: Method Matrix l.309 and OLD_PLAN_architectural_changes l.13/25 quotes exact. SRS has zero hits for LOIO, natural abundance, Costain or r_s; Ch6 body (l.943-1047) is purely Kabsch SVD alignment and axis permutation, and Kraitchman survives only as unchecked items in the non-normative 'AI Researched' checklist (l.1065-1066) — so 'dropped' should read 'demoted to a non-normative checklist'. Code has src/cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_kraitchman.py with Costain errors, confirming the SRS lags the code.

findings.chapter: Ch10 §10.2.2 (HITL workflow step: conformer / binding-topology discrimination)
findings.claim: The SRS treats conformer identity as a post-hoc failure trigger (ΔB > 5 % → CONFORMER_MISMATCH) rather than as the campaign's first decision: ranking several TORQ/TOPOS candidate topologies against the observed spectrum, flagging dark conformers, using relative intensities and the inertial-defect sign, and handling the common case that two or more species are present simultaneously.
findings.evidence: l.1648: "If the preliminary assignment loop yields effective rotational constants (A, B, C) that deviate from the TORQ-provided equilibrium constants ... the conformer is immediately flagged as highly suspect or outright misassigned"; Method Matrix l.668: "Any conformer with |μ_α| < 0.1 D on an axis is flagged dark in that selection rule and is excluded from the predicted line list"
findings.why_it_matters: For a 5–10 atom complex there are 3–9 binding topologies (Method Matrix l.105) differing by ≥11 % in B; the spectrum often contains two or three of them plus monomers. A workbench that loads one candidate and fails over to TORQ when it does not fit will mis-handle the normal case. The Boltzmann synthesizer in code addresses this but is unspecified.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-CONF-001..004: (1) load all candidate species from the bundle as separate predicted catalogs with populations (two-temperature), dark-axis flags and inertial-defect sign; (2) score each candidate against the peak list (windowed matches weighted by intensity) and present a ranked table; (3) allow concurrent assignment of several species to one spectrum with per-species residual lists; (4) the Method Matrix binding rule 'computed and experimental inertial defects differing in sign ⇒ structure wrong' SHALL be displayed as a hard flag on the fitted species.
findings.verifier_note: l.1648/1728 and Method Matrix l.668, l.105 ('3–9 structures'), l.311 ('≥11 % in B') quotes exact. 'conformer' appears in the SRS body only in Ch10 as the CONFORMER_MISMATCH failure trigger; 'inertial defect' only in the Ch6 checklist (l.1070); no ranking, population, dark-axis or multi-species step exists, while cochem_boltzmann_synthesizer.py l.1-12 implements two-temperature conformer-pool weighting the SRS never requires. The inertial-defect sign rule is binding per Method Matrix l.321 ('correct sign, always'), so the hard-flag recommendation is sound.

findings.chapter: Ch3 §3.2, Ch5 §5.5.2, Ch9 (HITL workflow step: A/E species and tunnelling doublets)
findings.anchor: l.373, 451 (quantum numbers 'J, Ka, Kc, v, …'), 913-920, 1764; Method_Matrix l.327
findings.claim: Although Ch5 describes an internal-rotation solver, the assignment-side model never carries torsional or tunnelling symmetry labels (A/E, σ, vt, or +/− doublet) in the .lin, UI or data model, and no step exists for searching an unknown splitting that theory knows only to a factor of 3.
findings.evidence: l.373: "upper/lower state quantum number designations (J, Ka, Kc, v, …)"; l.1764: "If the theoretical barrier provided by TORQ deviates significantly—resulting in failed A/E state fits—a BARRIER_HEIGHT_ERROR is flagged."; Method Matrix l.327: "splittings span 6 MHz to 279,650 MHz within one molecule"
findings.why_it_matters: For complexes with methyl tops or intermolecular tunnelling every rotational line is a doublet (or more); assigning requires labelling each component and often fitting two sub-states with a shared rotational set plus a splitting parameter. The user needs a 'doublet search' tool (pair peaks with a trial splitting across J series) and the data model must carry the symmetry label to the .lin or SPFIT cannot be driven.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-LAM-ASSIGN-001..003: (1) extend quantum labels with a symmetry/sub-state field (SPFIT vibrational-state index convention) in all records and writers; (2) a doublet/multiplet pairing tool that proposes component pairs given a trial splitting and its factor-3 band; (3) separate per-sub-state residual statistics. Make the hardcoded A=4/E=2 weights of l.913-918 a user input (see SCOPE-25).
findings.verifier_note: Quotes l.373/451, l.913-918 (A=4/E=2 table), l.1764 (dup. l.1684) and Method Matrix l.327 exact. Ch5 mentions v_t only solver-side (l.883); the assignment data model carries a bare 'v' never tied to A/E or any symmetry convention, the UI tooltip (l.1485) shows only J Ka Kc, and no doublet/multiplet pairing step exists anywhere. Making spin weights a user input matches Method Matrix l.760-762 ('PGOPHER requires user-supplied weights … enter them into PGOPHER or SPCAT explicitly').

findings.chapter: Ch5 §5.5.2; Ch9 §9.2.1 (HITL workflow step: nuclear spin statistical weights)
findings.claim: The SRS hardcodes spin statistical weights for one case (three equivalent protons, A=4/E=2) and claims to 'strictly enforce nuclear spin statistics based on the molecular symmetry group', whereas the Method Matrix states, as a binding software correction, that no tool in the stack automates MS-group weights and they must be user-supplied for every system with equivalent nuclei.
findings.evidence: l.913: "SpycFit strictly enforces nuclear spin statistics based on the molecular symmetry group (PI group). For a generic C3v internal rotor with three identical spin-1/2 nuclei"; Method Matrix l.762: "determine the MS group from the set of feasible permutation-inversion operations, derive the spin statistical weights by hand, enter them into PGOPHER or SPCAT explicitly ... No package in this document's stack automates this."
findings.why_it_matters: Water dimer, ammonia complexes, (HF)2, benzene complexes and any system with equivalent nuclei have alternating intensities (and missing levels) that determine whether a predicted line exists at all; getting them wrong 'is what makes a crowded CP-FTMW spectrum unassignable' (Method Matrix l.751). The intensity formula at l.1464 has no g_I factor.
findings.recommendation: Replace §5.5.2 with SPYC-SPIN-001: 'SpycFit SHALL accept user-supplied statistical weights per symmetry species (with the feasibility argument recorded as free text in the result bundle), SHALL apply them in the intensity model and in the .int/SPCAT input, and SHALL NOT compute them from a point group. A library of pre-derived weights for common cases (CH3 top, two equivalent H, two equivalent 14N) MAY be offered as defaults flagged as such.'
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified verbatim at SRS l.795/913 ('strictly enforces nuclear spin statistics based on the molecular symmetry group (PI group)') and Method_Matrix l.762 ('derive the spin statistical weights by hand ... No package in this document's stack automates this'); the intensity formula at l.1464/1549 has no g_I (the only g_i in the SRS is the HITRAN Q(T) at l.1270), and the C3v A=4/E=2 table is the sole case covered. Recommendation must be corrected: SPFIT/SPCAT take spin weights on the .par/.var option line (WTPL/WTMN for even/odd states, EWT for E species), not in the .int file (CDMS SPINV docs, https://cdms.astro.uni-koeln.de/classic/predictions/pickett/spinv.01.2001.html), so SPYC-SPIN-001 should say '.par/.var WTPL/WTMN/EWT' and note TORQ-EXP-003 (TORQ SRS l.328) already requires the nuclear-spin convention to be reported.

findings.anchor: SRS 0 hits for 'publication', 'LaTeX', 'table' as output; OLD_PLAN_workflow l.33-37; src/cochem_spycfit/interfaces/cochem_vibspyc_snap.py l.1-12
findings.claim: The SRS specifies no end product of a campaign: no constants table with 1σ uncertainties and units, σ_fit, N_lines, J/Ka ranges, correlation matrix, inertial defect/planar moments, derived structure, or the .lin/.var/.cat archive that journals and the Method Matrix's provenance rules require; the old plan had this via SCRIBE and the code has an AASTeX exporter that nothing specifies.
findings.evidence: old plan l.37: "SCRIBE now possesses the complete dataset required to automatically generate the final LaTeX publication methodology, BibTeX references, Supporting Information (SI) tables"; vibspyc_snap.py l.6: "Publication-ready AASTeX and LaTeX longtable rendering with siunitx and booktabs."
findings.why_it_matters: The deliverable of a spectroscopy campaign is a table of constants per species with uncertainties and the supporting line list; without a requirement, the agent cannot verify number formatting (SPFIT-style parenthesised uncertainties), unit conventions (MHz; χ in MHz; Δ in amu Å²) or that the [M]/[D]/[E] provenance of theoretical comparison columns is preserved.
findings.recommendation: Add SPYC-OUT-001..003: (1) per-species results table (A,B,C, quartics, χ, F/V3/ρ or splitting, Δ_i, P_gg, N_lines, σ_fit, J/Ka ranges) with uncertainties in SPFIT convention, alongside the theoretical column with its Product class and tag; (2) exported as LaTeX (booktabs/siunitx) and CSV/JSON; (3) the archive bundle (.lin/.var/.par/.int/.cat/.fit, peak list, result JSON, SHA-256 manifest) as the unit of hand-off to BASE/SCRIBE.
findings.verifier_note: grep of the SRS returns 0 hits for publication/LaTeX/booktabs/siunitx/AASTeX/journal and 'table' only as a document table (l.1035); the only output statement is l.60/129 'writes the final output constants (.fit / .par files) to a designated egress node'. Decisive external evidence: Method_Matrix l.3450 defines 'A deliverable checklist for every reported species: the .par and .int; the .cat over 2–20 GHz at 2 K; the dark-branch flags ...; the inertial defect and the three planar moments; the Stage E deduplication audit log', none of which the SRS mentions; old plan l.37 and vibspyc_snap.py l.7 (not l.6) quotes verified.

findings.anchor: README l.12, 14, 18, 30; Manual l.748, 786, 789-790, 854-860; OLD_PLAN_architectural_changes l.48-56
findings.claim: The two user-facing documents define SpycFit as an IR/Raman/UV-Vis/microwave spectrum generator driven by a %spycfit block with cm⁻¹ FWHM and PGOPHER .pgo export, which the recovered 2026-08-07 plan explicitly rejected as a scope violation; neither has been updated, so a new agent will re-implement the rejected scope.
findings.evidence: README l.30: "cochem-spycfit --type IR --broaden Voigt --fwhm 4.0"; Manual l.856: "FWHM = 4.0                # Full width at half max in cm^-1"; old plan l.55: "Any proposal to expand SpycFit into UV-Vis, TD-DFT, STEOM-CCSD, or time-dependent laser dynamics is REJECTED as a direct violation of the CoChem Scope Exclusions."
findings.why_it_matters: The README also claims the 'Valeev stack (MPQC, TiledArray, Libint)' and '11-Arrow Canonical Pipeline' and the code parses 'MPQC/g-xTB' output (fitter.py l.124), none of which appear in the Method Matrix's codes-in-one-line (ORCA search/VPT2, CFOUR CCSD(T)) or in the SRS; the user-facing docs are a fourth, independent product definition.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite README §1-3 from the SCOPE-15 definition; in the Manual, move §5.2.1 (IR/Raman) and §5.2.3 cm⁻¹ broadening to a separate vibrational-rendering module chapter, drop `Type = IR|Raman|UVVIS` from %spycfit, and replace §5.2.2's 'PGOPHER .pgo' with the SPFIT/SPCAT contract decided in SCOPE-14. Remove MPQC/TiledArray/Libint claims unless TORQ's SRS lists them.
findings.verifier_note: README l.12/14/18/30 and Manual l.748, 786-789 ('.pgo file'), 854-856 ('FWHM = 4.0 # ... cm^-1') verified. Two corrections: (a) old plan l.55 explicitly REJECTS only UV-Vis/TD-DFT/STEOM-CCSD/laser dynamics; IR/Raman is superseded, not rejected (l.3 'transition the module from a standard linear IR/Raman convolution engine', l.60 'transform from a static IR spectrum generator into an interactive ... microwave spectroscopy fitting engine'), and Method_Matrix Tables 8-9 (l.3221, 3257) keep IR/Raman prediction in the ecosystem on the TORQ side, so the Manual's IR/Raman text should be re-homed rather than deleted while 'UVVIS' is dropped outright; (b) fitter.py is 58 lines, the MPQC/g-xTB parsing is at l.5/18/29, not l.124.

findings.claim: PCA-32 makes SpycFit responsible for computing equilibrium rotational constants from Cartesian geometries with nuclear masses fetched from 'the latest AME database at runtime', a Tier-I/TORQ computation that an assignment tool should receive, not perform; the Ch6 improvement list then contradicts it by demanding hardcoded IUPAC masses.
findings.evidence: l.483: "The atomic masses m_i are dynamically injected from the latest AME (Atomic Mass Evaluation) database at runtime"; l.1064: "Hardcode IUPAC Mass Constants as Immutable Tier III Enums."
findings.why_it_matters: The only mass-dependent operations SpycFit legitimately performs are isotopologue scaling, Kraitchman/r_0 fitting and inertial-defect conversion, all of which need the standard conversion constant 505 379.005(36) MHz amu Å² (Method Matrix l.684) and a fixed, versioned isotopic mass table recorded in the result bundle for reproducibility, not a runtime download (which also contradicts the SRS's own air-gap). Computing A_e from geometry belongs to TORQ.
findings.recommendation: Replace §3.3 with SPYC-MASS-001: 'SpycFit SHALL use a pinned, versioned isotopic mass table (AME2020 or later, version recorded in every output) and the CODATA conversion constant; it SHALL NOT recompute equilibrium constants from geometry except as a consistency check against the TORQ bundle, flagged as such.' Delete the nuclear-mass (M_atom − Z m_e + B_e/c²) directive from scope (physics lens will address its correctness).
findings.verifier_note: l.483 ('dynamically injected from the latest AME ... at runtime') and l.1064 ('Hardcode IUPAC Mass Constants as Immutable Tier III Enums') verified; MM l.684 gives 505 379.005(36). Severity raised from MINOR: TORQ SRS l.25 ('derives supported spectroscopic observables') and TORQ-EXP-004 l.332-340 (/molecules carries 'isotope masses, geometry', /observables carries values) already own geometry-to-constants, so PCA-32 creates a second, divergent theoretical prior; stripping Z·m_e shifts B by ~0.027-0.054 % for C/N/O/H, the same size as the Method Matrix's 0.03-0.06 % semi-experimental accuracy target (MM l.307), and 'runtime' AME fetch contradicts l.19 'Zero external ingress'. That is a material contradiction, not a clarity issue; recommendation stands.

findings.claim: The automatic Sobol/PCE parameter freezing and the automatic 'feedback hook' trigger remove from the spectroscopist the determinability and model-selection decisions (A vs S reduction, which quartics to float, when a residual pattern means a perturbation) that are the expert content of a HITL tool, while the chapters claim to eliminate them.
findings.evidence: l.1214: "is automatically flagged as insensitive and is aggressively pruned (frozen at its ab initio or ground-state value) from the active optimization vector"; l.1222: "eliminating the manual trial-and-error parameter toggling historically required by spectroscopists"
findings.why_it_matters: A parameter that is insensitive at the current J-range is exactly the one the user will target next by assigning higher-J or higher-Ka lines; silently freezing it hides that opportunity and biases the fit if the frozen ab initio value is poor (quartics are only good to a factor of 2 per Method Matrix l.319). The product scope should be 'assist and expose', not 'automate and hide'.
findings.recommendation: Re-scope §7.4 as a determinability advisor: compute and display per-parameter sensitivity/correlation and recommend float/fix, but require explicit user confirmation; log every automatic decision in the fit history. Re-scope Ch10 triggers as advisory flags surfaced in the UI, not autonomous state transitions.
findings.verifier_note: l.1214 ('automatically flagged as insensitive and is aggressively pruned (frozen at its ab initio or ground-state value)') and l.1222 verified (draft duplicate at l.1140-1142); Ch10 l.1698 states the feedback 'operates completely autonomously' and l.1700 has SpycFit changing job_board state itself; Ch9 §9.3 (l.1492-1505) exposes only value sliders, no float/fix control, so determinability is nowhere user-decided. Severity raised from MINOR because Method_Matrix §20.3 (l.3510-3512) is binding: 'Any parameter whose reported value is influenced by a prior is flagged in the published table, exactly as fixed parameters conventionally are' and regularised/unregularised values 'never appear in the same column'; a silent freeze at an ab initio value (quartics good to a factor of 2, MM l.319) with no logging contradicts this governing rule. Recommendation should cite MM l.3388 (H2CO-HCl, A fixed at 42 GHz and disclosed) as the fix-and-disclose model.

findings.claim: SR-4.2.1 (kappa<0 -> I^r, kappa>0 -> III^l) is contradicted by the only implementation, which switches at kappa=0.5 with a +-0.05 hysteresis band and uses III^r, and the unit test codifies the code's rule, not the SRS's.
findings.evidence: SRS l.539: 'shall automatically enforce a Type I^r representation for kappa < 0 and a Type III^l representation for kappa > 0'. jax_builder.py:287-289: 'Default threshold is kappa = 0.5. If kappa > 0.5: Oblate character dominates -> switch to III^r'. Test l.110: 'based strictly on kappa threshold 0.5'.
findings.why_it_matters: Representation choice changes the K-ordering of eigenvalues and therefore the J_{Ka,Kc} labelling used to match observed transitions; a spec/code/test three-way disagreement means the trace matrix would show 'verified' for a requirement the code violates. For the Method Matrix system class (near-prolate vdW complexes) the SRS rule is also physically questionable: I^r is normally used for all kappa<~0.5-0.7, and a hysteresis on a fitted kappa is unusual but defensible.
findings.recommendation: SRS v2: state the representation rule once, with rationale (recommend: I^r for kappa <= 0 and near-prolate, III^r for kappa > ~0.5, user-overridable, and specify the eigenvalue->(Ka,Kc) labelling rule for each representation). Add test V-HAM-002 asserting labelled energies for a known oblate molecule (e.g. NH3-like or a planar oblate top) and a near-prolate one.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified: SRS l.539/635 'I^r for kappa<0 and III^l for kappa>0'; jax_builder l.290-292 and l.312-332 switch at 0.5 with DEFAULT_HYSTERESIS_DELTA=0.05 (l.46) to 'IIIr'; test l.110 'based strictly on kappa threshold 0.5'. Two corrections: (a) the SRS table at l.536/632 writes 'Type III^l (z=c, x=a, y=b)', which is the III^r mapping per the standard representation table (PGOPHER asymsym: III^r z=c, x=a, y=b), so the III^l-vs-III^r part of the disagreement is an SRS mislabel, and III^l/III^r are unitarily equivalent (sign of the Delta-K=2 element) with identical eigenvalues; (b) representation does not change eigenvalue ordering or energy-ordered (Ka,Kc) labels, only basis conditioning, Wang-parity bookkeeping and eigenvector-based labelling. The substantive spec/code/test conflict is the threshold (kappa>0 vs >0.5) plus undocumented hysteresis; SRS v2 should also correct the table label.

findings.claim: The 1193-line jax_builder never maps eigenvalues to (J,Ka,Kc) labels or to transition frequencies (0 occurrences of Ka/Kc/transition) and its Wang-block path discards eigenvectors; only the 548-line jax_driver contains the eigenvalue->J_{Ka,Kc} index rule, and only for I^r.
findings.evidence: jax_builder.py:985: 'evecs = None  # Full eigenvectors can be extracted from standard diagonalization if needed'; grep -c 'Ka|Kc|transition' jax_builder.py = 0. jax_driver.py:60-64: 'Ka = 0: index 0 ... Ka + Kc == J + 1: index 2*Ka - 1 ... Ka + Kc == J: index 2*Ka'.
findings.why_it_matters: SRS Ch7 (l.1112) says nu_calc 'is the difference between two eigenvalues'; the assignment step that picks WHICH two eigenvalues is the core of a fitting engine and is specified nowhere in the SRS. The large 'builder' module is scaffolding (bucketing, sharding, pmap, Hermitian locks) around a Hamiltonian it never uses for prediction.
findings.recommendation: SRS v2 requirement SPYC-HAM-00x: 'The engine SHALL label every eigenvalue of H^(J) with (Ka,Kc) via the standard energy-ordering rule for the chosen representation (and by eigenvector overlap/continuation when distortion reorders levels), and compute nu_calc for each assigned transition from labelled levels'. Make jax_driver's get_asymmetric_level_index the kept implementation (add III^r), and discard jax_builder's batching/sharding layers.
