findings.evidence: "To operate strictly in the microwave frequency domain (Hz/MHz/GHz), the equilibrium rotational constants are generated directly from the PCA-32 masses, correctly omitting the speed of light $c$: $$ A_e = \frac{h}{8 \pi^2 I_a} \dots $$"
findings.why_it_matters: B = h/(8π²I) gives Hz; B = h/(8π²cI) gives cm⁻¹ — both are correct in their units, and the draft was not wrong. Reproducibility at the 10⁻⁷ level requires pinning h/(8π²) = 505379.0 MHz·u·Å² (CODATA 2018; the Method Matrix quotes 505 379.005(36)) and the cm⁻¹↔MHz factor 29979.2458, and requiring MHz as the internal unit for V₃, α and χ as well (SR-4.4.2 covers only rotational tensors and α).
findings.recommendation: Replace the sentence with: 'Rotational constants are stored in MHz, B[MHz] = 505379.0 / I[u Å²] (CODATA 2018 h and u, values and source recorded in provenance); cm⁻¹ inputs are converted with 29979.2458 MHz/cm⁻¹.'
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.486-487 quote is verbatim; the draft at l.409 used A_e = h/(8π²cI_a), the correct cm⁻¹ form, so 'correctly omitting c' mislabels a unit choice as a correction. CODATA 2018 h and u give h/(8π²) = 505379.009 MHz·u·Å² (own computation), the Method Matrix quotes 505 379.005(36) at l.377 and uses 505379.0 at l.445/545, and grep finds no 505379 or 29979.2458 anywhere in the SRS. One detail in the finding is inaccurate: SR-4.4.2 (l.601) also normalises centrifugal-distortion constants to MHz, so the uncovered quantities are V₃ (l.927: 'in cm⁻¹ or MHz'), χ and μ, not CD constants; the recommendation is unchanged.

findings.claim: The two Chapter 1 versions disagree on the sign of the transition-frequency expression; the draft (E'' − E') is wrong and, with constants stored in MHz, the division by h is a units inconsistency.
findings.evidence: l.39: "\nu_{obs,i} - \left( \frac{E''(\mathbf{p}) - E'(\mathbf{p})}{h} \right)"; l.108: "\nu_{obs,i} - \left( \frac{E'(\mathbf{p}) - E''(\mathbf{p})}{h} \right)"
findings.why_it_matters: ν = (E' − E'')/h with ' = upper, '' = lower. Leaving the draft in the document gives an implementing agent a 50 % chance of reversing every residual; since SR-4.4.2 stores all energies in MHz, ν_calc = E' − E'' directly.
findings.recommendation: Delete the draft chapter; keep l.108 and drop '/h' (or state energies in MHz explicitly).
findings.verifier_note: l.39 reads E''(p) − E'(p) and l.108 reads E'(p) − E''(p), both verbatim; with the standard ' = upper, '' = lower convention only l.108 gives positive ν, so the draft is the wrong one. The sign discrepancy itself is already in the brief's established facts, but the finding adds the determination of which version is correct and the units point (SR-4.4.2 l.601 stores HamiltonianState in MHz, making '/h' inconsistent with the stated internal units). MINOR is appropriate: it is a residual-sign ambiguity an implementer could resolve, not a design error.

findings.claim: The slider ranges/steps are inappropriate for the domain: quartic constants of van der Waals complexes span 10 kHz–MHz, and 1 Hz steps are below determinability; A/B/C ±100 MHz is smaller than the de novo search windows; S-reduction labels here conflict with the A-reduction default of Ch1/Ch4.
findings.evidence: "| **Centrifugal Distortion (Quartic)** | $D_J, D_{JK}, D_K, d_1, d_2$ | Ultra-fine precision ($\pm 10$ kHz range, $1$ Hz steps). |" "| **Rotational Constants** | $A, B, C$ | ... typically $\pm 100$ MHz range, $0.001$ MHz steps"
findings.why_it_matters: Floppy complexes have D_J ≈ 10–100 kHz and D_JK up to ~1 MHz (Method Matrix §3.1 asks only for a factor-2 prediction); a ±10 kHz slider cannot reach them. Product-A windows are ±0.5–2 % (±60–240 MHz at 12 GHz, Method Matrix decision card). Ch1 (l.100) and Ch4 default to the A-reduction (Δ, δ) while Ch9 exposes S-reduction (D, d) sliders.
findings.recommendation: Make ranges data-driven: ±5σ of the current fit or ±(Method Matrix class window) for A, B, C; log-scaled sliders over 1 Hz–10 MHz for quartics with step = 0.1σ; label sliders by the reduction actually selected.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at l.1589-1590 are verbatim. The Method Matrix's own Ar–ketene anchor (l.3386) has δ_K = −152.24(23) kHz and δ_J = 16.09 kHz, so a ±10 kHz quartic slider cannot reach a textbook vdW-complex value, and 1 Hz steps are below the 230 Hz uncertainty quoted there; the decision card (MM l.78) gives Product-A windows of ±120–240 MHz at 12 GHz for 1–2 % floppy predictions, exceeding the 'typically ±100 MHz' range. Ch1 l.29/98 and Ch4 l.547 make A-reduction (Δ_J, δ_J) the default while Ch9 l.1577 and l.1590 expose only S-reduction names (D_J, D_JK, D_K, d_1, d_2), so the label mismatch is real.

findings.claim: Tunnelling is misattributed to barriers 'comparable to or smaller than kT', and the 'm_max ≥ 21 for 10⁻⁶ MHz convergence at 400 cm⁻¹' number is unverifiable and likely a garbled recollection of BELGI's 21-function torsional basis.
findings.evidence: "potential energy barriers that are comparable to or smaller than the thermal energy ($kT$), resulting in quantum tunneling" (l.828); "A standard threshold requires $m_{max} \ge 21$ to achieve convergence to $10^{-6} \text{ MHz}$ for barriers around $400 \text{ cm}^{-1}$" (l.907)
findings.why_it_matters: At T_rot = 1–2 K, kT ≈ 0.7–1.4 cm⁻¹ while V₃ is 10–1500 cm⁻¹; A/E splitting is zero-temperature tunnelling through the barrier, not thermal activation. The convergence statement depends on s = 4V₃/(9F) and the target quantity, not on a fixed m_max; BELGI uses 21 free-rotor functions (k = −10…10) in its first step (Hougen, Kleiner & Godfrey 1994; Kleiner 2010) — I would check those papers before citing any number. A fabricated constant in a spec becomes an untested magic number in code.
findings.recommendation: Reword 5.1 physically ('splittings arise from tunnelling between the three equivalent minima and persist at 0 K'). Replace the fixed m_max by a convergence requirement: 'increase |m|_max until all fitted transition frequencies change by < 0.1 kHz; record the final basis size.'
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at l.828 and l.907 are verbatim. kT at T_rot = 1–2 K is 0.70–1.39 cm⁻¹ (computed) against Method Matrix V₃ anchors of 11.2, 49.4, 197.7, 439 and 565 cm⁻¹ (MM l.729), and MM l.3662 treats tunnelling splittings as zero-temperature observables, so 'barriers comparable to or smaller than kT' is physically wrong. The literature confirms '21' is the conventional first-step torsional basis count in BELGI/RAM36 (21 functions kept at the first diagonalisation step, arXiv:1908.07790; '21 × 21 free-rotor matrix is sufficient to obtain experimental accuracy', arXiv:1109.5076), not an 'm_max ≥ 21' (= 43 functions) threshold tied to 10⁻⁶ MHz at 400 cm⁻¹; the SRS sentence also contradicts its own preceding claim that m_max is set dynamically from V₃/F.

findings.claim: Argon is named as a ghost-peak species to be subtracted via a .cat file, but a rare-gas atom has no rotational spectrum.
findings.evidence: "If the ghost peaks belong to a known chemical species (e.g., residual Argon or a known solvent), the UI allows the user to import an existing CoChem `.cat` or `.par` file representing the impurity."
findings.why_it_matters: Ar is the carrier gas and is spectroscopically silent in the microwave; writing this in a spec signals the authors did not model the experiment. Real contaminants in a CP-FTMW jet are monomer, water, precursor fragments and known complexes — all of which are catalogued species whose .cat predictions can indeed be subtracted or masked.
findings.recommendation: Replace the example with 'monomer, water/HDO, precursor fragments, or previously assigned complexes (from .cat predictions at T_rot)' and note that subtraction must use the same T_rot and lineshape as the target simulation.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.1609 (and draft l.1524) reads verbatim 'residual Argon or a known solvent' as a ghost-peak species to import as a `.cat`/`.par`; argon is a closed-shell ¹S₀ atom with no dipole and no rotational levels, so no Pickett catalogue can represent it. The Method Matrix mentions Ar only as the partner in complexes (Ar–ketene l.3386, Ar–oxazole l.660), confirming that the carrier gas contributes to a jet spectrum only through its complexes. The surrounding §9.4 framing (l.1594: 'reaction mixtures or broadband discharge experiments… pump oil… local oscillator harmonics') is mm-wave absorption-cell language, supporting the recommendation to re-anchor the example on monomer/water/precursor/previously assigned complexes at the same T_rot.

findings.claim: The two Voigt definitions use different Doppler parameterisations (σ vs γ_D) without defining γ_D; if γ_D is read as the Doppler HWHM the profile width is wrong by √ln2.
findings.evidence:
l.280: " rac{	ext{Re}[w(z)]}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi}} ... z =  rac{(
u - 
u_0) + i\gamma}{\sigma \sqrt{2}}"; l.1389: " rac{\operatorname{Re}[w(z)]}{\gamma_D \sqrt{\pi}} \quad z =  rac{(
u - 
u_0) + i \gamma_L}{\gamma_D}"
findings.why_it_matters: Both are correct only if σ is the Gaussian standard deviation and γ_D = σ√2 is the 1/e half-width; the HITRAN convention γ_D (HWHM) = σ√(2 ln 2) differs by 0.83. A code taking γ_D from a HWHM slider (l.1589 'Δν_D') produces wrong widths and peak heights.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one definition (σ, γ with FWHM conversions stated) in a 'Lineshape conventions' subsection and reference it from Ch2, Ch8 and Ch9.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes verified at SRS l.280-282 and l.1389; grep shows γ_D is used eight times in Ch8 (l.1283-1431) but never defined (no Doppler-width formula anywhere), Δν_D at l.1589 carries no HWHM/FWHM qualifier, and Ch2 (l.278) parameterises as V(ν;σ,γ). The two forms coincide only if γ_D = σ√2 (Gaussian 1/e half-width); reading γ_D as a HITRAN-style HWHM = σ√(2 ln 2) narrows the Gaussian by √ln2 = 0.83 and raises the peak by 1.2, exactly as claimed. Recommendation is sound for CP-FTMW (and should add that the jet Doppler/instrumental width is a fitted or instrument parameter, not the T=296 K γ_D(T) that Ch8 l.1385 implies).

findings.claim: 'Lorentzian broadening regularization' of eigenvalue derivatives at degeneracies is not a physical or standard numerical device; eigenvalue derivatives are well defined at degeneracies, only eigenvector derivatives carry (E_m − E_n)⁻¹.
findings.evidence: "the custom VJP applies a Lorentzian broadening regularization scheme or delegates the degenerate subspace derivative to a subspace-projected perturbation metric"
findings.why_it_matters: ν_calc depends on eigenvalues only; ∂E_n/∂θ = ⟨ψ_n|∂H/∂θ|ψ_n⟩ (degenerate perturbation theory within the subspace if needed) contains no divisions. The NaN risk in jax.numpy.linalg.eigh's generic JVP comes from the eigenvector branch (0·∞); the correct fix is an eigenvalue-only custom JVP/VJP, not an ad hoc smoothing that biases the Jacobian. Exact K-degeneracies occur only in the symmetric-top limit; asymmetry and distortion lift them.
findings.recommendation: Specify: 'Derivatives of transition frequencies SHALL use an eigenvalue-only custom JVP (Hellmann–Feynman, with subspace diagonalisation of ∂H/∂θ when |E_m − E_n| < ε_deg); no regularisation of the Jacobian is permitted.' Add a finite-difference cross-check test at 10⁻⁸ relative.
findings.verifier_note: Core claim confirmed empirically (jax 0.11.2, x64, reviewer test script not committed): at an exact 2-fold degeneracy jacrev of eigvalsh, of eigh(H)[0] and of E2−E0 returns finite values, an eigenvector-dependent output returns nan, and a 1e-14 split gives finite gradients even through eigenvectors — so the SRS's 'NaN when E_m ≈ E_n' (l.1196) is wrong and no regularisation is needed for a frequency-only Jacobian. The sub-claim that Lorentzian broadening is 'not a physical or standard numerical device' must be withdrawn: a 'Lorentzian-broadened custom VJP' is literally what the PyPI `eigh` JAX package (https://pypi.org/project/eigh/) and tad-mctc's `lorn` option (https://tad-mctc.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modules/storch/linalg.html) implement, the latter documenting that it 'will induce small errors in the returned gradients' — which strengthens the recommendation to forbid it for ν_calc. Keep the recommendation and make the subspace clause mandatory: at an exact crossing autodiff returns diag(P ∂H P) in whatever basis eigh happened to return (my test gave 0 where the one-sided derivatives are ±1), so diagonalising ∂H/∂θ in the degenerate subspace is required, not optional; severity stays MINOR because the biased branch only affects eigenvector-dependent outputs (intensities), not the position fit.

findings.anchor: SRS l.409 vs 486-487; TORQ SRS l.54 (TORQ-SCI-002), l.64
findings.claim: The rotational-constant formula appears with and without c, neither carries units, and the text declares one form 'correct' while retaining the other.
findings.evidence: l.409 'A_e = h/(8 pi^2 c I_a)'; l.487 'correctly omitting the speed of light c: A_e = h/(8 pi^2 I_a)'.
findings.why_it_matters: Both are valid in different units (cm^-1 vs Hz); the defect is the missing unit declaration and the retained contradiction. TORQ-SCI-002 fixes MHz and a single constants service; the Method Matrix fixes B[MHz] = 505379.0/I[amu A^2].
findings.recommendation: One equation with explicit units (MHz) and the conversion constant from the shared constants service; cite it once in the conventions section.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.409 reads A_e = h/(8 pi^2 c I_a) and l.486-487 reads 'correctly omitting the speed of light c: A_e = h/(8 pi^2 I_a)'; the final text names a domain '(Hz/MHz/GHz)' but neither fixes one unit nor gives the unit of I_a, and the bare formula yields Hz only with I in kg m^2. TORQ-SCI-002 (TORQ SRS l.54: 'Spectroscopic output uses MHz for rotational/coupling constants ... conversions from one versioned constants service') and TORQ l.64 (B^Hz = h/(8 pi^2 I)) are as cited; Method_Matrix.md l.545 gives B[MHz] = 505379.0/I[amu A^2] while l.373 gives 505379.1, which itself argues for the single constants-service recommendation.

findings.claim: The Voigt profile is defined with two different parameterisations and an undefined width symbol, and a real-valued function (erfcx) is named for a complex Faddeeva evaluation.
findings.evidence: l.195 'V = Re[w(z)]/(sigma sqrt(2 pi)) ... z = ((nu - nu_0) + i gamma)/(sigma sqrt 2)'; l.1291 'V = Re[w(z)]/(gamma_D sqrt(pi)) ... z = ((nu - nu_0) + i gamma_L)/gamma_D'; l.1345 '`jax.scipy.special.erfcx` (or equivalent optimized Faddeeva approximations)'.
findings.why_it_matters: gamma_D (HWHM? 1/e half-width? sigma?) is never defined; 'or equivalent' makes the requirement unverifiable. For a jet experiment at T_rot 1-2 K the relevant line shape is Doppler/instrumental, which the SRS never states.
findings.recommendation: Symbol table with one Voigt definition and explicit width conventions; replace the primitive mandate with a numerical accuracy requirement (e.g., Voigt evaluation relative error <= 1e-6 against a reference implementation on a named grid).
findings.verifier_note: Core stands: l.195-197 use V = Re[w(z)]/(sigma sqrt(2 pi)), z = (dnu + i gamma)/(sigma sqrt 2) while l.1291/1389 use Re[w(z)]/(gamma_D sqrt pi), z = (dnu + i gamma_L)/gamma_D, and gamma_D (introduced l.1283/1381) is never given a width convention (0 hits for HWHM/FWHM/half-width in the SRS). Two corrections: (1) strike 'the SRS never states' Doppler/instrumental, since Ch9 l.1472/1557 says 'Phi(nu - nu_ij) represents the instrumental and Doppler line profile' (the valid point is that Ch2/Ch8 define the Voigt in IR/NMR/HITRAN-296K pressure-broadening terms with no jet/CP-FTMW statement); (2) reword the erfcx sub-claim: current JAX docs define erfcx(x) for 'real or complex' input and w(z) = erfcx(-iz) (https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/_autosummary/jax.scipy.special.erfcx.html), so it is not inherently real-only, but `erfcx`/`wofz` exist only on JAX `main` and are absent from jax/_src/scipy/special.py at every release tag from the pinned jax-v0.4.13 through jax-v0.10.0, so the mandated primitive does not exist in any installable JAX; the accuracy-vs-reference (scipy.special.wofz) recommendation stands and the anchor should add l.1472/1557.

findings.anchor: SRS l.66/135, 1343/1441; repo trees cochem_spycfit/ and src/cochem_spycfit/
findings.claim: Repository and package names in the SRS do not match each other or the code, and the module path implies a shared `cochem` namespace that the polyrepo requirement forbids.
findings.evidence: l.66 'isolated Git repository (`cochem-spycfit-core`)'; l.1343 '**Module:** `cochem.spycfit.convolution`'; actual package: `cochem_spycfit` in two divergent trees (26,019 vs 42,129 LOC).
findings.why_it_matters: A fix agent needs the canonical package path and a single source tree; the SRS gives neither and contradicts 1.5 'Polyrepo architecture prevents lateral dependency bleed'.
findings.recommendation: State the canonical repo (CoChem-SpycFit), package (`cochem_spycfit`), and add SPYC-OPS-001: exactly one package tree; foreign-module copies (src/cochem, src/cochem_base, src/cochem_topos, core/) SHALL be removed and consumed as versioned dependencies.
findings.verifier_note: SRS l.66/135 names `cochem-spycfit-core` and l.1343/1441 names module `cochem.spycfit.convolution`; the dotted path `cochem.spycfit` has 0 hits in any .py file, the convolver actually lives at cochem_spycfit/physics_core/cochem_convolver.py and src/cochem_spycfit/convolver.py, pyproject.toml name is 'CoChem-SpycFit', the git remote is ProfJJK-CoChem/CoChem-SpycFit, and the two trees reproduce at exactly 26,019 vs 42,129 LOC with two egg-info dirs. Minor nuance for the write-up: a PEP 420 `cochem` namespace package is not per se incompatible with a polyrepo, but in this repo `src/cochem/` is a copied foreign tree (qc/, topos/, torq/...), so the lateral-bleed contradiction with l.66 holds in practice.

findings.claim: Stray or inconsistent technical statements: L-BFGS appears once and nowhere else; the Ch2 vmap convolution is the approach Ch8 forbids; a cited method has no reference; the UI exposes only S-reduction constants while Ch1 writes the A-reduced Hamiltonian.
findings.evidence: l.187 'Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) and Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (L-BFGS) minimizers'; l.199 'vectors these computations via JAX's `vmap`' vs l.1299 'a naive JAX `vmap` approach will attempt to allocate terabytes'; l.1503 '`D_J, D_JK, D_K, d_1, d_2`' vs l.35 Delta_J ... delta_K.
findings.why_it_matters: Each is a small inconsistency, but together they show no consistency pass was ever made; a fix agent would implement whichever chapter it read last.
findings.recommendation: Consistency pass with a single symbol/algorithm table; UI parameter set derived from the chosen reduction; full bibliography for every named method (Transtrum, Watson 1977, Kraitchman 1953, etc.).
findings.verifier_note: grep confirms 'L-BFGS' occurs only at l.187/272 and Ch7 (l.1172-1179) uses LM exclusively; l.199/284 'vectors these computations via JAX's vmap ... massive SIMD payloads' is exactly the O(N x M) full vectorisation l.1299/1397 calls 'a naive JAX vmap approach [that] will attempt to allocate terabytes'; 'Transtrum's geodesic acceleration metrics' at l.1179 has no reference in the body (a bare '(Transtrum et al., 2012)' appears only in the Ch7 Improvements checklist l.1236, and the repo's references.bib holds three unrelated entries: Valeev 2004, MACE 2022, MPQC4 2020). The UI table at l.1503/1588 lists only S-reduced D_J, D_JK, D_K, d_1, d_2 while Ch1 l.35/104 writes the A-reduced Delta_J...delta_K operator and Ch4 l.565-570 plus SR-4.3.2 define both sets with kappa-based branching, so the UI set is inconsistent with both chapters.

findings.claim: Feedback-trigger thresholds are undefined or internally incoherent (1-3% expected deviation but a 5% trigger) and not tied to the Method Matrix accuracy ladder.
findings.evidence: l.1648 'beyond the expected vibrational-rotation interaction bounds (Delta approx 1-3%)'; l.1650 '|...| > 0.05'; l.1643 'chi^2_r > tau_critical after k Levenberg-Marquardt iterations without converging to a predefined tolerance'.
findings.why_it_matters: Method Matrix 3.1 gives the actual expectations (Delta B_vib 0.1-0.7% of B_e; floppy B0 1-2% [D]; topology discrimination 1-3%), so a 5% gate would pass a wrong-topology candidate. Undefined tau_critical and k make the requirement unverifiable.
findings.recommendation: Parameterise triggers as configuration with defaults and Method Matrix provenance (e.g., Delta B > 3% for semi-rigid, > 5% floppy, both [D]); define tau_critical, k and tolerance in the config schema.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes are verbatim at l.1643/1723 and l.1648-1650/1728-1730; tau_critical and k occur only there with no definition, and Method_Matrix.md Sec. 3.1 does give Delta B_vib 0.1-0.7% of B_e, floppy B0 1-2% [D] and topology discrimination 1-3%. The why-it-matters is wrong on topology, however: the same table says distinct topologies 'differ by >=0.2 A in R_cm, i.e. >=11 % in B', so a 5% gate would catch a wrong topology; what it fails to catch is a wrong conformer (conformer-to-conformer Delta(A,B,C) = 0.1%) or orientational isomer ('not achievable from A, B, C alone'), and the SRS compares effective experimental constants to TORQ *equilibrium* A_e,B_e,C_e, the B_e-vs-B0 confusion the Method Matrix calls 'the commonest way this document can be misused'. Revised recommendation: configurable thresholds with Method Matrix provenance, comparison against B0 = B_e + Delta B_vib (or an explicit semi-rigid 0.3-0.5% / floppy 1-2% band on B_e), and tau_critical, k and the convergence tolerance defined in the config schema.

findings.anchor: .docs/task1_subsystems_architectural_specification.md l.10, 116, 770; Method_Matrix.md l.9; SRS grep for 29148/830 = 0
findings.claim: The SRS makes no standards claim at all; the governing-standards claim lives only in the copied CoChem-BASE arch spec, which cites a withdrawn standard alongside 29148 and mislabels the Method Matrix version.
findings.evidence: arch spec l.10 'Governing Standards: ... IEEE 830-1998 / ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018, CoChem Method Matrix v4.1'; Method Matrix l.9 '**Version 4 - 9 August 2026.** Supersedes v3'. README l.6: 'CoChem User Manual v4.1' (the v4.1 is the manual/ecosystem version).
findings.why_it_matters: A standards claim that is not in the SRS cannot be audited against it; IEEE 830-1998 is superseded by 29148; a wrong Method Matrix version number breaks the one citation the science depends on.
findings.recommendation: SRS v2 document-control block: 'Conforms to ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 clause 9.6 (SRS) and 5.2 (requirement characteristics). Governing science: Method Matrix v4 (2026-08-09). Ecosystem: CoChem User Manual v4.1.' Drop IEEE 830.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: arch spec l.10/116/770 cite 'IEEE 830-1998 / ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018' and 'Method Matrix v4.1', Method_Matrix.md l.9 reads 'Version 4 — 9 August 2026', the SRS has zero hits for 29148/830, and IEEE's own page lists 830-1998 as superseded by 29148:2011, itself superseded by 29148:2018 (https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/830/1222). Revision: 'v4.1' is not a one-off mislabel but an ecosystem-wide name collision — CoChem_User_Manual.md l.1 titles itself 'CoChem v4.1 Official User Manual & Method Matrix', ~40 CoChem-BASE .docs files say 'Method Matrix v4.1' and CoChem-TORQ_True_SRS_Iterated.md says 'v4.2' — so the recommendation should pin the governing science by filename+date ('CoChem-BASE/Method_Matrix.md, Version 4, 2026-08-09') and explicitly disambiguate it from the User Manual's embedded matrix. The 29148:2018 subclause numbers (9.6, 5.2) could not be confirmed from any online source; cite the standard and verify subclauses against the purchased text before writing them into the SRS.

findings.claim: Linear molecules and symmetric/spherical tops are implied as inputs but no requirement defines their treatment; kappa is undefined at the spherical limit.
findings.evidence: l.417 'rejecting an asymmetric top Hamiltonian request for a linear molecule dataset'; l.580 'all 3N-6 (or 3N-5) normal modes'; TORQ-EXP-002: kappa 'is undefined at the spherical-top limit'.
findings.why_it_matters: The fix agent needs to know whether linear rotors (e.g., Ar-HCN-type complexes in the system class) are in scope or must be refused with a stable error.
findings.recommendation: Rotor-class scope statement: asymmetric tops SHALL be supported; symmetric and linear tops SHALL be supported or explicitly refused with an error code; spherical tops refused.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes at l.417/495 ('rejecting an asymmetric top Hamiltonian request for a linear molecule dataset'), l.580/676 ('3N-6 (or 3N-5)') and TORQ SRS l.326 ('undefined at the spherical-top limit') are verbatim, and the Method Matrix confirms linear/near-linear complexes are in-domain (l.308 'T-shaped or near-linear complex', l.2223 Ar···HCN worked example, l.2293 'linear fragments, a common vdW motif (OC···HF, HCN dimers)', l.2322/3233 'skip for linear complexes — unsupported'). Narrow the claim: symmetric tops DO get a thin treatment (κ=±1 rows l.533/537/629/633 'Exact K degeneracy'; SR-4.3.2 l.570/666 'forces A-reduction on a symmetric top ... DegenerateSingularityWarning'), so the genuinely undefined cases are linear rotors (A→∞, κ formally −1, 3N-5 modes, no .lin quantum-number convention) and spherical tops (κ = 0/0), plus the missing rotor-class scope statement; add l.533/537/570 to the anchor.

findings.claim: The SRS claims a CI pipeline that 'rigorously tests the non-linear optimizer against known spectral benchmarks', but pytest.ini runs 11 of 1,096 tests and CI runs none; traceability has no enforcement point.
findings.evidence: pytest.ini: 'testpaths = tests/test_provenance_fair_security_suite.py'. SRS l.68: 'sterile CI/CD pipeline that rigorously tests the non-linear optimizer against known spectral benchmarks (e.g., the established millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide)'; grep -i propylene src tests = 0.
findings.why_it_matters: Without a CI gate that runs the full suite and the trace-matrix check, SRS v2's traceability requirement (TRACE-01) is unenforceable and the next agent can repeat the testpaths trick.
findings.recommendation: SRS v2 SPYC-NFR-00x: CI SHALL run the complete tests/ tree, the requirement-trace check and the Pickett round-trip (or mark UNVERIFIED); restricting testpaths or adding amnesty files is prohibited; benchmark datasets live in tests/data with source citations.
findings.verifier_note: Verified: pytest.ini 'testpaths = tests/test_provenance_fair_security_suite.py' (11 'def test_') vs 1,096 'def test_' across 60 tests/test_*.py files; .github/workflows/cochem_spycfit_ci.yml has a single job that only runs a find for *.h5/*.parquet/*.fit/*.lin/*.lock and no pytest or lint step; SRS l.68 and l.137 both state 'sterile CI/CD pipeline that rigorously tests the non-linear optimizer against known spectral benchmarks (e.g., the established millimeter-wave spectrum of Propylene Oxide)'; grep -ri propylene src tests = 0 and no tests/data directory exists (tests/fixtures holds only orca.out, orca_freq.out, gxtb.out, nbo.out). Only Ch6's Kabsch/SVD concept has an implementation (intake/cochem_spycfit_orchestrator.py:864-916 compute_eckart_rotation_matrix), under a different name; the §6.3 axis-permutation overlap matrix (l.1014-1029) has no implementation (only a planar 'PermutationError' guard in cochem_inertial_defect.py:145).

findings.anchor: SRS l.18, l.55, l.60; src/cochem_spycfit/core_engine/cochem_fit_registry_manager.py:1-8; core_engine/cochem_spycfit_state.py:1-3; cochem_spycfit_ml_storage.py:1-6
findings.claim: Ch1 models TORQ as a message broker pushing into a stateless SpycFit, but ~3 kLOC of the code is a persistence stack (SWMR HDF5 registry, Zarr, FileLock, immutable FitState DAG with time-travel) that an agent cannot classify as compliant or non-compliant because the SRS's ecosystem model is wrong (TORQ is the QC engine; BASE orchestrates; TOPOS generates conformers).
findings.evidence: SRS l.60: 'It holds zero persistent state regarding the origin of the data.' vs cochem_fit_registry_manager.py:3-5: 'Authoritative state persistence, atomic locking, cryptographic dataset hashing, FAIR compliance, SWMR HDF5 tensors, and Zarr tensor persistence'; cochem_spycfit_state.py:2: 'Immutable FitState model and DAG CommitManager for spectroscopic assignments.'
findings.why_it_matters: Assignment sessions are inherently stateful (Ch9 l.1455 says so); the trace matrix needs a correct context diagram (BASE -> TOPOS -> TORQ -> SpycFit -> BASE/SCRIBE) to decide which persistence is required (session/provenance) and which is scope creep (registry, zarr, locks).
findings.recommendation: SRS v2 Ch1: replace the tripartite/air-gap text with the real ecosystem context (per CoChem User Manual Ch5 and TORQ SRS §12), define SpycFit's state model explicitly (project file = assignments + .par/.lin + provenance; no daemon, no job board), and give it an ID so the persistence modules can be kept or discarded against it.
findings.verifier_note: Quotes are verbatim: SRS l.18 ('Task Orchestration & Routing Queue ... message broker'), l.55 ('TORQ acts as a unidirectional data diode ... TORQ pushes'), l.60 ('It holds zero persistent state regarding the origin of the data.'), cochem_fit_registry_manager.py:4-5 and cochem_spycfit_state.py:2 exact, cochem_spycfit_ml_storage.py:1-8 (DAGCommitManager, time-travel reversion). The SRS contains 0 occurrences of Zarr/SWMR/FileLock/registry/FAIR/time-travel while §1.4 (l.60/129) says stateless, Ch9 l.1455 says 'The Voila kernel maintains the persistent state', and Ch10 l.1700-1701 has a 'SpycFit daemon' writing the SQLite job_board, so the 3,146 LOC (registry 1,500 + os_adapter 912 + hdf5_cache 353 + state 381; 3,801 with ml_storage 655) genuinely cannot be classified; os_adapter.py:4 even cites 'SRS Task 10 (Section 3.2 Immutable File Lock)', a section that does not exist in this SRS. The sibling-doc references hold (User Manual Ch5 l.742; TORQ SRS §12 l.320, V-CONSUMER l.469, WP10 BASE/SpycFit l.503); the ecosystem-model error and the Ch1/Ch9 contradiction are already established facts in the brief, so MINOR is the right weight for the incremental content (the state-model requirement with an ID).

findings.claim: The LM normal equations are internally consistent (with r = ν_exp − ν_calc and J = ∂ν_calc/∂θ the right-hand side +JᵀWr is correct, and λ·diag(JᵀWJ) is Marquardt's scaling), but the text conflates Transtrum's 'delayed gratification' λ schedule with geodesic acceleration, which is a separate second-order step correction.
findings.evidence: l.1179: "The damping factor λ is dynamically adjusted per iteration using a delayed gratification strategy (e.g., utilizing Transtrum's geodesic acceleration metrics): it is decreased if the step significantly reduces χ², and increased if χ² increases."
findings.why_it_matters: An agent may try to implement 'geodesic acceleration metrics' as a λ rule, which does not exist; geodesic acceleration needs directional second derivatives of the model and is optional.
findings.recommendation: State the sign convention explicitly next to l.1102; write the λ rule as 'λ ← λ·ν_up on rejected step, λ ← λ/ν_down on accepted step (e.g. ν_up = 2, ν_down = 3, Transtrum & Sethna 2012)'; mention geodesic acceleration, if at all, as an optional separate feature.
findings.verifier_note: Quote at l.1179 is exact (the draft copy at l.1104 states the same λ rule without the geodesic clause, and l.1236 lists 'Geodesic Acceleration for the LM Engine' as a separate Improver). Transtrum & Sethna arXiv:1201.5885 §2.1 defines delayed gratification purely as asymmetric λ factors (raise ×2 on rejected step, lower ×3 on accepted, vs Marquardt's ×10/÷10), and §3 defines geodesic acceleration as a separate second-order step term δθ₂ requiring the directional second derivative r''=K δθ₁δθ₁ — so the recommendation's factors are right and the conflation is real. Sign check: with r = ν_exp − ν_calc (l.1090) and J = ∂ν_calc/∂θ (l.1110), −½∇χ² = JᵀWr, so the RHS at l.1102 is correct but l.1095 never states the sign of r.

findings.claim: Ch2 names 'Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) and Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (L-BFGS) minimizers' while every other chapter specifies only LM; L-BFGS appears nowhere else and is unsuited to a least-squares problem with an available Jacobian.
findings.evidence: l.187: "the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) and Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (L-BFGS) minimizers operating within the Spectral Registry compute accurate Jacobians (J) and Hessians (H ≈ JᵀJ)"
findings.why_it_matters: An implementing agent may add a second optimiser path (and its tests) that the rest of the SRS never asks for.
findings.recommendation: Delete the L-BFGS reference; the SRS specifies one optimiser (LM with the normal equations of §7.2).
findings.verifier_note: Quote l.187 (=l.272) exact, and grep shows 'BFGS' occurs nowhere else in the SRS; Ch7 §7.2 (l.1098/1102) specifies only LM. The text also conflates BFGS with its limited-memory variant ('Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno (L-BFGS)'). The drift the finding warns about is already visible in the repo — src/cochem_spycfit/cochem_spycfit_ml_engine.py:253 passes optimizer="fmin_l_bfgs_b" — though for an ML hyperparameter path rather than the spectral fitter, so NIT is the right severity.

findings.claim: FP64 is justified with NMR/FT-ICR numbers instead of the rotational-fitting argument; the conclusion (FP64 required) is right.
findings.evidence: "In high-field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) or ... FT-ICR MS, distinguishing subtle J-couplings ... requires resolving frequency differences on the order of $\Delta \nu \approx 10^{-3} \text{ Hz}$ against carrier frequencies of $10^8 \text{ Hz}$"
findings.why_it_matters: The real argument: eigenvalues of H_rot reach ~A·J² ≈ 4×10⁶ MHz (A = 10 GHz, J = 20) while residuals must be resolved to ~1 kHz, i.e. 2.5×10⁻¹⁰ relative — three orders beyond FP32 (1.2×10⁻⁷) and comfortably within FP64 (2.2×10⁻¹⁶). Stating the correct magnitude also sets the Jacobian finite-difference cross-check tolerance.
findings.recommendation: Replace the NMR/MS sentences with the rotational estimate above; keep the FP64 mandate.
findings.verifier_note: Quote verified at SRS l.264 and the proposed arithmetic checks (A·J² = 10⁴ MHz × 400 = 4×10⁶ MHz; 1 kHz / 4×10¹² Hz = 2.5×10⁻¹⁰; FP32 ε = 2⁻²³ = 1.19×10⁻⁷; FP64 2.2×10⁻¹⁶). For the Method Matrix class (T_rot 1–2 K, populated J ≲ 10, but A up to ~10.4 GHz, e.g. Ar–ketene at Method Matrix l.3386) the in-domain ratio is ~10⁻⁹, still ~2 orders beyond FP32, so the FP64 conclusion holds. Partly overlaps the established fact that Ch2 is NMR/FT-ICR-based; the added value is the replacement estimate, so NIT is the right severity (l.266's 'numerical differentiation of lineshape gradients' also contradicts Ch7's analytic autodiff, worth folding into the rewrite).
